This is a pretty solid alternative to Cloud Print for devices on the same subnet while bridging to CP for off-network access. It offers a variety of detection/connections options including a wizard that instantly found all the printers on my home network - although some were inaccurately identified as "WiFi" devices when they are actually network printers hardwired to the router. Device configuration options are far superior to Cloud Print and are similar to what you might find in the 'properties' dialog on Windows (eg: paper type, size and duplex settings). Supports most Android apps either via dedicated print (eg: Gmail) or sharing links (look for Hammermill in list of destinations) within the app. Supports preview - woohoo! Does not interfere with the operation of my device, doesn't constantly run in the background and only displays a single non-intrusive ad after print job has been submitted. Works on Kindle HDX along with several relatively standard Android devices. Downside: configuration options can be confusing (-1 star) so plan to spend a few minutes learning the app after novelty of actually being able to print to the device of your choice wears off. This appears to be a sponsored version of "Print Hand" which is a paid app that offers no appreciable benefits IMO.

Headings: Works great for me printing email
Base_Reviews: Works great for me printing email, .pdf files, calendar items, contacts list, word processor documents, etc.. I have a Samsung Galaxy Tab 4, printing on a Canon Pixma MG6320. Some useful points:When I first installed it (leaving the default settings) it found the printer, but nothing happened when I tried to print the test page. But I remembered an earlier reviewer had said to change the app Protocol setting to "IPP" so I did that, and the app has been printing fine since.Here is how to access its print function from within other apps. If clicking on Print within another app does not do it for you, click on Share instead and Hammermill should be listed as an option; clicking on that takes you directly to Preview and Print.If that doesn't work either, click directly on the Hammermill app from your Home screen. Look to see if the app/file type you want to print from is listed down the left (that is how I print from the Calendar and Contacts apps that came with my tablet). If the app/file type is not listed, click on the Files option in the list and look for the file name that you want to print; click on that file and  the Preview and Print screen should appear.Once you are on the Preview screen, you can choose the printer, paper size, and a few other options, but it's not until after you hit Print that you will be asked for the number of copies and page range to print.This a fantastic app, very useful, and the only ads you have to look at are for Hammermill paper.

Skype ignored repeated request using email (no phone for a telephony provider?)Just today, pursuing use for my Kindle Fire, I found that my initial deposit was forfeit for inactivity. I used chat to request reinstatement. The representative seemed unable to extract information despite a "Dick & Jane" narrative, asking off-base questions and even, well into the conversation, requesting my screen name -- provided on the transcript. It became apparent that, if not illiterate, the representative was trained to deflect callers and outlast any caller's attempt at redress.

So far, I'm really enjoying the way this app submerses you into the language and forces you to remember how the verb in particular ends rather than list is like language classes do. The app helped me learn the languages faster than it did with an actual teacher. The learning is personal and if you fail out of the lesson, you have to start that lesson over and I like this since the questions aren't in the same order, so it's not totally just memorize the right answer to pass. You're still learning and it's great!My only complaint is, I took three years of French and started using the French portion to get better at my listening skills, since that's where I do poorly, and sometimes the translations are wrong, or vastly differ from what I learned. For example the app teaches you instantly that jolie and joli mean lovely or nice, which in fact the word means 'pretty'. I know it's similar, but it threw me off since 'bonne' was also an option and that fits 'nice' better than 'jolie' does... Just my opinion...Anyway, once I got passed that, the French portion became easier and I was able to skip ahead using the skip ahead feature so if you know basics, you're not stuck completely relearning them!So far, this is the best learning tool I've found to help me learn new languages and I would really love to see more languages added~!!

Headings: A little lacking, but otherwise good.
Base_Reviews: I originally downloaded this app to help me brush up on my French, which is pretty rusty after 15 years of little to no use, and my Spanish, which is just a little rusty after a year of little to no use. I am somewhat pleased with this app. I don't like it as much as I like my French and Spanish classes, but as far as a language tutor, it's great. The only thing lacking in this app is that it doesn't explain the conjugations of verbs with respect to pronouns. For instance--and I'm going to use Spanish as an example here--it doesn't explain why the verb 'ser' gets conjugated to 'eres' when you say "tu eres," or why it gets conjugated to 'somos' when you say, "nosotros somos." If it explained the process of conjugation for each language, that would make the app SO MUCH better and also help newbies have a fuller understanding of the language they are trying to learn. Anyone who doesn't know the first thing about other languages is going to think that this app is great, but if you are like me and you have had formal classes before, you will know that this app is seriously lacking. Formal classes give you the fundamental principles of the language to help you, and one of those fundamentals is learning conjugation so that you will not only understand what you're saying, but WHY you're saying it that way. I know this app isn't the same as a formal class, but if the developers are going to market it as an alternative to expensive formal classes, then they need to at least offer better teaching tools within the app.

Headings: One of the best language-learning apps I've seen so far
Base_Reviews: This is an excellent app and an excellent website. I've been a language learner for over 40 years, and Duolingo is one of the best facilitators I've seen. It combines some of the best aspects of its predecessors, like Rosetta and Mango, but it's free (!), and it's very entertaining (it keeps you translating sentences like "I'm a horse, and I speak English"), and it reminds you when you need refresher work. I've only been using it for a short time, but it's excellent for learning the bones of a language. I don't think it's for the weekend traveler; it doesn't give you the hello/how are you stuff. It concentrates on vocabulary and grammar (in a fun non-schoolroom way). So, if you just want to learn Please and Thank you and How are you?, buy a phrasebook. If you're going to be in Norway / Spain / France / Germany for a month or so, try Duolingo. It will entertain you and educate you, and give you what you need.

Headings: A good start on an NBC sports app, but with plenty of room for improvement.
Base_Reviews: The NBC sports app is a huge improvement over the prime-time coverage, but the app still needs work. It can be difficult to navigate among events; the olympics ended up being a single string of several thousand individual events, with no search option, and a paucity of informative labeling. To recognize the individual sports you had to identify the thumbnail image -- there was no accompanying text describing the event. Playback was generally good, with nice high resolution imagery, but from time to time the feed would fail or compression artifacts would interfere. I don't have any trouble with this streaming most video, so I have to assume it is the app or (more likely) the back-side server. There is no option to watch an event part way and then return to it at the same point, and searching and scrolling functions are awkward. Still, despite these problems, this is how I chose to watch the Olympics; the prime time broadcast is dead to me.

Headings: Get this if you enjoy being frustrated and miserable
Base_Reviews: If you're looking to seamlessly mirror content from other devices to your TV to follow along exercise/dance videos, learn a new skill, or enjoy general entertainment on the big screen...this product isn't for you.However, if you would like to be constantly dissatisfied or disappointed, you've come to the right place! Enjoy the frequent buffering and frame skipping of an inferior product that will never be mentioned in the same breath of a ChromeCast, Apple TV, or Firestick. But who values reliability and quality anyways? Being constant is dull. AirBeam TV keeps things FRESH by spontaneously throwing in wrenches into your streamed content. This app will take your favorite videos and movies, and mindlessly chop-and-screw it until it devolves into a hot/disheveled mess that once resembled your original content. But hey, everyone loves a good remix. Remixes are awesome and always better than the original!And if you enjoy horrible customer service, you can always count on AirBeam TV to not be there for you. If you had questions or comments about the product, but are repulsed by the thought of talking to a human being, AirBeam TV will gladly send you through an infinite loop of automated responses while deferring all blame to the user. It's not enough that I've restarted my computer and modem, closed all other extensions/applications, and checked the internet connection of my TV...I probably need to give up my left kidney and bladder too for my video content to be streamed without a hitch.AirBeam TV's connectivity strength and resolution may be inconsistent, but your disappointment with the product will remain constant over time!

App works just fine. You need to download the app *both* for your FireTV or Fire Stick, as well as a .dmg file for your Mac.  Once both are installed and running, and both your Mac and FireTV are on the same wifi network, you will have an icon on the top bar on your Mac to connect your TV as a mirrored display.The Mac software is a free trial - runs for only about 5 minutes, so be ready to test-drive the things you want to mirror on your TV!  See if you like the results.  The purchase price for the Mac license is $9.99.For me there is about a 1-second lag between laptop and TV, which is fine for screen sharing with others in the room.  It's like teleconferencing software in that regard.  I have not used it yet for streaming video, but I have another app for that already.

Headings: It would certainly be useful for monitoring a child with sound from another room ...
Base_Reviews: As this indoor camera is so inexpensive I had not got high hopes for it but it has surprised me.  It comes with a small bracket that can be fixed to the wall.  I use it to monitor my aquarium with discus fish and it is ideal.  Anywhere in your house that has a wireless connection can be used to place the camera and to view it over the internet.  I am able to check on my aquarium from my daughter's house.  One can move the camera remotely and I have found by experiment that it will zoom and focus remotely as well.  The colour picture is low quality which one would expect at that price, but it is adequate and also had infra red illumination at night with black and white picture. I have not used the filming or alarm at movement; or the addition of a memory card. It would certainly be useful for monitoring a child with sound from another room but would not record pictures in high enough quality for evidence. I view the picture using Bluestacks on my Windows 10 computer as the software is Android.  There is a Windows app on their website4 but with no instructions, I could not get it to work on Windows 10.

Headings: Absolutely horrible interface and regular crashing

In that time, the amount of recorded shows that had technical difficulties and crashed without recording the rest of the episode or having to start all over and find where it crashed is substantial.  And they only carry the locally covered NHL games so if you are a hockey fan, this is a terrible option.  Ultimately, this service drove me nuts and was extremely more frustration than an actual "service".  The only benefit it had over some other services (ie. Youtube TV) is that they are actual recordings that you can fast forward and skip commercials (as long as it doesn't crash the interface which happens regularly).  Otherwise, trying to figure out how to run the interface was and still is a complete nightmare.  At least on an LG smart TV.  I have to scroll up to get to a menu 6 or 7 times before it actually does it.  The UI is completely unintuitive and a nightmare to figure out.  Even when you finally figure out the completely unintuitive actions you have to take to pull up a menu while watching a show, you have to do it over and over and over before it actually does it.  The frustration level with this service is way beyond what its worth at one of the highest price points of all streaming services.  I highly recommend anyone who's considering this to just move on to the next service on your list.  This one is terrible.

I've tried quite a few drawing apps, and I have to say, this one is my favorite. I love how my sketches seem to almost happen by themselves! The feel of the sketch brush  really gave me confidence in my drawing. I've never been able to sketch something on my phone that wasn't overtly simplified and cutesy. This app changed that for me. I'm a fan.

I'll admit it up front -- I'm a sucker for draw-and-paint programs on mobile devices. There's something deeply satisfying about noodling around on a touch screen, building up an image. You learn early on that you can't expect to make anything as detailed or realistic as you can with physical media, or even a PC-based drawing program hooked up to a drawing tablet. But that's just the nature of the beast. They're built for different purposes.Sketch Guru is the latest offering from Bejoy Mobile, a company that specializes in simple drawing programs for mobile devices. In some ways, this is simpler than most. There are no layers, for instance -- everything is created on a single plane. There is no flood-fill tool. There is only a color palette, a color-sampler tool, and a set of brushes.But what brushes they are! These are not your normal set of smooth-or-fuzzy lines, virtual mimics of physical media such as pencils, marker pens or brushes. They are computational brushes, brushes driven by algorithms that transcend mere imitation. The "furry" ones sense the presence of nearby lines, and generate cross-linkages to them. There is a brush that creates a regularly-spaced grid of concentric circles. There is a brush that draws a swath of crosshatching, like loosely-woven cloth. The result is that even simple doodles acquire a subtle complexity, effects usually associated with much more sophisticated media.There are three other features that boost this product from 4-star "Like it" to 5-star "Love it". The first is the "Rainbow Color" option, a feature used in many of Bejoy's products, which cycles the color through the spectrum as you draw. Lifting your finger from the touch-screen changes the color. This is more of a gimmick than a serious tool, but it's a heck of a lot of fun. And, with careful selection of the algorithmic "brushes", it can create some stunning effects.The second "5-star" feature is the ability to send a drawing directly into another program. I have been pairing Sketch Guru with Autodesk's SketchBook Mobile, a more sophisticated drawing program. There, I can add new layers and work up the raw sketches from Sketch Guru into something more complex. The export doesn't always work properly, but it's worth fussing with it.The third "5-star" feature is the price. This is a free app. As in, actually free, not "freemium", where you get the basic program free but then need to purchase add-on features. You can't get any better than that!

Headings: Pretty awesome for the price of free!
Base_Reviews: I just downloaded this app, and so far it lives up to my expectations. I'm in college for an art related degree, so I'm pretty knowledgeable when it comes to digital painting programs. I was looking for a free painting app that I would be able to create decent quality digital sketches with. I haven't tried out many others, but I was happy to see this one offered a lot of the things I was looking for. Here's a list of pros and cons I've thought of after exploring the app for a few minutes.Pros: Better brush selection than I expected. Some of them seem a bit impractical for serious art, but for something creative and fun, its pretty cool!Ability to adjust brush width and opacity.Effective color selection. I haven't figured out if colors picked may be saved for easy reselection, but if so that would be a super bonus.Ability to undo stepsI haven't explored the eraser tool, but its good that its thereThe video playback is super cool, but I haven't figured out if the videos are able to be saved.I haven't explored what the photo editing feature does, but its cool to know its there.Ability to save. Note: images seem to save only as a PNG file.I didn't spend much time testing it, but it seemed to run pretty smooth with no lagging or choppy lines.If the eyedropper tool works like any other program with an eyedropper tool does, it should be to select colors from your image. I haven't tried it yet, but if that's what it does, bravo to the developers.Cons: Upon first opening the app, it looks like a kids doodling app.The ads are annoying, but to be expected with a free app.No layering features for the serious digital artistsIf there's no way to save the video playback, I think it would be something the developers should add in an update.Another note for the developers. Maybe add an option to save the file as a jpg.This is what I came up with on first impression. So far it seems pretty useful. For the price of free, its great, and I think its worth trying out.

Base_Reviews: Don't get me wrong, I love this app, and I use it all the time to make amazing things. But, while I can put up with the ads, I think there should be a few more brushes to chose from, that'd be great. Also, it would really help if I could use layering with my normal drawings. What I mean is, when you use a photo you can press an icon that looks like 3 papers, and doing so makes the photo go on and off the canvas. I'd like to be able to do this with my regular drawings, only, it can give me the option to choose another drawing from my gallery, so that way I can combine some incomplete drawings on the same canvas to make one, completed image. I'm sure this is probably a feature on the pro version, if there is one, but I still think it would be nice to have those options on the free download as well. So yeah, 4 stars for an amazing app that just needs some minor adjustments in the next update, please and thank you. Other than that I love this app and I definitely recommend it for anyone who likes digital sketchbooks! <(^v^)>

Headings: Good, but weak on handling of incoming calls.
Base_Reviews: I'm using this app on a Kindle Fire HD 7.Skype, in general, is excellent. This version of Skype app for Fire is only OK.It works well for making outgoing video/voice calls, and texts.If the Fire is locked, incoming calls/texts aren't notified and don't appear until you unlock and open the Skype app, at which time they appear as missed calls.IF the app is OPEN and TOPMOST on the screen (or the top app in the open-app-stack), it works fine for incoming calls. Incoming text messages appear almost instantly, but without any sound notification, so you need to watch the screen if you're expecting a message.If the app is either not running at all or not on the top of the open-app-stack, incoming calls aren't notified at all.Also, even if the app is open and topmost on the screen, calls to a Skype phone number from a mobile or landline phone (as opposed to from a Skype contact) don't appear on the Fire (but you do eventually get a "missed call" indicator).All-in-all it appears to be well behind the Skype app on other devices; I don't know if that is because development is lagging or because the Fire simply doesn't have the capability to respond to incoming notifications.

Since Skype isn't available through the BlackBerry World App Store in Canada, it had to be downloaded through the Amazon App Store on my Uncle's BlackBerry. Basically, my Uncle lives in Canada, and he's not tech-savvy at all. I live in the US (SW Virginia), so I had to walk him through downloading Skype over the telephone. For some odd reason or another, Skype isn't available for BlackBerry devices in Canada. However, my Uncle has a newer (and I use that term loosely) BlackBerry "smartphone" on the Rogers network which includes the Amazon App Store. Considering the fact that he's not a tech person, he doesn't have an Amazon account. I had to "loan" him mine to download the app. After about an hour of hearing things like "There's no 'download' button, only a 'get app' button." or "Am I paying for this? I already pay too much." the application was finally installed on his phone. I set up his Skype account remotely to avoid any more unnecessary confusion, and I sent him the login information. As soon as he accepted my friend request, we were talking face-to-face over 800 miles away! Now, considering that my Uncle lives out in the boonies of Ontario, the call has dropped once or twice. But the overall is surprisingly good from a BlackBerry to my iPad 2. Sometimes we even talk through my Samsung Galaxy S6 or my Acer Aspire | M laptop. The microphone quality sucks in-general on my laptop, but I use a USB Behringer Mixer with a RadioShack Vocal/Karaoke microphone to get the job done. All in all, Skype has served us well for many years. FaceTime, however, never worked right on my iPad 2. And since Microsoft and Skype are now partnered, it's easier than ever to use!

Headings: Happy with voice calls, but app needs updating
Base_Reviews: UPDATE 8/11/2016After writing my review below I have been experiencing problems with Skype on PC after five minutes after connecting.  I hear the voice of the other person, but the other person does not hear mine. Also the line has started to drop. I keep my app updated in my PC and was quite satisfied with it until say the last month, when having a chat online has becoming too much of a hassle on my PC, but if I use my Skype for Android I have no problem.Please fix the app for PC, otherwise is worthless at present.PREVIOUS REVIEWI have used Skype since it first saw the light, many years ago. I  have it installed in my computers and gadgets. I use it all the time. In my PC at least once a month for intercontinental chat about 1-2 hours long.Regarding Skype for PC, I am mostly happy with it. The quality of the sound is usually very good, with no return sound or delays nowadays, which used to happen often in the past. The line drops at times but rarely. In the last year, using this app *at least* once a month, I have had a bad experience just once.My main problem with the app is for voice+audio chats, as it is a pain in the butt: frozen images, or very slow movement or very bad quality image. I don't know if it is related to my Internet carrier or not, but it is most annoying. The result is that I don't make video-calls any more.Skype's interface for PC is a bit outdated, not clear enough and not customer friendly enough. The home screen should clearly show the options, voice call, video call, written chat alone, send photo and/or doco, plus the contact list on the side bar.My account is totally private, only close friends and family are there, I cannot be found by name or email. Headings: Some things to note about the latest Skype version
Base_Reviews: I have had a 32GB 8.9 HD kindle since it first came out in late 2012 & some earlier models. If you read through many of the reviews you should notice that most of the 5 star ones were written shortly after the release of the HD series in late 2012 & early 2013. On the other hand, the poor 1 & 2 star reviews were written since late 2013 & later.I would agree with this as it matches my own experience. The original Skype for the Kindle Fire HD series worked very well but an update issued sometime late last year changed all of this. There appears to be two main issues:1. SOUND VOLUME:Even if your volume is set all of the way up before launching Skype, conversations are barely audible. This may be because MS/Skype expect you to use ear buds which is a common way to use the app. If you in fact do this then you will find the audio level to be okay. HOWEVER, if you don't use ear buds then check the volume setting within Skype using the hardware volume switch and you will probably notice that the volume is way down around 25%. If you raise the volume to 100% using the hardware volume control then conversations can be heard okay just like the earlier version and it stays this way in subsequent sessions. They may have made the initial setting this way to prevent ear bud users from blowing out their ears.2. CRASHES:I don't know what to say about this except to confirm that I have had the same experience. Skype starts okay but invariably crashes (frozen screen, no sound, etc.) within 5 minutes and will then the Kindle will spontaneously reboot. This makes what is otherwise an excellent app next to useless.So, this problem has been around for over 6 months without being fixed. Amazon gets a failing grade from me on this issue as they should at least make the original version available for download from their app store for folks having this problem while they are sorting out the issues with the latest version.

Headings: Text Me App is GOOD, does what it's supposed to, but too many ads unless you Pay for No Advertisements!
Base_Reviews: TextMe is a good application for texting those friends and family with a smartphone or cellular phone where they have text messaging enabled. In the beginning, far less advertisements were part of the experience and after recent install on my Kindle Fire tablet I've had the system lock up and even crash. On both Android and ios the install was rapid and I didn't ever experience a crash or sluggishness. I did use my neighbors Kindle Fire, a slightly newer version, and he and I experienced very similar problems. However, it will work on all platforms and he and I actually text each other through TextMe daily. You'll get a new phone number or you can bring your current smartphone telephone number over and porting works well. You can either pay for international texting to countries serious the globe or you can use the app to earn minutes by watching advertiser videos. They often will have a double points event. That's when it's well worth it to take part in any number of their point earning options. Most every call I've made has been of high quality and I've not had a dropped can and have made over 100 calls overseas. You can share photos and videos and it's great to keep connected with friends and family abroad or anywhere in the United States. You can pay to rid the ads and that's not a bad idea. I've used other similar apps, like Whatsapp, so can honestly compare. Whatsapp, created by disgruntled executives from Yahoo is the definition of Five Stars and they avoid ads at all costs. Go ahead and download and enjoy your new application! Cheers from Peter with 16 months experience with this app.

Headings: Without hesitation, I would recommend this app!
Base_Reviews: I absolutely love this app! It doesn't slow down my kindle, it runs smoothly, and (the best part) I can now call and text FOR FREE. I gave the app only four stars, however, for two reasons. 1. There are ads. This isn't all bad, but they are distracting, and I live in constant fear that I'll accidentally tap one and I'll be redirected somewhere else. 2. Although texting is completely and utterly free, calling requires "credits". You earn credits by watching and rewatching the 15 second ad videos over and OVER again (each time, earning only one or two credits), or you can play a small free game and/or submit your email and subscribe to some website and earn more credits that way. But, another plus: unlike Skype and other such apps, the person you hope to text does NOT need an account also. You can simply type in their phone number, and from there you can text and call. Likewise, a person can call you with the free phone number that TextMe gives you when you get the app. Overall, I would definitely recommend this app!!!

Headings: The 6 month update, tldr = not free, more like "Bugmeware!!!"
Base_Reviews: All the things I said before are true. The app works, the price for the "No Add's" version is high, to high unless you are using a fire tablet as a primary texting device. The App gets more of a "PIA" the longer you use it. Dire warnings that unless you text or call someone in the next "X number of hours" you will lose your number ! If This was after 6 months of more I could see it... But the way This App works it's like blackmail to keep your phone number... It became such a pain that I removed the app. This is why I made This edit and dropped my rating from 3 stars to 1Star.  I think the "Free" label is false advertising, Free Trial would be closer. If these folks came up with a tiered cost system it could be a workable texting app. But with the $14+ a month price just to use the app without adds or use it or lose it threats, it's not worth it for my use. Why they don't see that  a $20 a year for 250 texts a month or something like that would give them a larger user base and how hard is it to count texts? Software! They have to have This for billing and management anyway.  Look elsewhere if you are just looking for an app to send a text to share a story you found reading the Washington Post with a friend.This App works. It gave me a way to send Text messages from my "Fire Tablet" I wanted to be able to share some news articles without having to use email. I have not used the phone call function. What I don't like is the amount of "Please upgrade!" Messages... I know they have to pay for the service they provide and make at least some profit from the effort. I normally do buy the "no adds" version of any app I use. But the price these guys want is more than what I really use is worth. If you needed the phone call function and if it worked as good as the text function... The the price could be worth it. The only reason I used this app was I didn't want to add Google's play store to my fire, if not for that I would have just used my Google Voice account.

It IS in fact, the best product on the market that I have encountered, but the price is quite high -- I found the free app "Duolingo" to give it a run for its money for the more commonly taught languages, and there is a lot that can be cobbled together from various sites and YouTube.I had purchased and worked with Rosetta Arabic ! about 10-12 years ago when investigating "self-instructional" language programs for students at my university. I found the pedagogy a bit lacking. This year, I took advantage of their "back-to-school" half-off sale  and find it much improved -- the on-line version, anyway. The first part of a lesson is an overview of the material, then it is broken down into focusses on discrete skill areas - listening, grammar, reading and writing. Every two weeks, you get a 45-min. session with a tutor via a form of Skype.I haven't investigated the games function yet, since I haven't gotten that far. Like all learning products, it requires self-discipline and motivation,but the pacing of the materials keeps you going.Some, but rather few, of the pictures and graphics are culturally appropriate. I think for verbs and everyday activities, they use the same photos for all the languages.

Headings: A not so mobile mobile app.
Base_Reviews: While the workflows for this app feel better than the PC version of the software, the app is severely limited by it's requirement for an internet connection.  I started using the app at work, which luckily has WiFi, however as my device has no cellular connectivity, I have been unable to use it during my recent travels, nor will I be able to use it to study during the 12+ hours it will take to fly Germany,With the Kindle Fire version of the App, the only apparent need for the internet connection is to sync your progress to the Rosetta Stone servers,  which is useful if you are going back and forth between your PC and mobile device while learning.  However, even this functionality does not work reliably; in my experience the App and PC only synced automatically every third or forth attempt.  While the PC has a force sync option this is not available on the mobile app so you are forced to restart the application through the device settings and hope that your PC synced properly at home.With these issues in mind and the fact that I like to use my Kindle while away from work or home, I wish the Rosetta Stone would have chosen a different method to generate a micro purchase income from their users; such as charging a one time fee to download the App, or charging for some of their more advanced online services.  The fact that I can't use the App as a a true mobile learning platform is endlessly irksome.I also wish that Rosetta stone had built in better orientation support for the app.  I have yet to figure out how the app is determining it's orientation for the session, but more often than not, the app will be incorrectly positioned in relation to how I wish to hold my device.  This is especially troublesome when attempting to use the app while charging the device.TL:DR - While the orientation problems with the app can be annoying, the biggest limiting factor is the requirement for an internet connection.  Which if you are using a device without cellular support effectively makes your mobile device about as portable as your home PC.

Headings: Fun way to learn French?  Oui.  Super-easy... non.
Base_Reviews: I have ALWAYS wanted to learn French, and now that I'm retired I have the time.  At my age I'm not somebody who wants to go to a class and have enjoyed other online learning experiences so I was ready to try this.  The concept is really simple; they show photos, usually four, and then they have a phrase; you choose the photo that fits the phrase.  There is NO English involved, which seems daunting at first, and you probably will choose some (maybe many) incorrect match-ups between phrases and photos, but you will eventually choose the correct pairing and learn the work or phrase.I get why there is no English as in other products as it's really a crutch and I think will slow down learning, but at times it is frustrating when you see a word with another word, and then later on you see the same word with another word... like 'La femme' for one photo, and 'Elle femme' for another later on... haven't figured out what the significance of that first word is yet, and it isn't explained, so I did pick up two additional books; one is just a pronunciation guide, and the other is a dictionary.I found the second lesson confusing at first as I didn't know what they were expecting me to do, and with no English instructions it was fairly frustrating at first.  A few tries later I realized that they were just speaking phrases and they wanted me to choose the photo of the scene they were depicting, based on the limited vocabulary they had taught in lesson one.Overall, I'm very happy with it and think that I can learn the language by going through all five levels, which were in the set that I bought during a brief 1/2 off special.  Now, something that I believe about RossettaStone is this; this software system doesn't want to just help you learn some of the language, words, phrases, etc. but is teaching you to start 'thinking' in the language, and it's already working.  Yesterday I saw a small group of men chatting in line at the coffee shop and my brain didn't register 'men' it registered des hommes.  Ha ha ha.  Yikes.

Base_Reviews: Rosetta Stone really does make learning a new language easy and feels quite natural.The Kindle ap is excellent for learning the sounds, understanding the spoken and written word of a new language.The only real downside I've noted deals with keeping track of plurals, special rules, feminine versus .masculine or neuter and first person, second person, third person usages.  These are there and they are practiced but they are not clearly explained.  A great deal must be inferred.  But then, this is the natural way our babies learn their languages as well.  None the less, after the first few sections, I did pick up an inexpensive grammar book to answer and clarify some of these questions.By the way, Rosetta Stone is NOT free, only the mobile interface application is free.  But  I did not expect Rosetta Stone to be free.  It's a well designed, well presented study program.  I wouldn't expect this level of quality to be free.

Used Rosetta Stone for 3 1/3 years and finished the five levels of Mandarin.  Then I went to China for a month to study further.  I was very comfortable with the language, and people were amazed that all I'd done was "study online" (I did online lessons every week).  If you stick with it and do the online classes you'll learn your language in the speaking area.  I'm now reviewing grammar, as it isn't strong in grammar or writing characters, and I learned characters on my own.

This app is easy to use and you will learn beyond just basic phrases. However, if you are trying to learn a language you are totally unfamiliar with (I was raised in a Spanish-speaking USA territory, learned English as a second language, and I'm trying to learn Japanese on my own), a good university level/self-learning language study and workbook will be necessary. You will also need a good dictionary. Rosetta Stone will not teach you why the verbs and other conjugations are happenning, and you'll end up doing a lot of guesswork when dealing with past, present and future conjugations. As a companion of a college course curriculum or self-study college book, it will be great to have because you will practice pronunciation and reading aloud without having another person there, and it will correct you if you mispronounce words! If you are already familiar with the language, then Rosetta Stone will be all the refresher you'll need.

Headings: Not free, not cheap, and a bit shady, but works as promised
Base_Reviews: This app is fine. It is easy to set up, and delivers the content well. Be forewarned however that it requires a subscription fee to use it past the demo period. (Amazon needs to start differentiating between demos and apps in the titles, but that's another issue)The Rosetta Stone teaching method is the best out there for practical (i.e. non-academic) language study.That being the case, it is a shame that they use such shady (and as others have posted - greedy) business practices. This app is a perfect illustration: Rosetta offers this app as a "companion" to their desktop software (which itself is extremely expensive) , but then "pulls the rug" out from under their customers by charging more for it after the initial period. While not fraud (they do tell you up front), it does feel like a bit of a shakedown.This is in addition to the fact that they charge the same for their courses whether they're the physical product (disc), download, or online versions. All versions require internet access to activate them - so why is this?Moreover, the disc version I bought came encased in a shameful amount of cardboard and plastic. The contents consisted of two discs, a cheap (and unnecessary) headset/microphone unit, and a (also unnecessary) plastic activation card. These were inside a cardboard sleeve, which was in a plastic wrapper, inside a small box, which was in a larger box, which itself was surrounded by a cardboard sleeve, which was taped shut and shrink-wrapped. Seriously? C'mon folks -it's not like you're transporting the *actual* Rosetta Stone here. Someone needs to tell the Rosetta Stone folks that connecting the planet linguistically isn't going to mean anything if there aren't any trees left.They've got us over a barrel folks -their language method really is that good, but is it worth the cost? You decide.

Headings: Looking forward to doing my lessons!
Base_Reviews: These are words I thought would never come out of my mouth! This is a must have for anyone who wishes to learn another language, I am simply having the time of my life with this! I never knew learning could be this much fun until now. If all leaning was structured like this in school, I would have made the Dean's list everytime! Highly recommended! Try it, and get the word out...and no, I am not sponsored, I am just very happy. This tool is not just all fun and games though ( well....almost not all fun and games ), one must put forth the effort, however, each time you practice, the more comfortable you'll become and interested.The lessons are designed not to intimidate you, but for you to challenge yourself at your own pace, and if you know you didn't do well in a previous lesson, the programs are contructed to make  you want to do better and give it another try.My greatest challenge at the moment is; calming myself down and practicing the proper pronunciation of words to utilize the proper diphthong, however, if one keeps getting them wrong, no stress, take a minute ( or two ), breath, and give it another try, what's really cool is, Rosetta Stone makes it so much fun that even repitition doesn't feel like some arduous and frustrating task like some of the other learning ( parrot-like squaking; "Polly wants a cracker!" )  software out there. The price makes you want to scream but, once you give it a try ( I HIGHLY recommend the free trial before putting down your hard earned money ) and decide to buy, you'll know that you have made a wise investment if your intentions really are to learn a new language and speak it with confidence. I've seen other reviewers describing the same problem: When I select a talk to watch, it plays for 1 second and then an error says something like "this video has been paused due to a network error". Then I click ok, and click play, and the video starts. But the red circling hourglass indicator remains on screen as I watch and will not go away. Soon the error occurs again, and again I press play and again the hourglass stays on as I watch the program. My bandwidth is variable, but it isn't low. When I test it, I always find my test app sees 10 Mbps on the first run, 20 Mbps on the second, 24 Mbps on the run after that, and about 34 Mbps on a fourth test. So my impression is that my phone company (AT&T) always gives up to 10 Mbps a new stream, and then bumps it up if the demand continues. Also if I try streaming HD video on another devices or if I don't, it makes no difference in the TED app errors, and the video on the other devices works perfectly regardless of whether the TED app is running.  So I conclude the app isn't able to handle changes in throughput, even though all my other devices and apps (with one app exception) work fine. I suppose it's also possible that AT&T is using software to sabotage the app, but that seems extremely unlikely in my opinion. So fix this app!

Headings: It's easier to curse the darkness than light a candle.
Base_Reviews: Do you know someone that seems to know something about everything? You know, someone always able to provide an interesting slant on the moral issues surrounding new technologies and the old problems they're solving. The first person to know about things beyond the cutting edge, who shares with you what Bill Gates, Stephen Hawking, or President Clinton think about issues facing the world. I can tell you something about that person: They know TED.TED is my daily moment of Zen; it's salt for the world, adding flavor to everything it touches; it's conference around the world discussing local issues that have, or will have, global influence; it represents the modern view of knowledge, that only by sharing and collaborating can we achieve the impossible, know the unknowable, where we can, as Aaron Sorkin wrote, look into the face of God.Lofty words.That is the TED spirit. Brilliant, talented, funny people that are experts, or often creators, in their field. You can watch Sergey Brin demonstrate Google Glass, Sir Ken Robinson telling you about how to save your child from schools (I'm a teacher, so no complaints), listen to Stephen Dubner prove working at McDonald's pays better than dealing drugs, or Mike Rowe sharing how important, and thankless, are Dirty Jobs. Musicians, artists, doctors, lawyers, politicians, authors, scientists... The list goes on and on. The topics cover, well, everything. I can't even begin to list the subjects that come readily to mind, just listing my favorites would take a page or two.Someone once said ignorance was bliss; today ignorance is criminal. Issues are facing the world that will affect humanity; some good, some bad, but all coming. Many of these issues require citizen involvement, which requires citizens to be familiar with the issues involved, which means, I suppose, if you want to be a good citizen of the world you must watch TED.I promise this: If you watch at least three episodes, they have a YouTube channel also, and you don't find yourself looking for more that interest you, then I will work hard to get a full refund for you (they're free).So what have you got to lose except some ignorance (remember, ignorance means you just don't know; if you've had the chance to learn something and you didn't, that's stupid).

Base_Reviews: I love watching TED. I used to watch it on Netflix, but I watched them all and Netflix is slow to update their list. So I began to watch it on Youtube and playback was flawless, but the user interface for YT on the Fire TV Stick is not comprehensive enough that you can't read the descriptions. Now for the TED app on Fire TV Stick: nice interface, nice playlists, horrible playback. At best, streaming stutters (freezes and plays), at worst it stops playing or locks up all together. I would have to relaunch TED app to continue watching the talks. It is aggravating not being able to watch TED talk from beginning to end without the stopping. Oh and I forgot to say that once it freezes and continues playing, the spinning circle on the middle of the screen doesn't go away. GRRRR. It is necessary to stop playback and resume (sometimes that works) but at other times I have to quit the app and relaunch. Before you say, "your problem is your poor bandwidth", I say that condition might be true but after trying to watch TED on the TED app, I can follow that by play several TED talks in a row on YT with no problem. I think the TED app doesn't handle fluctuating bandwidth gracefully and the developers were too quick to publish the app. The TED app needs improving.

Headings: Directions for how to access SEARCH on TED app
Base_Reviews: If you like to learn new things, the TED TV app for Fire TV and Fire TV Stick is for you!  Released on January 23rd of 2015, this app seems to run smoothly and offers an enjoyable viewing experience on my Fire TV Stick. It's a small app (8MB) taking up virtually no space on the device, and it is user friendly for the most part.I do run into issues once I'm viewing a video with trying to get back to the main interface. I try the return button on the remote and sometimes get a black screen. If I hit the Home button and go back into the app and use the rewind button, I can get back to the main TED page. Weird!Other than this issue, I find no problems using and enjoying content with the app. It is a tad tough to figure out what to do to find more than the featured talks, but if you click 'down' on your remote you will eventually get to 'Trending' after you pass through your viewed videos labelled 'My Talks'.  Below 'Trending' you'll find 'Playlists' which highlight specific types of talks on various subjects like Sex, Insects, Tech, etc.There is a SEARCH icon in the upper right side of the screen, but it's tough to figure out how to get it to open.Here's how you open SEARCH:1. Get to the main TED screen with 'Newest Releases' showing.2. Click the upper part of the wheel on your Fire TV Stick remote (probably works the same on the Fire TV or use voice search feature) to 'up' and see the magnifying glass SEARCH icon (red background with white magnifying glass) grow slightly larger.3. Press the center of the wheel on your remote to open SEARCH.4. Press a second time on the center of the wheel to bring up a keyboard to enter info, then click NEXT to SEARCH.The app is stable and the content is amazing, but the SEARCH feature was tough to see and figure out for me. I hope this helps someone else figure it out a little quicker than I did!

Headings: WHAT THE INTERNET AND TV ALWAYS SHOULD HAVE BEEN.......and finally ARE!
Base_Reviews: TED is one of those rare things that Television and the internet always PROMISED to be but never quite made it the full distance. TED is a rare gem that (if explored enough) really has something for just about everyone. The topics are as educational as they are entertaining and they are always expanding and enlarging their intensive array of short but very full videos. For those new to TED, it is a fairly new concept of gathering some of the world's best speakers on a wide variety of topics and giving them somewhere in the area of 15 minutes to connect to their audience by relaying information that is the best of the best. For those who are new to this I'd say GIVE TED a try. The folks here are not trying to sell you anything or beat you over the head with intrusive ideas. They gently invite you to listen and learn and widen your horizons. TED has made me laugh, think more deeply and made me more appreciative of this amazing world we live in.

Headings: It will help you to learn to read Spanish. Listening and speaking requires more than this.
Base_Reviews: Duolingo is a great program. I have been learning with it for just over two years now (I upgraded to the Pro version) and by studying at home, with just Duolingo, I am now able to read some Spanish novels, read some magazines and newspapers, and I have a general understanding of the language.But ... if you really want to converse with others, you will need more than this to do that. When I listen to Spanish TV or music or a movie, I"m lost. I have Spanish speaking friends and if they speak slowly, I will understand but in order to respond, it will take me too much time to think about how to properly frame the response. If I were asked to write down my response, I could do that more easily than speaking.My point is, this is an excellent program and I enjoy using it and feel accomplished. But, to truly learn the language, you will need interaction with others who are fluent in the language.Let this get you started and, if you find yourself enjoying it, get a tutor, take a Spanish class, or travel and do some immersion learning. As you're taking lessons, Duolingo will help along the way.Great things about DuoLingo -** It has an active discussion group, so if you're confused about an answer, just click and you'll likely see 100's of posts about that issue.** It has a dictionary so that you can find words that are not part of your lesson** As you learn words, it adds them to your personal word list and shows you when you last used that word so that you can practice vocabulary that you might have not used in a while.** You can read stories that are based on your reading level; it is not just grammar.** The Android version is very easy but I prefer to use it on my laptop or Kindle. Fortunately, Duolingo has platforms for all as well as iOS.** It lets you set your own pace and will remind you daily if you've met your goal for the day. You can change the time you spend per day whenever you like.** Duolingo has a podcast as well which is good to practice your listening skills. It may be too advanced, but it's still good to help you learn the flow and tone of the language.I deducted one star because many people will think this IS the answer, when in fact it is only a part of the answer. The program also has a bit of trouble with voice recognition but then, it might be that my Brooklyn accent does not translate well into proper Spanish.

This is more like practice than actual lessons, but it's a nice supplement for vocabulary and grammar review. Some of the Spanish to English sentence translations are too easy to guess out of the limited choices, because it's the only choice that makes any sense.  So sometimes it's just simple guesses rather than actually learning and knowing what the Spanish words mean. I love that it includes a spoken portion with the microphone, though!

My only quibble is that it doesn't really give any explanations.  When you guess incorrectly, and you do, sometimes have to guess because words are thrown in without introduction, it often tells you that you've used one form instead of another, but it hasn't explained how and when the forms are used.  I understand the natural learning strategy it uses, it does work, but I think I would catch on more with very basic usage explanations.  For free, though, this is a gift to the world.

Headings: Sentences are sometimes odd but good app

The main thing keeping me from rating it 5 stars is that there is no alphabet tutoring for the languages. If I'm learning Spanish, it isn't an issue. But, what if I want to try Greek? What are the letters, and how are they pronounced?

Duolingo is a wonderful language app that teaches through immersion. One actually learns conjugation in the early lessons without being "taught" how to do so. It is terrific how each lesson seamlessly builds on the previous one and brings back vocabulary learned earlier on to keep it fresh in one's mind. My son is using it to teach himself French before he studies abroad this Fall and I am using it to dust off my college French that I took quite some time ago. I would therefore wholeheartedly recommend this app to someone either learning a new language or brushing up on an old one.

This is a great program to learn with. Try it and you will immediarely be learning a new language. Before you know it, you will make connections between words that are meaningful and easy to remember. There are a couple of glitches but overall, this is an incredible program.

If you want to learn a new language, this is the app for you! It makes it easy to learn a new language, and if you need to you can go back to re-read words. The only problem is that you can't learn very many languages, including Chinese/Japanese, which I wanted to learn. With how great all the lessons are, I assume they will be updated to have them in the near future. Otherwise, this is an AMAZING app!

I've always wanted to speak another language, but I could never find an app that made learning something new fun and easy until my grandmother showed me Duolingo. One lesson and I was hooked and showed all my friends.

Headings: Excellent way to learn another language
Base_Reviews: I really enjoy this app.  The lessons are short, painless, and fun.  The teaching is a mix of assorted styles that actually enhances memory retention.  I don't mind taking the few minutes needed to complete my lesson and I feel like I actually learned something when I'm done.  Make a Japanese app next!  I would get that one, too!

Headings: Great practice and was surprised how much I remembered
Base_Reviews: Got this to brush up on college French over 30 years ago......Great practice and was surprised how much I remembered.  Strength exercises are particularly helpful to keep what you've learned fresh as you progress through the lessons.

Headings: Wow! I can't believe this free but it is.

I can only say very simple sentences right now but it looks like it provides an extensive list of lessons that will come as I continue to work through the lessons. I have had some trouble with getting the hang of conjugating verbs which this program doesn't spell out for me. So, I would recommend this program to anyone who wants to learn a foreign language. I downloaded this app with my former classes in mind thinking the basics were going to be extremely dull and basic  enough for a child to learn at a young age. I was wrong. This app is helpful so far and I am surprised at how much Spanish I remember during the lessons. The lessons seem to get longer as you progress, which I find to be a great idea in duolingo. very cool and easy app to practice a language.  Only disadvantages is that if a language has unique symbols like umlauts, etc  the Kindle keyboard does not show those options. and Duolingo marks it incorrect.  Also, the microphone does not always work.

Headings: Duolingo is an excellent language app
Base_Reviews: Duolingo is an excellent language app! It covers listening, writing, reading and speaking. You complete excercises at your own pace.  It also  enables you to redo parts of already completed sections to refresh the vocabulary and grammar you have learnt. It is the best language course I have ever come across.It allows you to listen again to sections to be translated as many times as you want before translating. When you mouse over a word, the English is displayed so this helps you translate when you are stuck on a word you don't know. It also lets you learn  different languages at the same time on the one app just by switching the language at the push of a button! You are awarded "lingots" after completing each section which is an incentive to continue as you can buy different additional bonus sections with them. This is a really well thought out language course and to top it all it was a free app! well worth 5 stars!

Incredible learning experience, reinforces what you've learned, reminders to invest time in learning, encouragement, everything Rosetta Stone isn't, everything Pimsleur should be.  This is a great tool and free, not in the current meaning of free (i.e. free for a few days then pay), but free as in no cost - ever, no ads, no pushes to upgrade, the only investment that is required is your time (so I guess its not really free ...)

It's free and helps the kid in spanish.

Headings: I Wish I Knew About Duolingo Sooner
Base_Reviews: If you're not using Duolingo, you should be. The App provides a simple way to learn any language. I tell everyone I know about this App. Quit saying "I want to learn Spanish one day" and start now!

Headings: I think this is a very good program. They use pictures
Base_Reviews: I think this is a very good program.  They use pictures, voice recognition, and recorded voices to aid you with the learning.  The sound quality of the recorded verses isn't the best but you can more or less make out what they are saying.  The give you daily email reminders to prompt you to study.  The only down side to the program is the limit choice of languages.  Otherwise, a very good program for learning a new language.

My love of  Italian music prompted my learning the language.  I'm so glad I found this program!  Now I find myself singing along and understanding a lot of it already after only a few lessons!  The program is really easy and fun at the same time, making understanding of the language just fall into place!  My son now uses it and I have it on every device I have! Love, love, love it!!!

Fantastic, easy to learn program and fun. Besides the written language you also get voice prompts so you hear how to say it. By the end of the first lesson, I could say several phrases and even a week later I still remember them. That is pretty good for woman  of 61 who is on several medications that cause short term memory loss. If you don't have memory problems, you will love this! Headings: Great tool, but the Kindle version needs work
Base_Reviews: I love this app! It's easy to use, and reinforces the things I've learned in  class. But, the Kindle version doesn't give the option of using accents (at least, it doesn't for Spanish). Headings: pretty good app for keeping your memory fresh

Headings: love this app, it goes great with the website
Base_Reviews: I use this app a lot. It is one of the strongest tools I've found to get me practicing French on an almost daily basis. They really make you work hard to learn a new language. So many real life scenarios and as you progress so does the work. You can test out your skills with others threw the online community. Headings: Fun, Easy to Use, and a Great Way to Learn!

I like how the app has matching games, pictures, and even voice recognition to make sure you are pronouncing the words/sentences correctly! It also gives you the option to turn off the voice recognition. I am thoroughly impressed with what this app has to offer!

Duolingo is a fun and easy way to learn another language. It's a little easier on a computer, but fun the same. The only problem I have is I don't know how to delete languages on my account. Apparently I am learning four languages now. And, they don't state the word very clearly on French. But otherwise, muy bien!

Duolingo is such a great app for language learning that exposes you to a variety of languages.However, while playing on Duolingo, it is VERY important to remember to also use materials to supplement your learning! Just using Duolingo and nothing else won't help you much with understanding grammar. In addition, I would also recommend you to use the web version as much as possible! The mobile version is slightly easier than the web one because writing out a sentence is just tapping words. :)Have fun!

Headings: EXCELLENT - levels get progressively harder, and it's all free
Base_Reviews: This has been a great app to review and deepen my Spanish. It's similar to Rosetta Stone in some ways, but I actually like this (FREE) program better. Headings: Best app I've seen to learn Italian

Headings: I like if for what it is
Base_Reviews: I like if for what it is. If you are a complete novice in a foreign language it helps you develop a vocabulary base. If you are like me and want to understand why certain verbs are conjugated in different ways, the difference between words that appear to have the same or similar meaning, or grammatical rules, you will need to find other resources.

You practice reading, writing, speaking, and listening, giving you a full experience with the language. You can also hear from the learning community about things you're struggling with, which I've found very helpful.

Duolingo is great for anyone who would like to learn a language. Although it teaches better if you have a microphone on your device (so you can work on your pronunciation), you don't need it. Nice and convenient way to begin to study a foreign language or brush up on language of your heritage. I wouldn't claim it as a complete source of study but I would compare it to a cellphone camera. The best camera that you have is the one that you have at the time you need it.

I tried to learn Spanish with Rosetta Stone years ago on my pc. I remember getting bored with it within a couple of weeks because it frustrated me. At first I thought that it made sense to learn a new language as a child does, with image and word association. After using it I realized that, as an adult, I wanted to know what the words I was learning meant, not just memorize what noise goes with each image.I don't mean to put Rosetta down, it's worked for a lot of people for a long time. But, Doulingo, in my opinion is much better. Aside from it not costing me anything, it also makes more sense to me to learn a language the way Doulingo teaches it. Instead of learning some words and very phrases over a 3-4 week period (as I did with Rosetta), I have actually learned many more words and longer phrases, and can put them together to say things that are relevant and useful!Also, the the presentation, rewarded skill points, and notifications really help keep me engaged. If feels like a game as much as an educational app. (I wish Spanish 1 & 2 in H.S. had been this fun). My 10 year old enjoys it too. In word matching vocabulary drills, the word "eat" pairs as a correct response to all of the following: como (I eat), comes (you {familiar} eat); come (you {formal} eat; comemos (we eat); comeis (you plural {familiar} eat); and comen (you plural/they {formal}) eat.  A more helpful approach would have been to match "I eat" with "como," "we eat" with "comemos," etc.Showing, not telling is the process used by Duolingo. Headings: This Is A Great App and You Do Learn
Base_Reviews: Fun and addictive.  I do Spanish and French.  Recently I took a speed Spanish course on line.  After using this app for weeks, I was ahead of the game when taking the course.  I never took Spanish in high school.  So apparently,  I actually learned something from this app!  I already understood the grammar rules and I knew most of the vocab already.  If I hadn't been usiing Duolingual, the course would  have been much too fast and too short.  I averaged 100% on every times and only missed one question on my final exam!The exercises really don't change much.  You are given a sentence in either the language you are learning or your native language to translate. If you set it, the exercises will also include you having to repeat a sentence in the language you hear.  (You can opt out if you are in public place and don't want to suddenly shout out , "I see a green pig" in Spanish in public).  Sometimes the speech recognition is iffy.  Although it seems to work much better on my Kindle than my phone.  The game runs very smoothly and doesn't crash (there was a very short period when it was crashing after an upgrade).If you don't understand why you got something wrong, you can immediately go into a forum discussing the sentence.  Usually there is a Duolingo staff person explaining, why the sentence is the way it is. Sometimes the sentences are a little weird and not something you would do in real life,  Sometimes the translation in English is a little off.  Anyway, you do have an option to send a notice to Duolingo that your answer should have been accepted if you got it wrong.The game, um, app has rewards that keep you going.  You an earn lingots which you can use to buy stuff in the store.  You earn lingots for going through an exercise without missing anything.  You get three hearts for each group of exercises. You can buy an extra one in the store.  There is a social aspect in that you can follow others.  But I don't see the worth, unless they are avid users like I'm.  There's an incentive to use it everyday so you don't break your streak.  You can also get notification or email reminders daily.You learn through repetition until you understand the grammar.  No grammar is explained.  There are not list of conjugated verbs.  From the very beginning, you are translating sentences.Research this app there's a great story behind it.  Then go view the Ted Talk video.
