I think I could actually get proficient in Portuguese within a few months if I work with Duolingo at least 30 minutes per day. That's not bad! I can imagine that kids would do even better than adults because they take to the technology so much easier. I hope they add more languages!

Headings: I've enjoy the application for the different learning levels
Base_Reviews: So far, I've enjoy the application for the different learning levels. It's a nice plus to connect with other that can "challenge" you in pursuit of achieving more in desired language. Not sure if one likes that it does the constant reminders of practice time, but sure every good application has ways of modifying things.

Not only is this app super easy to use on my 7" fire, it gives me daily reminders so I don't even have to remember! I was crossing my fingers that this wasn't just a smaller version of the desktop/browser Doulingo, and I wasn't disappointed--this is completely revamped for mobile devices. Glad I got this.

This app is wonderful. I bought it to see if I ciuld learn a few words in Spanish. As a retired speech therapist and educator, I appreciated the fact that the app incorporated listening, writing, speaking, comprehension and grammar skills as a teaching mode. I had taken French years ago and started the French to see how much I remembered. I did pretty well! I have to remember, though not to do both languages at the same time because I'm definitely confusing myself!! I would highly recommend this app to anyone who really wants to get a basic overall command of a language.
Never though being repetitious would be good - but it has certainly helped!!!

Been using this for a few months to learn Spanish and German. Not sure I consider myself very fluent in either yet, but think I could definitely get by. Fun and easy to use. I look forward to spending a fews minutes each morning using this app.

I love this app. I had heard good things about it and I can confidently add to the praise of Duolingo. The method for teaching is simple and allows you to learn how to form simple sentences from the get go. This is useful in order to see the grammatical structure in which sentences are formulated in whichever language you're learning. A feature that I really appreciate, and which is extremely helpful to understand mistakes, is the comments section. You can click to see what other learners have asked/replied to to the same mistake and even contribute to the discussion. For some learners this is a key point for the learning process. I highly recommend this app as an effective self study tool.

The duolingo is the best translator I have ever TRIED! (And believe me I have tried them all) The duolingo is 100% free! It teaches you how to say pretty much anything! one thing that it lets you do that others cannot is it lets you look at pictures for memorization and it lets you file complaints if you need to. (but there's really nothing to complain about) The duolingo is very special from others especially since you can communicate with others Anne chat and give advice about words and experiences with the different languages. Oh yes you heard me right you can even learn more then one language like Spanish French etc. I highly reccommend it and I think its about time for you to try duolingo.

This app is easy to use. I have learned a good deal of Spanish by using it. The only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars is that I was going to try to stack languages and start learning French but the application said I would  have to change my base language to Spanish. I wanted to keep practicing Spanish from English and practice French from Spanish.  Sometimes the voice recognItion is a little glitch on my Kindle Fire HD. However, I use the app every day. I would suggest it to anyone. This is the kind of thing there should be more of on the internet.

I love this app. It generally picks up my voice correctly, and the program has been excellent in helping me relearn Spanish and pick up German. Trains you to speak, write, and read. I recommend it to anyone who wants to learn English, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, or German. If you're interested in Eastern dialects, this does not have any yet, but I personally would be enthusiastic about the availability of Gujarati or Mandrin in a future update. It still deserves 5 stars.

I use this app to practice Spanish and it is a great program. I really like the fact that it has advanced levels because most language programs only teach the basics. The set up and format is very simple and easy to use. The only thing I think that could be better is the fact that you have to spell out sentences and sometimes if you make a typo it will accept it and other times it says the answer is incorrect. Typing on the Kindle isn't very easy and sometimes you can easily press the wrong buttons. Also when the automated voice says a sentence sometimes they don't speak very clearly and it is hard to understand what it is saying. Overall this is a much better program than most.

I love you get to practice spanish and Learn a lot of new words and you can go to the area where it explains if you miss something th  only reason I gave it 4 stars was because some of the levels have no training instruction you have to of had some spanish to know it or you get it wrong so it doesn't teach first or explain why you got it wrong only other people learning the language but you do get to practice alot

I have numerous books an have taken classes in the States and Central America and I feel this is a fun and engaging way to study Spanish. The combination of writing, reading, and speaking is important to really understanding the language. My current instructor is a native of Guatemala and provides my classes via Skype. He noted the improvement in my pronunciation and confidence speaking after using this program. I occasionally disagree with some of the translations but reading the comments has taught me a lot. Great language program!

Our of every app I've used, this one is the best. Every other language-teaching app throws you random words from the start, but this one has pattern that allows me to easily learn every word I need at my own pace.
this app combines userability with an interactiveapp that does not make learning boring.some areas of improvement could be providing explantion for controversial rules or tougher to understsnd logic

This app is so amazing! It is good for kids, adults, and elders! It teaches you how to speak, write, and use the words of a certain language of your choice. Im only 11, and I am already taking my high school language course, right here, on Duolingo! So please, dont listen to bad reviews or bad mentionings! Get this app and explore the words of German, Italian, French, Portuguese, and Spanish!!!!

Headings: for new and "just to brush up" learners
Base_Reviews: I downloaded this app to brush up on French while I took an intermediate college class. I was surprised to see that I was still learning words and phrases that I hadn't covered in class. The creaters use Roedger's learning technique, which improves learning dramatically. My 10-year-old is a beginning learner, and he's picked up a lot of French. I love this app. I hope it stays free, without ads. I'd gladly pay for it.

Using Duolingo to learn French, and so far it's working out really well (I'm only about 5 lessons in). The lessons are easy to follow, follow a good pace of introducing new words/concepts, and the app/navigation is really nice. I've used it on the web on my laptop, on my Kindle, and on my Android phone and while there are minor differences, it's easy to use on each of them.

Headings: Great app for the casual learner
Base_Reviews: I've tried the elementary levels of both French and German and have come to the conclusion that this is a great little app for the price. Kindle fire has no mic, so it never prompts me to do speaking bits. But I also haven't had a problem figuring out tenses or grammar, as the other reviews suggest. Very intuitive play. The only problem I have is that you need to do at least a little every day, or you will forget  what you learned. I don't think you will ever achieve fluency with a language app, but this will take you through a lot of the basic vocab and structure.

Headings: Don't waste your money on something else.
Base_Reviews: This is about the best imaginable app for what it does. I think it would be great if it had more languages (I.e. Mandarin, Aramaic, Arabic, Yiddish, Latin, Ancient Greek, Elfin, etc.) Using this helps a lot with reading, writing and understanding the chosen language. I am thoroughly satisfied with this app and look forward to any improvements. Thank you.

Headings: Duolingo a good way to learn a language.
Base_Reviews: This has been quite a surprise.  I thought maybe I could learn just a few words to help me when I travel but was happy to see that not only do I learn what can help me there but words that will help me converse with my gardner for example.  Although he speaks English he is more comfortable with Spanish and it gives me a chance to practice.  If you use the mic  you get feed back on how you sound when you speak and if you are pronouncing the words correctly.  You can't beat the price when companies that teach languages can charge hundreds of dollars.  I also like the convenience of having this on my Kindle so I can learn and practice whenever I want.  The only drawback that I can see is that they have a limited number of languages that you can learn at this time.

This program is set up very well.  I know spanish, and so far, I haven't learned anything new, but it is good for refreshing the memory.  There are mistakes though.  I don't know how much confusion this could cause a beginner.

Easy to use, and learned some French. I didn't have money at the time to pay for the rest of the French class, but would recommend this app to anyone wanting to learn basic words, some phrases, time, numbers, and a good start to learning a new language. :)

Headings: A great tool to help you learn a new language-but you gotta practice!
Base_Reviews: I've taken 2 adult ed classes in conversational Spanish this spring and find I need to keep up the learning process because I have a long way to go to be somewhat proficient in speaking this language. I saw this app in time magazine and loaded it instantly. I practice writing what I hear, multiple choice and also speaking the words. This is fun and I'm learning and building on what I've learned in class.

Duolingo is a great way to learn languages. You can learn to read, write and speak whatever language you want. And you can get extra lessons like flirting or idioms in the shop plus other cool things like outfits for your owl or tools to help you during lessons. And for all you Star Treck fans Duolingo offers Klingon lessons. :) Great app!!

Decided to brush up on my French.Fantastic approach to learning; listening, repeating, multiple choice and writing. I was especially happy with the initial placement test.Well done! Maybe I'll try Spanish next as a beginner.

Over the years I have bought several CD's from various companies and some of them quite expensive. I found Duolingo to be SUPERB to all others as it allows you to travel through at your own speed and lets you know when you have successfully completed an area. Then occasionally it throws in "old stuff" to help you stay fluent. I LOVE THIS APP! Thanks SO MUCH!!!

Headings: Awesome tool to help learn languages. Can't believe it's free.
Base_Reviews: I've been using Duo for over six months to learn Italian, and I still can't believe it's free. You may still want to use other websites to learn grammar and more vocabulary, but you definitely want to use Duolingo to learn how to put everything together. Maintaining the daily streak might be the best tool I have to make sure I keep learning.

This is a remarkable program!!.  While it isn't Rosetta Stone, it is a very close second and you can't beat the price.  I bought several language books in French and Spanish, but Duolingo is much easier to use and learning can be fun.  The only drawback is sometimes you need to take a break and I haven't found a pause button to stop unless you complete the lesson.

Like I said with the other post of the other language program I hate learning languages. I'm working on Italian language number 4 or 5  I am fluent in all my others... Italian is killing me and the program is great for solving those problems... I like it better than the Rosetta Stone program and I use both daily

Headings: This has been wonderful for me and my kids
Base_Reviews: This app is absolutely amazing! Both my 4 year old and 9 year old have their own account set up that tracks their progress, and they have made a lot of progress in a short time. There are so many languages to choose from and it's very interactive. This app makes learning fun! Good for kids and adults.

I have been dealing with Duolingo for over two years, first trying to relearn Spanish now French. They have made strides in making sure that it is a learning tool that can help anyone interested in foreign languages.

We travel a lot,  so I can practice different languages on Duolingo before we go to feel more comfortable with reading signs or with basic speaking/listening.  Wish there was a basic phrase dictionary for quick reference.

Headings: Best free app for foreign language!
Base_Reviews: This has helped me learn more Spanish than the 3 years of Spanish I took in middle school and high school!  The pronunciation is super helpful and the way the app rewords the lessons so you are learning the same vocabulary, but in different sentences.

Headings: Where was this when I was in school?
Base_Reviews: I have had 8 years of french and wish that this program was available when I was in school. This App is fun and I know that I am learning and refreshing my french. It also makes me feel more confident about my language skills and is very rewarding. I love Duolingo!
Like alot

I've tried a lot of apps to learn French. This one is fun and simple. There are no in app purchase catches. It has a few different styles of questions and though maybe a bit repetitive sometimes it really does teach you.My favorite part is if you do not check in constantly you lose part of your progress. Encouraging you to keep up on your skills.I take it back my most favorite part is the it's free.

Headings: Great app ... and it really is free
Base_Reviews: Outstanding.It starts a little slow but then moves right along at a comfortable pace. Good reviewing available. I use on my desktop ans Kindle. It looks a little different but works very well on either.I have used Rosetta STone and like Duolingo as much or better.Really FREE and NO advertising - what a nice surprise that was.

I'm using duolingo to review the French I learned in school and it's awesome. The lessons are very clearly laid out and well organized. The only reason I give it fewer than five is that a) it's great for review but I think you need more conversation to really learn a language, and b) the app is wonky and quits on me a lot, making it impossible to get to the next lesson (you can't skip). But A++++ for language review.

Headings: Great app to practice and learn a new language
Base_Reviews: Great app to practice and learn a new language. Only thing is that it makes you translate a lot and that is not the best learning experience, but is a good start and a great way to practice lexis and basic grammar rules. Lots of practicing options and a fun way to learn while waiting at the doctor's office.

Headings: Helps for learning the basics for an additional language.
Base_Reviews: Love, Love, Love this app! I am clearing the levels quick, easy to understand and quick to catch. Very educational and is helping me more than anything. I do mango, tried Rosetta, I can take DuoLingo anywhere with me and be able to continue where I left off. You have to finish the lesson to be able to start at the next one, if you quit or exit in the middle of the lesson, you have to start the lesson over, regardless how far you were. Love it though!

My favorite app. I regret buying rosetta stone... Rosetta stone does not allow you to use the app unless your paying extra every month. And their system is boring. In the other hand, Duolingo keeps you on your toes with daily challenges. And their owl is pretty cute.

Headings: a great way to learn a new language
Base_Reviews: I have been using duolingo to learn Spanish. I think it is the most intuitive way to learn a language other than immersion.  I like that you can go back and redo lessons if you take a break from it for a few days, and brush up on what you've previously learned. Sometimes I don't understand why my answers are incorrect, though and thst can be frustrating.

I have so much to say about this program, but I will keep it short. It has it goods and its bads. It assumes that you know some of the language already. The pronouns are throwing me for a loop. Very tricky and they don't explain that part too well. Other than that, I like being able to hear it, learn how to spell it etc. I am still plugging away on it. Wish me luck! Darned those pronouns!

Headings: Duolingo is great! As a retired language teacher
Base_Reviews: Duolingo is great! As a retired language teacher, it is obvious to me that this program is based on solid language acquisition principles. It recycles, recycles, and repeats per individual learning patterns. It's dynamic and exciting. Seriously! I've tried other language programs, and they're somewhat boring. You'll stick with this one!

I realized in hindsight that this looks like a children's game.  It was too late however, because this endlessly useful program is the best I've found out there for learning language's.  I also own Rosetta stone, but I liked this better for learning accents.  It's also more well made and easy to engage.  I only wish they had Korean.  Alas I must wait for them to finish making it.
Good app

This app is great, I am so excited to see if I can start understanding Spanish speaking people,and then be able to speak to them. I am 7 levels in and when we drive down the street, I can read the Spanish stores and know what it says, Exciting. The only thing I think would be better to know in the beginning is the numbers, alphabet, and how to pronounce them.
I've been using Duolingo for several years on my computer and have found it very helpful.  Now I can carry it in my pocket and practice, practice, practice even more -- it's wonderul.

Although I love having goals, I found this website a little off-putting when I was reminded at 11 pm that I had my quota of French yet to be met.  Although I had targeted 10 minutes per day for study, it many times took me 45 minutes to complete the two lessons each day, not something that inspires confidence.  I also found it difficult when new words or phrases would be randomly introduced without any predicate.  Considering that you have three possible mistakes in the course of 20 questions, new words at the end of a difficult sequence forced me to start again.  Slight spelling typos were also problematic when my i-Phone keyboard auto-corrected.  Although I love this concept, I think the program needs work.
Won't work on the Kindle fire. It just keeps going back to the first screen no matter how many times I pick a language. So frustrating!

Headings: Worth the time spent practicing with it
Base_Reviews: I used this to work on my once-fluent but rusty French before a trip to France, in conjunction with many other things such as watching youtube videos in French.  Alone it won't have you speaking good French, but if you need to brush up it's well worth the time you'll spend with it.  I didn't finish it before my trip and plan to continue with it for my NEXT (hopefully) trip to France.

Awesome refresher.Keeps you interested by rewarding you as you move along and allows you to set the intensity of the learning by setting minimum daily time goals. I enjoy the additional quiz options it gives to test your learning, and the hints if you are unsure of the correct word.

This app makes it fun to learn a language.  It has short lessons that help you to understand conversational Italian (my language of choice, but several others are offered). The lessons are well organized and build upon one another.  The format allows the student to have success, which makes you want to continue the process.  Since the format is similar to a game, it challenges you to go to the next level.  I also like the review process that allows you to go back to previous lessons. I'm currently on Level 3 so I don't know how comprehensive the entire program will be, but it definitely appears it will give you a very good foundation in a new language.  The only criticism I have is that the native speaker is sometimes hard to understand and I have to listen to her several times to make sure of pronunciation.  However, that is becoming less of a problem as I become more accustomed to her voice.

Headings: Great for language review and getting started.
Base_Reviews: It's good for reviewing infrequently used verb tenses and menus for travel. Pronunciation is included.Georges C

I was seeking a language app or program, and I discovered Duolingo in an online review. I studied Spanish, French, and German some years ago, and Duolingo provides an enjoyable way to review these languages.  It combines reading, writing, listening, and speaking practice in each lesson.The lessons are brief enough to complete in a few minutes, yet long enough to reinforce vocabulary and grammar retention.I installed Duolingo on my Kindle and iPhone, and I bookmarked the website on my tablet PC. The Kindle format seems to be the most convenient.I wish that Duolingo included Chinese.

I loved how this app built on previous lessons to teach grammar through use. I've been on the verge of true fluency in spanish for many years; reading and dreaming but never able to catch more than a few words in conversation or being able to speak. Duolingo was the perfect app for stitching everything together into a comprehensive whole. I've always struggled with grammar in spanish, and this app helped me develop a subconscious understanding. The only complaint I have is that there weren't formal grammatical sections. It would be nice to have lessons strictly on conjugation that I could practice.

The only thing is that you can only learn one language at a time.  I would like to learn more that that. Great for beginners like me who want to read, write and say the correct pronunciation of the words. I use this app along with a couple other free  (or nearly free, depending on where you get them) apps and books to better understand the rules of the language.

There's a good mix of all of these and I can go back and practice, practice, practice. It really is a lot of fun. I use it on the computer, which gives me the chance to use the special letters you need (accent marks, etc) and I now have it on my Kindle. It's different on the Kindle, but just as fun. Plus it's free!

Very easy to use with a friendly interface. It seems to use the right amount if repetition along with various methods of presentation to make sure you learn the concepts. Plus it's a fun way to learn. I recommend it to anyone wanting a low stress way of learning a language.
An excellent language learning program. I found it immensely helpful planning for a trip to Central America.

Fantastic app for easy learning...if ya want to work on it !!One major flaw for me is im learning Spanish , French and brushing up on Irish but the app regularly opens up in'learning English for Dutch speakers 'Takes a while to get back to my courses.This happens on my kindle fire 2014 hdand fire phone and for reference ipod touch 5th gen

I took French in high school but after many years of not speaking it I have forgotten a lot of what I learned. Duolingo is very easy and fun to use. The lessons slowly teach you more and more words and along with the images you can progress very quickly. I enjoy the fact that you can learn a few different languages. You can't beat a free language learning program especially since similar programs like Rosetta Stone cost a lot of money and work pretty much the same way this program does. I would recommend this to anybody interested in learning a second or even third language and for those who are learning English as their second language.

Headings: Great Way to Learn New Languages
Base_Reviews: I've actually not tried this out on my Kindle Fire yet, but I thought it would be a good idea to have it on there, just in case. I do have this app on my iphone though. I've found that it's a LOT easier and more motivating to use this app on mobile devices than it is to do it on the computer. Don't get me wrong, the website/computer version is good and well, but can be a little cumbersome. The app, if you've installed the right keyboards, which I don't think is very difficult (easy on the iphone, not sure about the Kindle yet. It was a Christmas present so I still am figuring it out), it changes automatically to the keyboard you need for each section of the lessons. I'm currently taking several languages, and it's nice to have the proper keyboard, a specified layout, and frankly, a whole lot less hassle.The downside is that the app takes longer to get the site updates. It took about a month for the app to acquire Russian for English speakers after the website launched it. If you don't mind that, then there isn't much of an issue, aside from actually learning the languages, which can be challenging enough, depending on the language and dedication you choose.

I use this mostly on my phone and tablet. Good for 4 of the languages I study.  More fun than games and you learn a lot on the 4 levels of language learning: reading, writing, listening, and speaking. I also recommend for my ESL students.

I've tried a lot of language apps, paid and free, and Duolingo is the best one.  Most language apps teach child-level vocabulary, one word at a time.  Duolingo uses complete sentences of increasing complexity from beginner lessons to advanced conversational language use.Every sentence of every lesson also has the option to discuss and comment.  If part of a lesson is hard to understand, people of mixed language levels including native speakers are probably already discussing it.Overall just a wonderful app, if you want to learn a language, get Duolingo!

Headings: Using it 32 consecutive days & counting! Need prior knowledge! You will learn spelling and grammer! But doesn't explain/teach!
Base_Reviews: Over 20 years ago, I lived in Italy for 4 years (not consecutive) and had several group lessons but despite the efforts of my various instructors, I just didn't have the patience to learn the grammar.  My knowledge of vocabulary was good enough for me to communicate and function but I never could get the hang of conjugating verbs, learning about the articles, and spelling words properly.  Later lived in Latin America for 4 years and that messed up my language skills big time!  So, now I speak both languages very poorly - just throwing out words to make a mishmash sentence.  A couple years ago I went back to Italy and they asked me if I could speak english because they couldn't tell if I spoke Spanish, Italian or some unknown language!  (Note: My native language is American English)So, I'm returning to Italy again for a 2 week vacation and I'm determined to be better this time and not embarrass myself.  So, I got Duolingo on Feb 20th and believe it or not, I'm truly addicted to the program!  I have a full time job and when I come home I'm tired and yet, every single day, I spend 1 hour to 2 hours working on these mini lessons from Duolingo!  Funny, they are kind of addictive.  They force you to learn the language by making you hear the language, speak the language, interpret the phrase back and forth between languages, to spell it properly, and put it in the correct order.  If you do it wrong more than 3x then, it kicks you out of the lesson and makes you start over, but the lesson is different the next time around.  Now, you would think one would get discouraged, I mean, I've had to redo some lessons about 6x, and yet, somehow, the way it is structured, it makes me want to keep at it and do it right!  I mean it is working on me, one of the most stubborn learners!So there are a multitude of topics at every level (beginning/intermediate/advanced) and within each topic they have 4-8 different minilessons in each topic.  It visually has a graph that shows you where you are at.  And, even when you think you are done with a topic (whew), every couple of days, that topic reopens and they make you practice it again so you don't forget!  Wow!  So, even with my background knowledge/vocabulary of Italian, I'm still at the very end of the beginners (Level 8; 335 words!) and I've been working hard for a month!  Oh, another downer is I was working on it for 12 days and suddenly it reset and told me I was back on day 1.  I thought it did that every 12 days but now it says I'm at 16 days. (IF ANYONE READS THIS FROM DUOLINGO; I WANT IT RESET TO FEB 20TH THAT I'VE DONE IT EVERY SINGLE DAY!).The downside is that if you have never ever studied a latin language this would be super hard for you.  I think if you already know a similar language like spanish and how it is structured, it will be easier for you.  However, if you are a person who has never studied a romance language and absolute beginner that only knows Ciao, etc..and hever had a lesson, then, you will have a hard time.  Also, if you are a miserable speller in your native language, learning to spell Italian will kill you because it is so difficult to get all of the vowels in the right place.  I have many times translated a very complicated sentence from english to Italian, only to get it counted wrong cuz I misspelled 1 letter!  But, it forces me to really think what I'm writing and how it all comes together to form a complete sentence.  Also, it really doesn't teach you the vocabulary or the grammar rules, at all.  I kept failing the lesson because I wasn't sure what some articles meant because they seem to mean different things at different times.  Yesterday, I finally broke down and got a grammar book so I can look up what all of the articles mean.  So, this program works for people who are already familiar.  I'm worried that when I get in the more immediate level, I might need to study before using this as it isn't really a good teacher - doesn't explain or introduce new concepts.  Good for people that really want to tighten up what they already know and go farther.

I am a beginner with the Spanish language. The structure of the lessons is confusing. Duolingo gets into the case structure too soon to suit me. Often I can not understand the Spanish phases. I must repeat them several times. I have had other Spanish software that I liked better.

Headings: Easier to use than Rosetta Stone, and free!
Base_Reviews: I am using this app to brush up on Spanish (learned 30 years ago) and German (picked up from my German family, but never studied formally).  I don't know how it would work for a language you were never exposed to before, but for brushing up purposes it is excellent.  You can easily test out of what you already know and focus on the areas that are weaker.  I also like that you are working on so many skills at once--from fairly passive translation (choosing from a list of English words), to straight translation in both directions, plus dictation and oral practice.  I mainly use it on my Kindle but also have it on my android phone.  Many thanks/muchas gracias/vielen Dank to the developers for keeping it free and ad-free!  Hoping they will add Russian to the list.

Highly recommended for anyone who wishes to learn any language.  There are many languages to choose from.  You can use this to learn not only how to spell the word but also how to say them.  It listens to hear if you have said something approximately correct and gives you feedback as to whether or not you said it right.  I learned quite a bit in a short amount of time. (This function can be turned off. If you're in a noisy, crowded place or don't want to be overheard.)The program, breaks down the learning of the language in much the same way as Rosetta Stone. That is to say that unlike your high school language teacher, you're not just learning active verbs or inactive verbs or pronouns in each lesson. You are learning phrases and how to build conversational structures.A couple of words of caution, however.The app assumes you have a basic understanding of the language you're learning. For example, I have a high school level knowledge of French, and this is been an excellent refresher course and brought back much of what I learned in school. However, when I switched over to try and learn a few German phrases so that I could be just as helpful on our trip, I found it more difficult and challenging to to engage with the program. That isn't to say, that someone could just try to pick up a language (for instance, I'm also working with the Italian section of the app. So when we go through Italy, I'll have some knowledge of the language.Second, the app won't let you advance to the next segment until you can complete the first without four or five errors per segment. Although it's not, strictly speaking, concerned with spelling as long as you're in the neighborhood, it will deduct points if you consistently spell something wrong or don't use the right accent over a letter.Overall though, I have really enjoyed using this and would recommend it to someone who wants to brush up on a language or learn key phrases in order to travel.

Duolingo is the most motivating language course I've ever seen.  It feels like a game, and is designed to keep you moving forward.  It is also concise and surprisingly comprehensive.  Each part has a lesson to read at the beginning, and if you don't understand why you got an answer wrong, there are discussion boards for each and every question.  So far I have not had a question I could not get the answer to, and I am almost halfway through.  I especially like how it encourages me to go back and strengthen skills in constant review.  This ensures that what I learn will eventually get written in my long term memory, its just a matter of time and consistency.  Anybody who uses Duolingo frequently, consistently, and for a long period of time (at least a year) will learn a new language.  Go ahead and get the answers wrong as often as you need to.  The algorithms are designed to program the human brain and you will eventually find yourself getting answers right in spite of yourself, even if you don't quite understand the grammatical principles behind it all.  Duolingo is built on principles of positive reinforcement, making it easier to persevere.  I use it in conjunction with short stories written in the language I'm trying to learn, and movies also in the language with English subtitles.  In only a month, I am understanding so much morevthan I ever thought possible.  I can't believe its free.  Its better than programs I've paid good money for.

Headings: Duolingo is an awesome way to learn and practice new languages
Base_Reviews: No two ways about it, Duolingo is an awesome way to learn and practice new languages. If you already have some education (say, old high school classes you wish you'd taken more seriously), it offers an assessment to put you at the right level, considering what you might already know. Duolingo breaks everything down into lessons that build upon each other, and prompts you to practice as you go, returning to older lessons to cement them while learning new words and grammar. Having used Rosetta Stone several times in the past, I think that Duolingo's program is just as good as the $400 software, and Rosetta Stone doesn't prompt users to go back to earlier segments over time.Duolingo also has a unique system where language learners help translate webpages (often Wikipedia) from their native language to the one they're learning, and will direct users to a level-appropriate page. This is a great way to see the language in a larger context, and helps give that feeling of confidence and mastery of the language.

This app allows me to learn things that I didn't learn in class that may be usefull. It's a good refresher during the summer and can really help you in a language class. Maby Italian next year...

I really don't know how it compares to other programs, since I have not tried other programs, but this was a free app and I like the combination of learning the vocabulary words, pronunciation and proper sentence structure.  It is better than sitting and playing other games.  I have traveled in Germany and so I know a little already and so it was easier to get started for me.

After years of struggling to learn german from books and even rosetta stone, my dad told me about this amazing app. Today I held my own in a conversation with my german co-worker. I didn't realize I had learned so much!  This app makes learning a language fun and easy and I highly recommend it!

The app actually included Arabic. I can't find any decent apps for it and if it was included here withthe awesome interface I could learn much faster. Overall great app. Brushing upon Spanish, learming Italian, neeeeddd Arabiiiccccc.Thanks for great work!

I really like this app! I really enjoyed Spanish in high school, and considered taking French for fun, so this app refreshed my Spanish memory and excited me to learn more languages too! This app may slightly confuse a beginner on verb conjugations because the differences aren't explained (at least not at the level I'm at yet) but it becomes pretty easy to tell when to use the different conjugations after a few lessons. I feel the pace is very nice for a beginner, small amounts of words added each lesson, not overwhelming at all. I do a few lessons a day sometimes because I can't wait to get into more! As a future speech therapist, I'm hoping to get a lot of use out of this app! :)

Headings: I can read and Write in french
Base_Reviews: This is a wonderful app, I began using this app Labor day weekend and its amazing I can have a conversation with my spouse of 31 years in french. This  app has fortified my french vocabulary and grammer in conjuction with having a native speaker i am very comfortable in holding a short conversation.

I have had this on my phone for some time and it was one of the first apps I downloaded when I got my Kindle Fire. I haven't had the problems others seem to have- maybe a newer version? But I definitely prefer this to the phone app, in no small part because it lets you test out of specific units. It does s!ow down/stop communicating from time to time but not nearly with the frequency others are reporting.

Awesome free app for learning many different languages. Probably the best one. It is designed in a way thats easy and fun to use. It keeps track of your fluency level, and I'm about 50% fluent in Spanish after only about 2 months. Highly recommend to anyone trying to learn a language.

This is very similar to an emersion program I bought for my computer a couple years ago. I downloaded this one onto my Kindlefire, and find myself using it way more since it's so portable. I like the feature of learning to write in Spanish at the same time--makes me pay more attention to the details. I just finished Lesson 3 and so far I'm loving it!

I've been using Duolingo for several weeks for Spanish and Italian. It's easy to fit the lessons into odd moments throughout the day. I like the progression of lessons and the way the "game" aspect of the app encourages me to continually brush up on old lessons. And it's FREE. Thank you, Luis and your gang, for making this so accessible.
Can work at your own pace!! Seems like a good brain exercise!! Could hopefully be beneficial in the world of today, if you stick to it!

I have tried several different programs but this is easily the best way to learn. The way the lesson is set up makes it easy to use, and fun to learn. It's more like a game where you must complete one area with one or more hearts in order to continue. You learn using pictures,words, and sentences. Very good learning tool.

This app is easy to use and you do find yourself quickly remembering words . You can set reminders, encourage others, and set goals. If you are looking to learn basic conversational phrases, this is not the right app. I would like to learn the language enough to speak, read, and write, so use this app to practice daily and continue to add new vocabulary.
Easy to use. I work at my own pace. Has already helped me at work. I get out of this app what effort I have put into it. Best one out there!!!!
Enjoyable all for language learning, it won't take the place of a good teacher or curriculum but is fun and helpful as an extra supplement.

This app has so many benefits. First, its free and user friendly. I think that anyone probably thirteen or older could use this app. Second, it's a fun way to learn.  I like that is shows me words  im becoming weak on and I have to practice those words again. Hoping this app helps me on my way to fluency.

This app is a delightful combination of having fun and learning something. Instead of messing around on the internet when I get bored, I can do Duolingo. The quality of instruction is high - I recently went abroad and was able to get by with what I'd learned through this app.

This language learning program is comparable to Rosetta Stone and it's free to use and easy to practice because the app is on my phone and I can practice any time like while  waiting in stores while my wife shops or when my kids are at sports practices.  very convenient.

Very fun and I look forward to playing it each day. It is almost addicting, exciting when you reach the next level. It has helped me learn new phrases and words. It has different learning methods, you can write what the person says, translate sentences, speak into your microphone when asked to say the phrase on the screen. Because of all these different ways you not only get better at the language but also improve the pronunciation too! Verdict= great app- definitely recommend for people seeking to be bilingual.

Headings: Improve or learn a new language
Base_Reviews: If you want to learn or better a language that you just learned, I highly recommend this application as well as being practical, it is also excellent for children, now there is no excuse to say no.

I homeschool my 3 children. We had trouble finding a foreign language curriculum that stuck; then we tried DuoLingo!!! I love how easy it is and how it makes sense. My youngest (3) is able to use it with a little help, and my older 2 love learning different languages. We love that it's free and that there's a large selection of languages to choose from.

The Duolingo app for the Kindle is really nice.  I have used the pc interface, android and ios and I really like how it operates on the Kindle.I am use a Kindle Fire HDX 7" and everything is clear and crisp on it.  I'd say the only problems I run into are the occasional restarts when I am in a lesson or the times I open up the search tab when I am trying to type an answer.Another minor issue is the auto correct on the Kindle sometimes incorrectly fixes your answer so it is best to check over what you have typed before hitting check.Overall, Duolingo is a fun language learning tool that in many ways reminds me of Rosetta Stone without the high cost to go along with that.Right now in app Duolingo offers Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, and Italian. Dutch, Irish, and Danish are in beta and Hungarian, Swedish, Turkish, Russian, Polish and Romanian are hatching.

Headings: A really good approach to learning is used
Base_Reviews: I am using it for Spanish and Italian.  A really good approach to learning is used.  Good practice exercises.
Has helped me a great deal. Would definitely recommend.

I am 72 yes old and learning French.  I never took French in school so it is a challenging subject to keep my mind active.  It really gives you a chance to learn all aspects  of the language at your speed.  You can go back and redue your steps so you don't forget what you thought you had learned.  Who knows I may go to France someday.

Headings: This is a great app. I downloaded it for my daughter so ...
Base_Reviews: This is a great app. I downloaded it for my daughter so she can have something constructive to do on her tablet. I'm really glad I did, she loves it and is learning really fast, what a wonderful and fun way to learn a new language.

I've only been using Duolingo for about a week and I'm surprised how much I'm able to retain from one day to the next. I don't pick up languages easily and I just wanted to learn enough to get by. I think I may end up being able to do more than just get by.

This program is so great, I can't believe it was free.  Apparently there are multiple languages in this program, but I chose English to Spanish.  It's divided into lessons, and each lesson has multiple parts, including speaking.  It will even send you a reminder, if you so choose, so your activity is consistent.  What have you got to lose?  Definitely try it!

Headings: love the concept, now for an improvement/suggestion
Base_Reviews: Really like the app.  I am more positive about actually retaining the language I want to learn.  However, the app never could understand what I was saying into the microphone... not sure if it just didn't pick up anything or if my inflections were always too far off to count.... might be helpful if it played back what it heard.  Also would be nice if the app could change the keyboard language to the language it is asking the user to write in and every it back to original keyboard language upon quitting.... Spanish and English are at opposite ends of the keyboard language list on my Kindle fire.
Easy daily reminders - chose a five minute daily lesson.  Perfect - I can do more if I have time!

Headings: This is a great app to learn some basic Spanish and doesn't require ...
Base_Reviews: This is a great app to learn some basic Spanish and doesn't require a lot of time each day.

I love this app, usually with language apps it's either hit or miss with most of them on the miss side. This app actually teaches you not only vocabulary but also grammar in a very concise step by step guide. I'd say it's almost like a mini Rosetta stone. My problem comes when I'm in the middle of a lesson and all of a sudden it goes back to the menu. I'm using kindle fire HDX so I don't know if that has something to do with it. It's incredibly annoying and frustrating when you have to do the same lesson five times because of crashes. I really enjoy this app, and it's actually helping me learn some Spanish but I'm going to be forced to stop if I can't move forward. Please fix this.

Headings: Issue on kindle fire showing pictures
Base_Reviews: We are having issues with the app showing the pictures on our Kindle Fire 8's.  We called the Amazon support people and from what they can diagnose, it's an duolingo issue.  My kids seem to really like the app.  Being at the beginning level, they know enough Spanish to figure it out without the pictures but worried it won't be so easy as they advance levels.  Hoping we can figure out what's wrong.

Headings: When you move from one level to the next the ...
Base_Reviews: When you move from one level to the next the introduce you to words you have never seen before and expect you to simple know how to translate them.  There ought to be some level of teaching prior to translation ect.  yet there is not even an introduction to the words.

Headings: Easy to work on a language for just a short time each day!
Base_Reviews: I really like exercising my brain with this app. It is fun to learn some Spanish and doesn't take much time at all. I really like how it customizes for you. It shows you the words you need to work on the most.

Admittedly, I am a language geek. But I have been coming back to this app over and over since getting a Kindle for Christmas to learn Italian, and my 11-year-old daughter has been enjoying learning French. It turns language acquisition into a game with new challenges and rewards at each level. Typical challenges include speaking into a microphone, filling in missing words, and typing in sentences that are dictated or written in the other language. It's a little frustrating to have to type accurately in the target language, though.

Headings: Fun and free! Not a ripoff like many "free" programs
Base_Reviews: I love using this app! I took this foreign language in college but haven't used it til now. Duolingo is an excellent refresher AND is teaching me more than I learned in college!

This is such a great app and I can't believe it's totally free - I love it!!!It teaches through a variety of methods, all intertwined to really immerse your brain in the learning process. For instance, I'm currently learning Spanish; I have to select correct photos with the Spanish word identifying them, translate Spanish phrases into English and vice versa, speak Spanish phrases to see if my pronunciation is correct, etc. This app reminds me a lot of Rosetta Stone (I was able to use that program for a time through a former employer) but a little less overwhelming; each lesson is very short and sweet meaning you'll actually do them (I remember dreading - and eventually stopping altogether - the RS lessons because each was at least a solid hour commitment each day which is a total buzzkill when you factor in work, social, and volunteer time). So, you can do one short lesson or if you've got the time breeze through several...the app views either as an accomplishment. And I love the owl reminders in my inbox each day because seriously: I can be a space case.This is a solid app for anyone wanting to learn a conversational foreign language, which is really the point, right? I mean, all I want to be able to do is communicate with other human beings in the language of the country in which I'm traveling (without an electronic translator!); who cares if I'm able to conjugate my verbs correctly every time I say something? I'm looking forward to learning a few languages with Duolingo!:)
This is one of my favorite learning apps. I was so glad when I discovered it is completely free. You can set daily goals,  and it helps you strengthen the areas you need help with.
It just tests u,doesn't actually teach,but I'm not giving up on it
Program was easy and fun!

I find it a useful and fun refresher course that helps me to communicate better with my customers at work. Both of my teen daughters use it to assist with their school French classes, keep up over the summer, and to learn additional languages.  Don't hesitate - just get it.

I use duolingo to teach English to Mexican kids.  I also introduced a friend, a retired Mexican pediatrician, to the program. He thought he could not learn English, but in just a few months he can carry on a conversation.  I use the Spanish course and it is perfect for my needs.  My friend is 75 years old, I am 68 years old, and my kids are 8, 10, and 11 years old, proof that the program works for all ages.

The Duolingo App was something I stumbled upon and I am glad that I did. I have all intentions to live and travel abroad and in order to enhance the experience I'd like to know the language. Granted that all languages aren't on the App itself, the ones that are available are top speaking languages. I have taken courses in both Spanish and French middle school through college and do not remember as much as I would have liked (no offense to my instructors, they were wonderful). Using this app is fun, effective, and encouraging. I'm looking forward to learning and speaking as many languages as I possibly can.

Headings: This is a great! I'm actually learning the language I always wanted ...
Base_Reviews: This is a great!  I'm actually learning the language I always wanted to, and they make it so easy!

Headings: I love duolingo and use it for hours at a time ...
Base_Reviews: I love duolingo and use it for hours at a time learning French ... The reason for only three stars is that I decided to take the placement test right off the bat without knowing anything about the program and bang! I'm instantly put at level 9 and I don't know how I got there...not sure which way is forward..not sure how many levels there are.. and there's nowhere to go to get answers.

Headings: It's Fun to Learn Something New
Base_Reviews: I heard about Duolingo from one of my friends at work. I am learning Italian right now and I would love to relearn Spanish. It is a fun app and it seems to be fairly easy too.

Headings: Easy to use.  Well laid out.
Base_Reviews: Very similar to expensive language lessons, but easier to use.  You can go very quickly through lessons if you're familiar with words & phrases.  Its great if you want conversational lessons.  I'm about 1/4 through so far, and I've picked up enough to have a basic conversation in Spanish if I have to ask directions, basic questions, etc. when travelling.

Headings: Very easy to use and learn a new language
Base_Reviews: Very easy to use and learn a new language!! I LOVE this app and I've been telling everyone how great it is.
This is a very good program.  It starts you with baby steps then gradually adds more challenging content.  It is not boring or too difficult. Kids and adults will love it.  I'm learning German.

I must admit I had my doubts with a free app.  But I have been amazed!!! I have been able to brush up on all the spanish I learned back in high school.  I am sure it may be a little bit more difficult for someone with no spanish background...but you would catch on quick.  It's fun and rather addicting.  At this rate, maybe I'll be fluent in a couple weeks :)

Duolingo is hands down the best app for learning a different language. It's fun, educational, and very easy to learn. Plus, it doesn't cost an arm and a leg. I have been using this app for a couple weeks now in the hopes of being decently fluent in another language when in travel out of country. And I gotta say...I picked up learning that language FAST. Thanks duolingo! 5 stars for you.

Headings: Duolingo is a fun way to learn a language
Base_Reviews: Duolingo provides a quick and simple method for studying another language in your free moments. You can sent your own pace and feel satisfied as you look back at your progress. The lessons are short, but educational. The app keeps track of what lessons you need to review to keep sharp. Finally, an app you don't have to feel embarrassed to admit you spend time using.

Headings: Good Concept- but slow and cumbersome.
Base_Reviews: I have just started using Duolingo, but have found it slow and repetitive.  The concept is good, but the app does not fully live up to concept.  I am working on learning Spanish, and using Duolingo as a secondary source and practice.  At this point I would not use it a primary or a stand alone tool, but as a secondary source it has worked fairly well.

App works smoothly and provides a great way to improve your foreign language skills--similar to what happens when you go somewhere and just learn the language by hearing and speaking it. I'm relearning rusty language skills, and it works great for that. Look for some other reviewer to get a perspective on learning a new language from the beginning.

I have used Rosetta Stone and DuoLingo works better for me hands down. I find it more intuitive and easier to use. I am brushing up on my Spanish and now learning German. They make it so easy to learn new words and sentence constructs. I highly recommend it.
Wish they had Russian! It works good and its fun, just wish they had more languages, and more outfits for Duo.

I've been using the app to study French for a few days now and I'm really enjoying it. I have used Rosetta stone in the past and I think this is pretty comparable.  There aren't structured grammar lessons, you just jump in, start translating and learn by doing.  It's easy to use and fun!

I am living in Peru and I use this to build my spanish skills.  It is great for vocabulary and you can learn spanish, French, Italian or German.  It's very helpful, but make sure to check for updates every once in a while.  My sister had a better update than me for a long time and I didn't know how to update it.  Great app all around!!!!

Headings: This app is wonderful. It is enjoyable and actually helps you learn ...
Base_Reviews: This app is wonderful.  It is enjoyable and actually helps you learn the language.  I really like the new 'bots'  that allow you to have a written 'text' conversation with an invented native speaker.  Really brightens up the dull repetition needed to remember what you learn.
I love using Duolingo because it's easy to use. I can move at my own pace and repeat the sections as needed. I really feel that I'm learning through practice and repetition. Great app!

Great app. Learning the basics of 2 languages, about 5 minutes a day for each. Able to "test out" of a section or go back and do a "review" module rather than a full set of lessons for a section. UI is very nice, easy to navigate, no random app closing or freezing. Very pleased with the free Duolingo app.

Very user friendly - even tracks the words you struggle with and offers extra training in those areas to reinforce your knowledge.  My only complaint is the limited number of languages on the app (maybe 5 or 6 available for English native speakers), but it works wonderfully and is GREAT for a free app.

I've found Duolingo to be an excellent tool for brushing up on my French. The app seems to assume a certain minimal level of experience or outside learning, so I don't know how appropriate it would be for someone trying to use it to learn a language from scratch, but as a practice tool, it's great. One quirk is that the tablet and phone versions basically synchronize, but are not the same (there are no pronunciation exercises in the tablet version), so if you use both, you have to keep going back and forth. It's not really a problem, it just means more practice, which is a good thing!

Headings: Too bad they don't have Japanese
Base_Reviews: Sadly, they don't have Japanese, however I've been learning Italian for fun, and the style is intuitive for learning. You can compare your data with friends and sign up through Facebook as well. All for free. Go at your own pace and learn a new language. German, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, French, and/or English, the choice is yours.
Love this, makes learning a language fun and easy. BUT the Kindle app needs upgrading so we can access our club. Currently have to do that on the cell phone. Other than that, highly recommend.
This makes learning fun. The repetition and interaction between languages really helps. I like use of sentences that are practical and useful for everyday conversation. Thanks

I have some Spanish background, but this revives what I've forgotten. I like the way you can keep going over things until you feel you have mastered them. It can be easy to test out without really knowing all the material. I also like their nagging emails that remind me to keep practicing every day. And it's free! Amazing!

Its amazing how much the little positive reinforcements make it more like a game than work. Each lesson starts easy then progresses. Doing about 10 minutes a day and it may take months to get good. But that is better than promising myself I'll work hard at it later and procrastinating.

Headings: This program is very user friendly and I'm doing fine so far
Base_Reviews: I took Spanish in high school, and remember various words--but I have acquaintances who don't speak fluent English, and I was hoping to somewhat improve my Spanish.  Hopefully just enough to have a conversation.  This program is very user friendly and I'm doing fine so far.
This app has all you need to learn a language except for the dedication. If you bring that, though, you will for sure learn whatever you want!
I like very good products.

This is probably the best free way to learn a foreign language available. I got this for my mother to learn Spanish. Now I'm several lessons into Italian. I only wish there were more languages available (such as Chinese). Hopefully more will be added. I highly recommend this app.

Headings: Great program and a fun way to learn.
Base_Reviews: I find this to be a very successful program. The lessons are short but well organized.  It is very easy and quick to review a lesson multiple times which makes retention easy. Each lesson uses a variety of learning strategies that aids learning and keeps lessons interesting. This is the easiest time I have had learning a new language. Give it a try., it is actually fun.

Headings: ... give the app 5 stars because it really is great. It's comparable to Rosetta Stone and is free
Base_Reviews: I have to give the app 5 stars because it really is great. It's comparable to Rosetta Stone and is free. In all honesty, though, I don't use the app often, it's better to just go to the website or use the app for apple.
Never gets past start screen.  Thinks four about three seconds and cycles right back to the start screen after signing in.

Headings: not intimidating and more fun than you might think
Base_Reviews: The easy progression and chances for review make for a comfortable way to learn.  I appreciate all the embedded pronunciation by a native speaker and the chances to have my pronunciation evaluated.  I bought an introductory Spanish book to help me see some of the basic grammar.  It feels like better use of my time than Candy Crush.

Excellent app. Very informative and fun. Works differently on various devices but builds vocabulary and usage on a step-by-step method. The ability to listen and speak as well as type in Spanish are a bonus. I gave recommended it to several friends.  Look forward to doing it daily.

A perfect compliment to the Beginners German class I'm taking.  You can spend  as little as 5 minutes a day, although you'll probably find yourself doing it even longer.  I recommended it to a friend for Spanish, and she also loves it.

Having been studying Spanish since high school as well as my years in college this is a great way to practice and keep the skills learned fresh and keeps brain active. Highly recommend to anyone and hope to learn Portuguese with this app in the near future once I finish the Spanish lessons provided.
Just started using it. We're traveling to Costa Rica and Spain thus year. So far, I like the user friendliness and repetition.

Headings: What a Fun Way to Learn Another Language!
Base_Reviews: This app is awesome!  It is fun and keeps my interest.  I studied Spanish, French, and Italian when I attended highschool.  I graduated in 1973.  It has been amazing to see how much I've retained.  Try Duo Lingo.  My 3 granddaughters are also studying with This app.  They love it.

I learned j' fait bon mea s it is good 5 starts great program easy interface uses both spoken and written Interfaces....I wish there was a flash card to introduce new words.... And more on masculine/ feminine subject agreements and ending....merci beaucoup ( French word I didn't know a week ago)

Headings: GREAT WAY TO VENTURE INTO A NEW LANGUAGE
Base_Reviews: I love most the encouragement it gives to move forward day after day.  I have also increased my vocabulary which reinforced throughout the drills.

I love love love this app! It is super fun, and challenges me on many levels. The app helps me translate English to German and vice versa. I also learn grammar and vocabulary in a fun way. The best part for me is using the microphone where I must put my German pronunciation to the test. There's no cheating here! Try this. You will love it. I've tried many different ways to learn German, but this one is the stickiest. Have fun!
best language app. it helped me with spanish so much. i went from failing the class to a B. its very quick to open and learn
I would like to try the voice more often but I am only able to try it when they say.

I like this app but it surprises you by putting up words you really haven't learned. I've been using some of my French to guess what the words are. It helps to go back when you feel like you don't know something. I do like that it goes back and takes you back into the categories it thinks you need to strengthen.

Headings: Best Free Language Learning App Out There
Base_Reviews: At first, learning a new language on duolingo can be difficult but once you begin to use it more often, it becomes easier to pick up the language. The app is designed to help you learn how to speak the language, recognize what is being said in the language, as well as be able to write in the language.  I especially like how at the end of learning a section, there's an extra module that tells you what you were weak in doing and provides additional exercises for you to complete to master these weaknesses.

Headings: Very easy to use, yet challenging
Base_Reviews: Trying to learn French and German at the same time.  I love the ease of the program.  So tough writing at the same time.  I am focused more on reading and listening which this program does well.  Free, which makes it great!

Headings: Best Language App I've Found So Far.
Base_Reviews: Cannot say enough good things about this app.  A fun, interactive way to learn and practice new languages.  I've learned (and retained) more Spanish with DuoLingo than I did in two years of high school and college Spanish.  And, it's useful Spanish... not the typical "at the restaurant", "at the hotel", "at the train station" sentences that I learn from many programs.  Previously learned words are incorporated into later sentences to help you learn and retain them.  Multiple languages are available... Spanish, Italian, French, German, Dutch, Danish, Irish, and others.I like that DuoLingo allows you to practice English to Spanish. Spanish to English, translation from written words and translation from sudio (occasionally difficult to recognize, but it does come with a "slow" option that phrases the sentence word by word instead of the rapid pace of a native speaker.  I would recommend that you also visit the DuoLingo.com webpage on occasion as it allows you to access sections like "Tips and Notes" that did not seem to be available from the app.Please note that DuoLingo does not actually provide "lessons."  It's more a learn as you go.  You can read the tips sections or just jump straight into practice sentences, but each sentence has a link to a "discussion" section where other Duo users (native speakers of either language) can help explain confusing grammar aspects.  I really enjoy the variety of "testing"... from translating pictures, to multiple choice, to picking the correct words out of an available group, or just typing in the translations without hints.  The web page also has the opportunity for "timed practice" so when you are reviewing lessons you feel you know well, you can set a thirty second timer and see how many translations you get right (extra seconds are added for each correct answer).Again, if I could give this app more stars I would.

Headings: Fantastic free app; not perfect, but great value and tries to keep the learning interesting and varied
Base_Reviews: For a free app, I was blown away by the value.You start by taking a sort of placement test.  After that, you're introduced to the "tree" of available subjects, in which you focus on one part of speech or related group of words: "Pronouns" or "Science" or "Past Present" or "Numbers".  These are collected in rows, and you have to finish all of the subjects in a row before you can move onto the next.Each subject consists of several "lessons", usually between 3 and 8.  You can work through the lessons one by one, and you'll be able to access definitions of words you don't know to help you learn.  Once you've completed all the lessons, you've finished the subject -- for now.  There is an alternative path to completion:  if you feel confident about the subject, you can "Test Out" by taking one roughly 20-question exam, and as long as you don't get more than 3 questions wrong, you can complete the subject that way, too.As you start filling in the tree, subjects you've already completed will open up again, so you have to keep going back to previous subjects to practice them and learn new vocabulary.  It's an effective way to keep you from "learning" something just long enough to finish the subject, but not really retaining the information.A word on the lessons themselves:  they're fairly varied.  I'm a native English speaker working on the Spanish tree, and I get questions where I have to translate a phrase or sentence from Spanish to English or from English to Spanish; spoken English where I have to type the Spanish translation and vice versa; spoken Spanish where I have to repeat it in Spanish; match-Spanish-words-to-English-definitions sets; and "choose all correct translations" multiple-choice questions.  In addition, you can access a kind of comments section for each question, where other Duolingo users post tips, comments, questions, and explanations.  You can also flag a question if you think it has an issue, and Duolingo reviews these and makes periodic updates.To up the fun factor, you earn "lingots" as you complete lessons, which you can use in the store to buy various add-ons.  You can also see your friends' progress, and a little competition can help keep you motivated!  You can also set daily email reminders and edit your goals to keep yourself on track.Overall, it's been a great way for me to refresh and improve my Spanish, which I haven't used in over ten years.

Great app! I originally downloaded this app to learn Portuguese in order to talk to my Brazilian roommate's family. After two weeks I was able to translate some song lyrics and understand parts of conversations that my roommate had with her boyfriend. I am most of the way through the Portuguese language tree and still loving it. Now I am planning to use it to learn a few other languages, as well.Some cons (possibly specific to Portuguese): The translations are not exact, so knowing some Spanish or Italian is helpful for learning the grammar rules. Also, the pronunciations are a little odd because of the computer voice; they are sometimes hard to understand and do not give you a good idea for how to say the words (e.g., "de" is pronounced like "jay" in the app, but native speakers say it more like "jee"). Listening to native speakers and doing some reading in addition to using the app would be best, but Duolingo is an EXCELLENT place to start (especially if you don't want to or cannot take a formal class).Some pros: You can report any errors in the translations and they get taken care of pretty quickly (one that I reported was cleared up within a day). Each question in the app also has a comment option where you can ask questions; there are native speakers who monitor the forums and can respond to your questions relatively quickly. There is also an online component that is really good for working on spelling. The website that is connected to your account for the app also keeps an index of all the words you have learned and has explanations about grammar rules. Finally, in the app, unlike on the web version of Duolingo, you can turn on voice recognition if you want to work on you pronunciation.Some additional notes: The sentences are created by an algorithm based on the words you have already learned. As a result, they can be a little odd (e.g., "A borboleta escreve um livro" means "The butterfly writes a book"). Some people don't like this about the app, but I think it's entertaining.Overall, I love the app! Even with some of the cons, I still give it 5/5!

Don't get me wrong - I am thankful for free apps like Duolingo to help me learn beginning spanish. But after emerging into indirect pronouns, I see why so many people I have met through the years have only mastered declarative statements and simple questions.This is how spanish really is: the beginning is a little steep, like inching your way down that incline in the swimming pool. You know there's deep water somewhere in your future but you feel safe, as you're taking it in tiny tiny increments.Then you graduate, with absolutely no preparation whatever, into indirect pronouns. You slip off that shelf in the pool and suddenly you're in deep water. Nothing makes sense. And the sad thing is that Duolingo has not prepared you at all with ANY education about it.I have been studying spanish for years and got to this point in a couple of weeks. I have had to go to external sites to get the information I need about this.Duolingo is great but they need some in-depth education about hard things like indirect pronouns, where EVERY sentence is structured ENTIRELY different than in English.

Many native languages to start from to learn many target languages! I have shared this app with friends, and they love it as well!I started with a basic high school French 1 knowledge, relearned many things I had forgotten, and have expanded my vocabulary with duo. I am even learning Irish, which very few learning apps support. I have introduced this to my 11yr old, and she is learning her second language as well.One huge plus is the various mobile platforms the app is on. I can relax at home with my tablette or be anywhere and learn on my phone. A WiFi or data connection is required for this, no offline learning option. It is 100% FREE!A few downfalls: 1 - the curriculum structure kind of befuddles me... some of the basics that are taught in classroom level 1 are last on the list here. 2 - sometimes a bit of explanation would be nice of a sentence structure or verb conjugation, or other basic notes are not explained and it is left up to the social aspect... 3 - I need to figure out how to turn off the notifications of someone else commenting in the social part, even months after I have. 4 - a few of the pronunciations need to be clearer. 5 - it doesn't always take in consideration spelling nor grammar errors.What else I would like to see added with a new update are more "game" like options during the learning process. A recent update added match the words. Absolutely brilliant. The update also included a proficiency percentage. I LOVE that! Oh, and the lingots, more options, please! I ran out of parallel lessons to spend my earned lingot crystals on, and the dressing up my owl isn't something I am interested in unless there are Halloween costumes or a Santa outfit ;)Thank you, Duolingo, for such an awesome app!

Headings: Fun and a great balance of easy + challenging!

They're exactly what I needed.I'd learned French in school, many years ago. I haven't spoken French in over 10 years, and only now and then recall it when I'm watching a French film with subtitles, or watching a Poirot mystery where it helps to know what he's muttering in French.Now, with a neighbor who speaks no English and our own planned move abroad, I need to refresh my French language skills. I'm starting from a point of recognizing a few words and phrases, but I couldn't say more than "Parlez vous..." ("Do you speak...") or "Je m'appelle..." ("My name is/I call myself...").So, I'm starting French again, not quite from scratch... but close enough.Duolingo is perfect for me. It's fun. It's light. It's free (though there may be ads on it, according to some reviewers), and I quickly learned: Pay attention during the easy lessons, because a challenge may be ahead. You'll need to remember those words and spellings.So far, the only reason I'd pay for the Plus version is because I want to support Duolingo. I love it that they provide these great lessons in basic French, free to everyone.I'm giving this an enthusiastic five stars. It's a light, fun course that feels more like play than serious study. In the app version the words are at the bottom, scrambled, with one extra word and you pick them one at a time to form a sentence. When you translate English into French you have to spell every word in both versions. The laptop version is better but the app works if you don't have a laptop with you. Duolingo is currently offered to students of Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Irish, Russian, Turkish, Polish, Hungarian and Romanian. I have worked with Duolingo's French program on and off for several years, so I can say from experience that it just keeps getting better and better. There are a few bugs, particularly in the recorded words, phrases and sentences, but there is also the capacity to give feedback when something does not sound right, or when the program is too rigid in its interpretation of "the" correct answer. There is a lively discussion group  among students, and this helps to resolve misunderstandings when they arise, as well as serve as another feedback mechanism for the developers. There are passages in the students' target language to work on translating, which range from Wikipedia entries to novels, and here crowd-sourcing really comes into play, as the finished products are being prepared for upload to the web. If working with a language you have not studied previously, I find it can be helpful to have an introductory text to the language to consult, but even that is not necessary, as there are valuable supplementary materials to be found online (e.g., at the about dot com sites for each language.)I have recently been working with the German and Italian programs, and I am enjoying them as much as I do the French. These programs can definitely become addictive, but in the best way possible, as the learner sees her/himself making progress in reading, writing and speaking the language, even one which may have been studied for years. And I haven't even mentioned the fact that this fascinating program is free! And that it moves seamlessly between the computer, smart phone and Kindle Fire!  I am waiting, along with many others, for the long-promised unveiling of the Chinese program.
