Headings: English to Spanish has lots of material and starts simply
Base_Reviews: Based on Duolingo's rating system, I am an advanced Spanish-language learner. I got this free app hoping to brush up on my very rusty Spanish skills. For this purpose, I have been very grateful for the option to test out of each of the first three levels, and then to test out of each individual subject after that. I haven't yet reached a section test that I can't pass, but I've been studying Spanish ever since elementary school. Taking the tests provides a decent review, but I'm not sure it will help my conversational Spanish much.I certainly hope that the sections I haven't reached will cover the subjunctive as well as the future and conditional tenses. I haven't seen anything in the vosotros form either, so this may not be the best way to learn the Spanish spoken in Spain.  The vocabulary is very text-book style. There don't seem to be any words specific to a certain region or even any colloquial phrases included. I haven't seen any cultural notes, either. Those are not necessary for an introduction to the language, I suppose.It looks to me like the lessons begin very simply and build very gradually, so it would be an excellent choice for a beginner. I'm not sure yet how far it will take you into the more advanced grammar.  It probably doesn't help with conversational Spanish, but a person-to-person setting is the best for that anyway.I'm glad I've had the chance to try this out. I think I'll get a taste for French or German next!

Headings: Good place to start, but more please.
Base_Reviews: I've only just started using this app, but find it pretty good thus far.Seems like it teaches you the way you would learn a language organically, through trial and error correction.  I know, through past language study, that Duolingo is, through that trial and error process, teaching you how to use formal/familiar, male/female, singular/plural, and the like, constructions.  But, it's very subtle if you didn't have a clue about theses sort of things.That leads me to one of it's shortcomings, at least for me, and the reason the app is a 4 and not a 5.  Namely, it doesn't provide a whisper of explanation of these sorts of things.  It would be a great help, for me anyway, if the little message that pops up when you make an error gave an explanation.  For example, you have (no pun intended) tu, usted, vosotros, and ustedes, which all mean you.  Now in English there's just "you," no (in order) singular informal/formal or plural informal/formal versions of you, though generally we figure that out through context.  So a simple, "you used tu (the familiar),when you should have used usted (the formal)"  would be helpful in my being able to separate the two in my head.  And, go a step further and give me an easy place to find that tells me when I should use one over the other.In the vein of more explanations, please; How about explaining (in an initial page?) what xp points are and how they are used.  Or the meter that goes around the microphone; is more better?  I tried really butchering a phrase and pretty much got the same reaction. If more is better, then I could aim for that.

I have to say that I am honestly amazed that this application. After all, it was free.However, (bet you didn't see the "however" coming) this simple program uses all the latest techniques for teaching a language. You can also download, again for free, a variety of languages.It uses what is generally referred to as an "immersive" method of teaching. Because of this it's essential that you have the ability to speak to your phone or tablet into a microphone and be able to listen to what the program says to you. But in this day and age I don't know of any phone or tablet that doesn't have a microphone and speakers.With the immersive method of teaching there is no long explanation in English (say you're learning French or Spanish). Instead you are presented with a variety of pictures such as a little boy or a little girl, and adult man or woman, dog or cat or dog and cat or any of what seems like hundreds of combinations on screen at a time. Well, you never see more than a few different blocks with different pictures inside of each of them and they contain the label in the native language you're looking to learn. A prerecorded voice will say the name of each object in the new language. Then quiz time starts.It starts by showing you individual graphics that you had just seen, for example the young girl, and you are presented with a variety of terms in the native language and have to choose the one that represents the young girl. Of course it tells you if you're right or wrong but there are no harsh buzzers that go off or anything that makes you feel stupid. After all, you are learning a new language. The process continues and you will be presented with other images and choices to identify them.But the application doesn't just give you a collection of words. After you attain a high enough score showing that you now know the words for the pictures you've been shown the program shows you how to string them together in meaningful sentences using the correct grammar. The final step, just to make sure you've grasped what it is teaching you, is to speak into the microphone of your device (in say, Spanish if that's the language you're learning) and the program either moves on or goes back a short way in the lesson if your pronunciation is off.Not only am I learning both Spanish and French using this program but just to make sure I'm not wasting my time I showed both programs to people who speak those languages natively. I also strung together a few sentences from what I've learned so far and was told that both the grammar and pronunciation are correct.As all reviews should end the question should be asked, "would I recommend this to a friend?" If you haven't gotten it from my review, the answer is an outstanding "YES"! I can honestly say I've never given ANY program such a positive, enthusiastic review. As a final side note, the method used here for teaching is the exact same method used by a program called Rosetta Stone. This tiny little app was free and still is as of the time of this review (April 9, 2014), to learn a single language using the Rosetta Stone program just at this level could easily cost you a couple hundred dollars. Thus the enthusiasm.

Headings: More than just a way to learn a language free....

This is a top quality program that will teach you to speak a major language in the style of Rosetta Stone.  It isn't exactly like Rosetta Stone and there aren't nearly as many languages, but it is free AND it is for a good cause.  The back story on Duolingo is that once you have reached a specific level of ability, you actually begin to translate books and websites.  You see, computers are really not very good at translation, but people are.  Once you are proficient enough, you will be translating actual webpages.  Your translation will be compared with hundreds of others to find what is correct (computers are good at this part).  Don't believe me?  Go to Duoling dot com and check it out. Headings: Bite-sized daily lessons mix variety and repetition
Base_Reviews: I studied French in high school and college years ago, and I've picked up a bit of Spanish here and there, and by reading some of the Bible in Spanish. I decided to pick up some German with Duolingo because I have a nephew who studied that. Well, that started out so well I decided to brush up my French and see what I could do with Spanish. Probably not a good idea to work on three languages at once, but I'm enjoying it and making progress. I was so rusty on French my attempt to test out of the Basics failed (just barely), but it's nice to know the option is there if you don't want to review from the beginning. Repetition is an important part of learning any language, but it can get boring. This program solves the problem by mixing up the styles of questions. It starts out very easy - some of the questions are as easy as tapping the picture of the word given in your native language with the target language below it. On some questions, you can tap the given word and see its translation, so you don't have to guess even if it is a new word (but guessing can be fun and doesn't "hurt" much!). Pay attention to the little words that go with them, though! In English (which is hard to learn in other ways) we just have "the" for everything, but in French and Spanish you have variations to match the gender and number of the objects (German has three singular forms, one being neuter, I guess). How do you know if an object takes a masculine (le or el) or feminine (la)? Practice, practice, practice! Take your time and think and memorize, and write words and combinations down. And Duolingo does let you go back and review skill sets. The instant feedback is much more enjoyable than doing written homework, but the German is making me want to get a textbook and do some extra studying! Some questions let you translate phrases or sentences by selecting from a choice of words, others let you listen to spoken words, phrases, or sentences and then select the words you hear. More challenging questions require you to type in the translation or words from memory. It even has voice recognition so some questions require you to repeat things in the target language. If it doesn't recognize what you say, it doesn't count it against you (lots of things can go wrong with voice recognition, such as background noises). If you can't get away from the noise or otherwise can't or don't want to use your microphone, you can turn off that feature and it will only give you the other kinds of questions. I've noticed that it also gives some leeway for typographical errors, although sometimes it's still counted typos as wrong and other times I've just been wrong but it was counted as a typo. It generally gets it right and the two kinds of errors balance out. I've typed in a translation when the task was to type out what was spoken in the foreign language, and it gave me a do-over. But watch out, if you make a mistake in your own language, it will count that wrong, too! English speakers had better know how to properly use "to," "too," and "two," for example. Or maybe using DuoLingo will help you with that, too! Daily e-mail reminders (which can be turned off) help you to stick to it.[ADDED LATER] Well, I'm up to Level 5 in all three languages, and I'm definitely feeling the pinch of trying to make it QuadLingo. As I fail lessons, though, previous skills re-open to show where I need to go back and practice more, which is a good thing. It's exciting to be learning these languages, and I'm thinking I might dig through my collection of language texts to add to and aid my DuoLingo studies, since I've gone and set myself a three-pronged challenge. I wish I'd thought of taking notes earlier (I just added that bit with this edit); I'm sure that would be enough to make studying one language a cinch with DuoLingo.

I've been using this app on my 7" Kindle Fire HD and my HTC One SV for approximately a week... maybe a week and a half now, and I absolutely love it!I'm using it to learn German... not sure what other language options there are, although I know Spanish and French are in there. So far I am hugely impressed. The app uses a combination of written, spoken, and visual cues/questions... so one question may ask me to translate a sentence from German to English, the next question might be to translate something from English to German, and the question after that may be to speak a sentence in German or to write a sentence in German that the app speaks (the app's voice is not great, but definitely serviceable)... reinforced occasionally by visual cues such as labeled pictures (i.e. a picture of a dude labeled "der Mann"... you get the idea after a bit).The teaching method works, I have to say... and this from a guy who always considered himself critically handicapped when it came to learning new languages.  Granted, I'm early into the program, but I am retaining a large part of each lesson, which is honestly more than I can say for my experience with Rosetta Stone.There are two cons that I've noted: First, and this may have been an individual problem, the app wouldn't let me sign in with either Google+ or Facebook... it has buttons for doing that, but they didn't work... so I had to go old-school and actually create a separate account.  Minor glitch, but still worth noting.  The second con is that in the course of the lessons, I haven't yet encountered a definitive explanation of certain rules of grammar, i.e. when to use one form or another of a verb. On one hand this is vaguely annoying, as I end up with wrong answers without being entirely certain why they're wrong; on the other hand, however, I suspect that this is actually increasing the effectiveness of the program, as this makes me really think about each word before I use it, and when I'm wrong, I really study WHY I was wrong, which ultimately increases retention of the language. So kudos for effectiveness, even if it is a bit annoying.Overall... freaking awesome.  Get this app.  I can't believe it's free, honestly, but as long as it is, get it!

Headings: Such a fun way to learn or reinforce a new language.
Base_Reviews: My grandson introduced this system to me as an aid in augmenting my Rosetta Stone and Pimsleur Italian lessons and it helps a lot.  Rosetta Stone is a multi-pronged method that keeps you at the computer and can frustrate you if you don't pay a lot of attention to the proper spelling of the new language.  I am not interested in writing Italian and it is pretty easy to figure out close enough to read because it is such a phonic language but many words are blended and therefore difficult to separate for spelling purposes.  Pimsleur is all audio and I can listen to it in my car or at home so it gives me more flexibility from that standpoint.  Duolingo offers aids that act as reminders to help reinforce your learning and gives the explanations that are missing in Pimsleur.  Maybe it is me, but I find it helpful if I can see the conjugations of verbs to make those connections.  This also has a fun aspect to it so I find I resort to it when I have a few minutes here and there to devote.  Both Rosetta Stone and Pimsleur require a more disciplined approach that needs you to set time aside each day for language learning and reinforcement.  Best of all, it is FREE....how can you go wrong!

There is a ton to learn and lessons are divided into very bite size segments.I know that the app tries to immerse you into the language and that is great. My complaint is that it is completely guess and check. Some questions are easy to decipher while on others I had to blindly guess or not put an answer. There is no instruction, not even basic grammar hints. You figure it out on your own. Like I said, this approach is good...to a certain extent. When things that "should" work don't, it can be frustrating. There is an option to comment on questions and looking through previous questions you can usually figure out where you went wrong. If your goal is to learn a language, this app shouldn't be used as your main source.

Headings: Better than my paid subscription to a language site
Base_Reviews: Really does help you learn a language with practice. It quizzes you to verify your understanding. It mostly asks you to select an answer without actually teaching you first -- so you guess a lot in the beginning. But that is not a bad thing. The process is engaging and ultimately inspires you to teach yourself without a physical teacher present. There are User Discussions associated with lessons, but I found myself doing additional Internet searches on certain words and phrases. The extra research significantly enhanced my understanding and helped me remember better.Also, there's a lot of fun to be had here. It offers multiple ways to learn (listening, speaking, writing and translating) which all serve to help you remember your new language. Plus, there is the "gaming" element that allows you to achieve points called "lingots" that can be traded for special learning modules. I gave this app 4 stars instead of 5 because it sometimes gave me "credit" for speaking the correct words when I had actually flubbed up the language. But for the most part, it was spot on!I actually have a paid subscription to a language learning site, but I find myself returning most often to this app.

Headings: A great way to begin learning a new language
Base_Reviews: I am at the very beginning of my journey to learn French, and this free app has made it fun and enjoyable for me.  This app starts you off by jumping in with both feet. No instructions really, just trial and error right away and I was pleasantly surprised at how effective it was.  If you miss a phrase, a little word balloon will open up showing you the correction. The best part about the correction balloon is the link to a chat page where other people have already asked questions and the incredibly informative responses. I've learned a great deal about the grammar and foundation of the language just from reading these back and forth questions and answers.  You are encouraged to participate daily which isn't a problem for me as I look forward to it. As you progress you earn Lingots (I think that's what they're called)  which you can use to purchase little fun add-ons for the app. What I am very happy with is how much content they give you. For French I can see the lessons go on for quite a while, providing more and more detail about the language. I've tried listening to French audio files and have even tried a free preview of Rosetta stone, but nothing I've tried before has been as interesting and informative as the Duolingo app. Highly recommended and I hope you enjoy!

Headings: Intuitive, Easy to Use, Great Between Devices
Base_Reviews: This app is fantastic! I've been using it for weeks now to learn Spanish. The controls are intuitive and I find it easy to learn a second language. I use this app on my laptop, my Kindle Fire, and my Android phone, and the app is great for that. It always keeps up on my progress, and I've had no issues at all. It's a great way to learn another language, and the best part is that it's 100% free. However, the one tiny issue that I have with this app is that you need to have speakers. This is fine when you're working on it at home, but in public places; not so much. It plays a word/phrase in whatever language you're learning, and you are supposed to type that word/phrase out. It's a bit awkward when one is in a quiet place (think waiting room at the doctor's office). You have to turn the volume way down and hold it up to your ear, or just wear headphones. This isn't a major issue, and all in all, I think that Duolingo is a fantastic app for people of all ages to learn an important life skill of being bilingual.

Headings: Good, if you already know the basics
Base_Reviews: I love this app. I use it to maintain and strengthen my Spanish skills; however, I do not find it very useful for learning entirely new languages. Instead of teaching rules and patterns, such as stem verbs, conjugations, etc., it requires the learner to memorize practically every aspect of the language down to the smallest details. In essence, there's no explanation of why. Why does the third person plural use this verb ending? Why do I use this past tense instead of that one (since in Spanish, there are two imperfect past tenses)? As a student of languages and their historical progression, I have found it crucial to teach languages according to rules, patterns, and conjugational conventions. This app, however, seems to overlook this extremely helpful principle. I had hoped to use Duolingo to continue learning German and begin learning Italian, but I will instead have to use a textbook to first learn all the necessary grammar rules and then use the app to practice and increase my vocabulary. Overall, it is a fairly solid aid to self-education.

Headings: An excellent resource and it really is 100% free
Base_Reviews: This is a great way to brush up on language skills.  I took Spanish in high school but made it my New Year's resolution to get back into it.  I love that this is totally free.  It encourages you to log in every day to practice the skills you've learned and add new ones.  It keeps track of your progress and can compare to friends who are also using the program.  It has a bunch of languages including Spanish, French, German and Italian and several others in the works like Turkish, Vietnamese and Polish.Each "lesson" incorporates translating from English, translating to English, speaking and listening exercises.  You can turn off the speaking and learning exercises.  I do. I find that it doesn't recognize my voice very well. I think part of that is my pronunciation and part of it is the voice recognition.Duolingo has both a mobile and online computer-based components.  You can use either one or both (all for free).  I like the computer version better.  It's easier to type on a real keyboard.  The PC version gives you more practice when you make an error, but the mobile version gives three chances before you fail the lesson and have to start over. I also like that the PC version has a translation mode and gives you an estimate of how much you can understand of the "real" language.There is a lot of pattern recognition and memorization involved.  There are some little tidbits in the lessons, but some things are very much missing.  I'm still trying to sort out "por" and "para" and trying to understand the personal "a."  (Feel free to comment with some hints).  Fortunately there are other web resources to back up this learning.I've almost finished the Spanish lessons.  I will probably work on Italian (while practicing Spanish) next.  It will be interesting to see if it's as helpful when I try a language that i have had no previous exposure to.

Headings: The VERY BEST language learning app!
Base_Reviews: I have had two years of French in school and used virtually every language program available. Here are my critiques:Rosetta Stone...didn't like that because it didn't present the material in a way that appealed to me or that stuck with me. Also, it frustrated me as it seemed disorganized and a backwards approach. Plus it's expensive. At least $400  for entire program. Pimsleur: it is pretty good actually. The one drawback to Pimsleur is that I sometimes can't understand exactly what they are saying, even after having two years of the language under my belt,  therefore, you don't get the concept of how the language is organized. Plus it is expensive. The pro to it though is that you can listen to the audio in your car or while cleaning house or jogging.FrenchPod: pros: you can download audio files to listen to wherever you are. The speakers have  a natural French dialog and then go over it bit by bit and explain the various uses of the words. You can alsodownload workbook pages to refer to.Cons: There us an extremely limited list of lessons, all of which are around 6 sentences to dissect. Also, there is no practice, either speaking or writing.Textbooks: Difficult. Boring.DuoLingo: pros:  you get to hear the audio spoken at a natural speed. Then you can slow it down so you can pick up on each word as it is enunciated. You are immersed in the language by having to type out, which forces you to remember placement of nouns and verbs etc.  It is formatted sort of like a game, so it doesn't feel much like work, and it is actually quite addictive. It's totally FREE! No ads either.Cons: it can get frustrating if you get an answer wrong because you miss points, so like with any "game," you might get frustrated if you're that serious about game points.I have learned FAR more with this app in 6  months than I EVER learned in all my previous years using other methods! It's fun and free and best of all...it works!!

Headings: No more reading recipes. Just watch the video!! I LOVE IT!!
Base_Reviews: I accidentally bumped into Food Network Kitchen 2 weeks ago (Jan. 2021) and it has CHANGED MY LIFE like nothing else in the kitchen has. I was down to Wawas gas station ready-to-go sandwich meals and could retire on what I've bought in Marie Callendar's Chicken Pot Pie boxes.My problem(s)? Which there are a GREAT many in the kitchen: I don't like reading recipes. I don't like listing out the ubiquitous "weekly shopping list" of necessary ingredients nor foraging the Walmart shelves figuring out where one gets the items. (Pro tip: Do you know where molasses is kept in the stores? Me neither.)SOMETHING had to give when I realized how upset I got when my local sandwich bar at the Wawas gas station was closed due to this pest called "Covid." I mean .. REALLY!!!I've had two large cookbooks I've owned for 5 years - still in their original saran wrap.  I could get full price for what they are worth today - mint condition. And they have big pictures in them - I think they do. Not sure. Never opened them. But much like people who join a gym with the intention to workout, the concept of cooking is "Nice."Forward 53 years (which I am today) and I have 2 siblings who do cook. But alas they live too far away for me to drop in for dinner. We all began sharing our recipes during Covid - to show off what we were doing in quarantine. They showed off their couscous on a bed of lettuce with fresh squash ... I showed off my latest Wawas $2 discount shortie sandwich - courtesy of the free gas app I had just joined.They showed off their fresh steamed asparagus with honey salmon while I showed off my grilled cheese sandwich with - might I add - a touch of melted butter (This was of course after I burned the first batch of bread by leaving it on high too long under the broiler).As you can imagine this gets embarrassing - me being the oldest sibling and all. My reputation was quickly falling to not relevant. And I'm a weight lifter to boot. It didn't help that my ex was a professional chef and I never needed to cook a thing. But this had to change.I went online researching recipe apps. I figured maybe I could at least READ a recipe on line. I looked up Betty Crocker (who, btw, is NOT a real person. Look it up if you don't believe me.). And I was bored with what I saw. More recipe reading. So I skimmed over the number of people who purchased the  various food apps - as I have more apps than I can count.I saw FNK - THOUSANDS of people!! I went .. "Hey, is that THE Food Network Channel?" I mean.. the BIG kahuna?WELL YES IT WAS!!!! Then I immediately felt dejected because I ain't no cook and I know the sandwich employees at Wawas by name. But curiosity got the best of me. I LOOKED. I OPENED the FNK APP. I saw my FAVORITE personality.. REE. I own her stuff from Walmart - all of it nearly (including the pie slicer!).I saw the videos. They were short. To the point (around 3 minutes) ... they told you the order of ingredients in the video. The FNK app created my grocery list FOR ME. I could easily add and remove items from the list. I could add my own custom items onto the list - food related or not. (Ya know - Qtips). t took me 15 minutes to figure out the app - it was EASY!!!!  ! can even call ahead now and have the ingredients all ready for me to pick up at my store if I don't want to do it myself. Free curbside service!I went HOLY COW ... KERI CAN COOK!!!!!Fast forward ONE week of owning this app ... and I have cooked meals that I can actually show off to my siblings (see attached photos - all made January 2021 in 1 weeks time. That easy! I never read a single recipe. I just follow the video. This FNK app is the bomb!!!!Best money I've ever spent on an app. And my goal is to no longer know the sandwich people at Wawas by name - not unless it's just to say, "Hi."

Let me start by saying that I have the iOS version, which is installed on both my iPhone and iPad.  It was as five-star app for a while, until iOS 7 was released.  I think they released one update that made it compatible with 7, but it came with an annoying bug - it makes you log in EVERY SINGLE TIME you want to access your recipe box, even though I had the "keep me logged in" thing checked off.  Very annoying.  I let the app developers know about this, they say they are aware of it, and it will be fixed in the next update.  This was months ago, I am still waiting for that update.When I saw that the Kindle Fire version was free (I paid $1.99 for the iOS version), I decided to give it a try and see if I can use it and avoid the log in issue.  That part worked.  What DOESN'T work is inside the recipe box itself.  When I tap on one recipe, it takes me to a completely different recipe.  It's not like I tapped the one next to it by mistake; it takes me to recipes that aren't even next to the one I tapped on. Headings: Good product but I expect more from the Food Network
Base_Reviews: First, let me say that this is a good product, not great. It marginally improves upon the foodnetwork.com experience on a tablet. It does the basics of allowing you to search for recipes on foodnetwork.com by show as well as save those recipes into a recipe box that are linked to the website. However, the recipe box does not allow you to create folders, only store in folders you create on the website so a little less functionality than the website.A nice (but incomplete) feature allows you to create shopping lists from recipes. However the app does not combine ingredients from multiple recipes so you have a short, concise list. It should also allow you to scale recipes based on the number of servings you would like to make.Likely the biggest complaint is that it has even less video than the website (i.e., no video at all from what I found...) Given that this application is published by the Food NETWORK you would think that they would have lots of video to include.  Also, when shows have multiple recipes that are pared together, there are no links from one recipe to another meaning you have to find it on your own.The app itself runs ok. It did crash once on my Galaxy Note 10. In short, I'd wait for them to put in a serious upgrade until paying the $1.99...

Headings: From Recipe to Grocery List without Over-Buying
Base_Reviews: You can use the grocery list as a running list of all one has in the house-what is crossed off is what you already have or don't need.  This is saving us from over - buying.  What is not to love about an app that scans recipes on web pages for you, saves them AND adds a recipe's ingredients to your grocery list?  This is not all - the app will sync your grocery list 2 your phone so you can do meal planning in the kitchen on a tablet then as you walk into the store, have your grocery list synced on your phone and you are ready to shop!

Love this app! It is so easy to use. Helps me stay organized and easily find a recipe with tags. Being able to clip a recipe I see on the internet and add it to my collections with pictures is wonderful!

I love this app!  It's perfect to store all of my recipes in one place.  It's such a chore to go from one website, blog, online recipe file to find the recipe you want.  Sadly I came across some of my old 'saves' to find the recipe has been deleted or the blog is gone.  This app keeps those recipes in ONE place along with my collection of pins from Pinterest.com. No more worries of loosing the recipes.A great feature of this app is that you can access the recipes offline.  This helps when you are at the grocery store to pick up the ingredients you need and there is no wi-fi.The larger Pictures and Grid View are a nice improvement.  I like having pictures for my recipes and being able to add pictures is a bonus.The added tag feature makes it even easier to find specific recipes without having to scroll through the hundreds of recipes I've saved.  (I'm actually over a thousand now:))The ONLY reason I didn't give it 5 Stars is that I can't use this app on my desktop or laptop (and currently not my Blackberry.  The app is only for Android devices).  I'd like to be able to add/edit recipes from there as I've been saving them in my bookmarks lists.  I ultimately emailed the recipes links to my email account and clicked the links from my kindle. I do understand from the Chef Tap website that this along with a cloud feature are two of the things they are working on.  Good.  I'll give you the fifth star when it happens :)  It'll be nice to share one recipe file across devices.  I've been due for a phone upgrade for awhile but I'd put it off waiting for the latest to come out.  The latest features on the new phones are great but since using Chef Tap along with a few other great apps from the Amazon App store I decided to upgrade to an Android phone instead of upgrading my Blackberry (kinda a tough thing since I've had a Blackberry for 10 years at least.)To save the backup file to my desktop I had to go through Dropbox because the app said the file was too big to send via email. This isn't really difficult so I don't count it against them.  I now use Dropbox for other things like sending my personal videos, pictures and other downloads to my desktop when I need more room :)  If you don't have a Dropbox account or don't want one you can manually save by connecting your device to your computer and saving the file that way.  The Faq page on Chef Tap has details.I recently saw from their FAQ page a way to transfer files from .txt .  This is an awesome idea I haven't yet tried.  But I will because I want to add my grandmother's recipe file.  Those are actually in a REAL recipe box on REAL recipe cards.  But that will be a project for another day.The Chef Tap FAQ page and Facebook page have lots of answers to help as well as being user friendly.  A really nice change from an app creating team:) They plan on adding new features and keep you up to date in a newsletter and on their facebook page and blog.  Looking forward to having the shopping list feature.Like I said earlier it's a GREAT app!  I don't mind the ads and usually don't but will pay for the ad-free just because the app itself is worth the money.

Headings: Love but I could madly love...
Base_Reviews: I love Chef Tap App.  Pure and simple best app for recipes I have found.  And I have tried at least three others but I always go back to the Tap!  I would madly love with three changes or added features. 1) I wish the app could generate a shopping list from choosen recipes.  2) I wish there were subset tags.  For instance, Vegetables but within Vegetables could add corn and beans, etc. And 3) in a perfect world I wish I could share a recipe with a friend in a recipe template.  When I share now the email is one big text.  I wish what I sent them was in "recipe card" format.  In the most perfect world it would be in a template I could customize with my name and  cutesy photo!  I brag about how wonderful the app is I think if when I shared a recipe it was in a nifty format more folks would want.  I know a lot of old ladies who do not easily change!I use Chef Tap with my Kindle and I did upgrade and am happy I did!Easily imports from most sources, especially easy with Pinterest on the Kindle.

This is my absolute favorite app. I love how easy it is to add online recipes by sharing them to chef tap. I also love how easy it is to search for recipes or ingredients. The only thing I wish it could also do is allow for uploading  or scanning recipes like Evernote does. Then it would be the perfect recipe app.

Fantastic customer service!  Unfortunately to find out if they had what I was looking for - I had to buy a year's subscription - only to find out that 1.  I had to update the software (which they updated on Aug. 29th, 2017) mind you I bought it on October 4th, 2017 and that the meal planner I was looking for had not been implemented.  Oh well.  It looks like a great app!  Just not for me at this time..

Headings: Great way to save online reipes
Base_Reviews: This s a great way to save online online recipes to access any time, even when offline. Its not perfect, I wish I could save personal recipes more easily. However, for most of my Ned's it works pretty well. I did pay for the upgrade so I can store more recipes and sync more frequently. I also wish I could clip re ipes on my pc or laptop without sending the file to another device which is why I gave 4 stars instead of 5.
I use it twice a week. Great for planning weekly meals as well.

Headings: I use this ap a lot!
Base_Reviews: I am impressed with this ap.  It is so easy to download a new recipe and then go to it in chef tap and categorize it.  The make feature really came in handy during the holidays.  It was nice to just access my list and keep on track with my baking and the meal menus.  This ap is accessible from your pc as well which makes it a little easier to add a favorite recipe of your own.  I use this ap almost daily to either browse new recipes, download new recipes, or access my already added recipes.  It is easy to scroll through the ingredient list or the instructions to keep on track with where you are at in the preparation of your dish.  Love it!

It was a joke.. It had to be.  my bad for buying it. What was I thinking...probably not thinking. I think it was meant to be a white elephant gag for a present that gets recycled from person to person.

I deleted all my other recipe apps after got this one.  It does it all!!!!  I can download recipes (complete with pics) from any website, sync my recipes across all devices and share them with friends and family.  It is great!!!

and I especially like to read recipes. I have had magazine pages and computer printed recipes piled up for years. This app is like someone put all of my recipes together in one place. Whether it's on another app or on the internet, I can move it to Chef Tap. I can even edit it if something isn't in the right order. I also like to read the reviews and edit based on what other people have or haven't tried. I only gave it 4 stars, but it should be 4 1/2. Until recently I couldn't figure out how to get recipes from the internet, only other apps. There was an upgrade not long ago and there was a video showing how to do it. Really like this app.

This is such a handy app!  I got it right before Thanksgiving (a bit over a month ago) and I just love it-- took me a little bit to figure out what was going on and how to use it, but after I did, I LOVED being able to save all my internet recipes in one place.  Also, for some reason, I am just incapable of following recipes exactly-- I'm always throwing in something extra, or leaving something out that I don't enjoy-- and you can edit the recipes to include these alterations.  Saving recipes is a snap and if I make one and decide it's a dud-- zap, it's deleted.  This is just great!  (I have a Kindle HD)

I use this app everyday. This is my 'favorites' recipe book. Whenever I . try a new recipe and it's a keeper...it goes into Chef Tap. I used to make my own 'favorites' recipe book in a binder with clear sheets to protect the paper recipes but now Chef Tap makes things simple and efficient.Now I just need to figure out how to copy and paste from my purchased kindle recipe books...not sure why this feature is not allowed but it's frustrating for adding to Chef Tap.Thank you Chef Tap! Their customer service is also top notch. I had trouble switching to their Pro when it came out and they helped get it taken care of right away!

Headings: Really Enjoyâ€”Although All â€œClippedâ€� RECIPES MUST BE CHECKED FOR ACCURACY
Base_Reviews: I really like this APP.  Very addictive.  A couple of weeks after I loaded the free version, I ordered the premium packageâ€”to be honest, I think they wore me down with all their requests to order the premium package.Admittedly, there were many times within the first 2 weeks that I almost deleted this APP.  I would get very frustrated because I found it difficult to use.  It seemed that I could never find the specific instructions I needed.  Iâ€™m not very computer literate.  I would finally figure it out and see how simple the procedure was.  A couple of procedures I did not find for months, and then only by accident.  Made me crazy when I discovered how simple the procedures were; showed me how little basic computer knowledge I have.One other problem I find is that frequently Ingredients and/or Directions will be missing or mixed in under the wrong category (i.e., Ingredients mixed in with Directions, or vice versa). I had never heard of this diet before (also suppose to be helpful for autistic children).  So I was surprised when this APP pulled up so many great recipes and websites.I would consider this one of the best purchases I made this last year.  Certainly one of the most enjoyable and useful.
Easy to use and very complete, with everything from importing and sorting recipes, tracking make lists and shopping lists.

Love this app. I have the premium and I have over a thousand recipes saved. It lets me categorize them so they are easy to find. I clip most of my recipes and for the most part it works wonderfully.  I also am on my third tablet and I love that it is easy to transfer your account to the new device. I definitely recommend this app.

Headings: Love it, but a couple requests
Base_Reviews: We have used this app for years and swear by it!  We even upgraded to the premium addition once we hit 1,000 recipes. The developers have made several great and timely updates, so I hope it isn't greedy to ask for a couple more?!?!First, a shopping list would be ideal. We plan our weekly meals in ChefTap, but then have to transfer the ingredients into another app in order to go shopping. Kind of annoying. Something simple like a check box next to each ingredient to add it to a shopping list and then the ability to sort your final list would be killer!Lastly, an Apple version of the app. I know this is an investment, but many folks have multiple devices and not being able to access the app from wherever you are limits its useability.Keep up the great work folks!!!

I've been using this app for a long time and really love it.  Having it on my phone as well as my tablet means I can use it anywhere.  Probably the best feature is that you can scale recipes up or down. Really useful!
A true virtual cookbook that works seamlessly across multiple devices with various operating systems & browsers! Full functionality for cooking and shopping. We use it daily and love It!

I love Chef Tap! It is so easy to import recipes from the web, including a picture, and once imported, it is easy to make changes to title, ingredients, and steps, so I can record my personal changes at will. I also really like how it keeps my Kindle from going to sleep while using the program when cooking. The step-by-step feature that keeps the list of ingredients visible is an added bonus. I used to use Big Oven on my laptop, but Chef Tap is so much more user friendly! As a cook who likes trying new recipes but wants to be able to track and recreate them, this is more than perfect. It is also very easy to type in those few old family favorites that don't exist online.

After studying several recipe apps, I settled on this one. It's been all I hoped for-- easy to use,  easy to navigate. It's super easy to import recipes from any site I've tried. The recipes come  through needing few adjustments, if any. If adjustments are necessary, they're very simple to make.  I do wish you got to store more than 25 free recipes, but to be fair, I haven't reached the limit yet. I've also been being conservative with the recipes I'm importing. But when I reach the limit, I like this app enough I'll probably pay for the subscription.

Central is a terrific app for managing recipes you enter by hand or find online.  Search features help you locate by keyword or ingredients.  Sometimes there are minor operational glitches, so not quite five star but developers quickly address any problems that users report.

Headings: I use this all the time.
Base_Reviews: I have used this for years and love it. Simple to use and very handy.  They also have frequent updates to address problematic web sites.

I started using this app but noticed my recipe photos were not syncing between devices.  I contacted the provider about the sync issue and the next update corrected the problem.  You have to find some of the free version limitations i.e. 100 recipes, weekly sync, no web import of recipe on PC but otherwise it works very well.  I have imported recipes from web sites without problems and have entered my own as well.  If there was a one time charge for premium (currently annual fee) I might pop for it.

I've been using Chef Tap for about a year now to get and store recipes. I love that it now stores to the cloud! This is the best and easiest recipe ever and I decided to finally upgrade about a month ago and pay the annual membership for the pro version to get unlimited syncing to the cloud and unlimited recipes. Best thing I ever did for about $16/year...it's definitely worth it. That's cheaper than my Netflix account per year! I definitely recommend getting this if you want a place to store your recipes.  Works great on my Kindle Fire HD!

Headings: THE best recipe clipper by far!!!
Base_Reviews: This is by far THE best recipe app out there. I have tried and uninstalled many apps to capture recipes from online. Not one of them, until this one has done so with a usable result. The closest I have seen is Pocket, which I still like very much for other articles, but not for recipes. With that one I would usually end up using the web view which takes away the recipe card aspect of the app.Mindframe Design has done a wonderful job with ChefTap. I can clip my grain free and raw recipes from the web, pick the picture I want to use, edit or change an ingredient or instruction effortlessly, change the recipe title and more. If anything is missing, it is easy to retrieve missing text and fix it, but this has only happened twice out of 78 recipes that I now have in the app.I love the ability to tag and then search, or choose a tag to see the recipes with that tag and also mark recipes as favorites.I also like the way you can mark the ones you want to make and just pull those recipes up.I use this app on my Fire Phone and on my Samsung Galaxy Tablet.I have not noticed anything that I don't like about this app yet.

Headings: The best recipe storage app out there!
Base_Reviews: I decided to try this app and was so impressed that I bought an annual subscription before I reached the storage limit.  I store apps clipped from the internet, from digital magazines, digital cook books and even enter my own original recipes.  I'm amazed at how accurate the imported recipes are.  The developers have done a really fantastic job with this app.
I love this app! You can download it inGoogle play and iTunes as well!To be able to have over 100 recipes,There is a subscription. But if you donâ€™tneed over 100, itâ€™s free!
Does what it says it will do. What's not to like?

....first of all it is amazimg how effortlessly (for the most part) receipes import into the program...and editing is a breeze....i love how i can change the picture and delete what i dont need in a receipe...folders are awesome, being able to create own and putting a receipe in multiple folders...the program dropbox has been a blessing for backing up my receipes...i have had to reformat my tablet on several occassions and cheftap is always there ready to import them again...i never have to print a receipe again and if i do not like it...i simply delete...no paper waste...thanks cheftap
I have this app on my Kindle. My only issue is that I can't update.

I love Chef Tap. It makes storing all my recipes in one place super easy.The import option from various websites is AMAZING and a wonderful time saver. The only reason I didn't give this app 5 stars is because of their lack of a cloud storage option. I have Chef Tap on my cell phone also but do not have access to all the recipes I have stored on my kindle. And when I upgraded to a Kindle Fire HD I had to go through quite a few easy, but annoying, steps to restore the recipes I had saved on my original Kindle. Altogether, though, it's a fantastic app and one I would've gladly paid for!

I have had Chef Tap for about 2 months now and like it better every day.  The upgrade was slightly hard to find for my Kindle Fire (have to look in the app store side bar for "updates") but the update was free and the app is even better now.  The new menus make categorization and navigation so much easier.  I have imported many recipes from the internet (The Pioneer Woman is a favorite) and it sure beats printing and keeping up with the recipe.  You can organize each recipe by as many tags as you want and create your own categories.  This is a plus for me because I can quickly find what I'm looking for.  I would say this is the most useful app on my Kindle Fire HD!

I am loving this app on my Kindle Fire so far! I bought my Kindle on Prime Day for $30 to exclusively use for recipes in the kitchen. I downloaded this app and splurged on the Pro membership ($20/year). Although I'm not crazy about the membership price, I am really liking the versatility of this app. So easy to input recipes -- and I loved that I could manually type in my personal recipes on the website and sync them to the app on my Kindle. I'm excited about using this in the future -- I especially love the "look" of the recipes when you pull them up (ingredients at the top, steps at the bottom). No more scrolling through Pinterest (HATE THAT!) or looking through blogs to find the real recipe.

Headings: I used to love this app, too...
Base_Reviews: Now that I have so many recipes in this app, suddenly I am being forced to either sign up for an account or stop importing recipes, period .... which is all his app does. Also, there have been insane amounts of updates in the past month. I will go back to e-mailing myself recipes or printing them out before I am forced to sign up for anything. I LOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOVE this  app!  I don't have a Kindle, just a cheap run of the mill android tablet and this app works well on it.  It is simple to use (most of the time, some websites have weird configurations),  but most of the time it's great.  The only thing lacking imo is the ability to categorize the recipes,  such as  creating folders for breads,  desserts,  beverages etc.  Worth paying for with that option added. Maybe sometime soon?  Anyway,  great job guys.  My now favorite go to cookbook  app.
Uninstalled...(the last update took away features that you have to go pro now to use...ðŸ˜ ).  I found another app that works much better...
I have had the Pro version for several years. Definitely worth the money! This app has never let me down.

I had to update my glowing review of this app because of the updates and changes they have made.  It is no longer user-friendly.  The ads, which were noticeable before, but small, are now annoying and often blocking area I want to read or edit. I absolutely love this app.  I have never had an app device before so I am new to this.  Because of frequent updates I lost my recipes numerous times.  They now have a subscription fee where you pay for a monthly or yearly subscription that expires, it is not cheap.  I would prefer to buy the app outright, that is not an option.I have since deleted this app from my device and found a different one.  I was SO, SO sad to let this one go.  It was my most used and favorite app on my Fire.Former review:  I cook differently than a lot of people focusing on healthy, fresh foods without the use of canned goods or processed foods.  These types of recipes are difficult to find in standard cookbooks and cooking sites.  But with Chef Tap I can read my favorite healthy cooking blog and instantly transport the recipe into Chef Tap, it is easy, painless and fast.  Editing is easy as there is an option to view the whole blog post and import any text that didn't make it into the recipe.You create your own tags and then you can add those tags to any recipe.  So I have my breakfast tag, beverage, salad, etc.  The recipes are searchable by its tag, but also by a title word.You can also add your own personal notes to any recipe which is a great way to make note of changes you made or even when it was prepared.I do have some wishes for the program:  I wish it did weekly menu planning including breakfasts.  I would also appreciate a generated shopping list.  And more than any other function I wish it could sync with a computer version and even a phone version.  I would LOVE this program on my browser.  Then I could STORE the recipes on my computer, but then access them from the Fire when I am in the kitchen.One of my biggest complaints is that the back-ups take a long time once you have several recipes in the program.  Additionally, the back-up runs automatically when you open the program so you can not access your recipes until it is finished backing up.  I would rather the back-up function operated in the background or even when the program isn't being used.  You can amend how you want the back-ups done and how frequently, which is helpful.My other complaint is that when you are making edits in your recipe you can't stay in an edit mode and have to click your options and start over for each step you edit.Overall it is the best recipe import program I have used including my experience with computer versions.

Headings: The couple that developed this app are super. Wish I could meet them in person
Base_Reviews: Use this app to put recipes on my tablet. Can't imagine not having it.  The couple that developed this app are super.  Wish I could meet them in person. Great support if you need it.

Love the program. Got it when you could store 100 recipes for free. What I don't like and won't do is pay a monthly fee to use it. Recipes can be saved to note pad and added to my Accuchef program I purchased for 20.00 years ago.

Headings: This app is perfect for storing my recipes
Base_Reviews: This app is perfect for storing my recipes. It syncs to an external website if you create an account so you don't lose any recipes in a phone crash. You can easily import recipes from a website link which is super convenient. I only wish you could store pictures of recipes for ease of uploading existing recipes. Overall, it's the best app I've found for storing my recipes!!

Headings: Perfect to create my own cookbook
Base_Reviews: I have been using this app since August 2012.  The creators of this app are so responsive to feedback.  If you have any tech troubles with any imported recipe, you can send them that link and they will look at it to see if they can solve it.I really love that I can import any recipe on the web and have it stored on my Kindle Fire.  If I am at the store, I can open Chef Tap and all my instructions/ingredients are there.This is very user friendly and worth a 5 star rating.  I'd give it 10 if I could.

I like this app. it's the only one I have found that allows me to import , tweek as I need, as well as manually put in my family favorites. Was a bit disappointed that I had to upgrade to pro after I had reached a certain number of imports, I would say let each customer back up themselves so the company doesn't have to incur the cost of cloud. But overall it's a great app to have if you like to collect recipes and cook. Beats pieces of paper laying around in a drawer unorganized.

After installing this app,find a recipe, open the Kindle "options" select "save to" and "cheftap".  It downloads the recipe to your Kindle then in a second or two, automatically imports to ChefTap (can take a minute). A successful import shows the dish name, a photo of the dish ( if available on the site), the ingredients, the preparation directions.  You can then edit it,add it to category(s), or find a photo if the webpage didn't have one, and add it.With the huge variety of web pages & their technical differences it is obviously going to be difficult to collect the right info, yet this app does most of the time. In the 6 months I've used it they have made many improvements in the importing accuracy and they track which websites don't import right then fix the process for that site. This app does something so complicated that I don't consider problems with a few websites (cookscountry.com is one of them) significant enough to take off a star, especially since they are so good about fixing problem sites. The down side is a Kindle problem not a Cheftap problem and that is that its a pain to enter my own or cookbook recipes since the Kindle doesn't support a keyboard (one finger typing a recipe is time consuming).I love this app and have recommended it to all my friends. I like having recipes in one place, on the Kindle, that i can use in the kitchen instead of paper or books. It makes the cost of the Kindle worth it to me.  I don't know of another app that goes to the website and imports both ingredients and directions with a couple of taps.  That alone makes it worth a lot, just in the time it saves me, as well as not having to print or get pen/paper, or track where I put the paper copy.The programmer is working on setting up cloud backup (a worry with the kindle) and each time you open the app it creates a backup and prompts you to send it to yourself until cloud saving is working. I do wish they had an option to use it on iThings as well as Android, but I will keep my Kindle for this alone if they never have an Apple version.I'm like the other reviewer who commented they couldn't believe this app hasn't gotten more attention. It is one of the most useful apps ive found and it is free.
Wish I had known about this year's ago, so nice not to have pages and pages of printed recipes.

I have been using this app for over two years. It certainly has continued to improve and evolve over time. Yes, to use the app for free, you can only have up to 100 recipes. I have found the annual renewal fee to be a minor issue. I am willing to spend a nominal annual fee to have the convenience of having my favorite family recipes, stored in the cloud and available on my tablet or smartphone at the touch of a button. I love being able to import recipes from different websites. No more newspaper clippings or recipe cards to lose. Also sharing a recipe with friends is a snap. Good investment for those who like to cook.

I absolutely love this app. It has a seamless interface that works well with my Kindle Fire. So quick and easy I couldn't believe it at first. I would go and peek at my recipe files. I recommend this app to anyone trolling the internet for new recipe ideas just click the share button on your tablet and select the Chef Tap app.I should also mention the formatting, Chef Tap re-tools and creates a clean, easy to read format for any recipe I've gotten from the Internet. Try it, I think you'll love it.
Easy to use, a great storage mechanism for recipes. Fabulous app.

Headings: BUG still exists in this version!
Base_Reviews: They said they fixed the bug in the version I downloaded, but IT WAS NOT FIXED. I love love love this app! Previous to finding ChefTap, I had hundreds of internet bookmarks for recipes I wanted to try. ChefTap gathered them all up and they are in one convenient virtual cookbook of recipes that I know i love. If I make changes, no problem..changed right there. If I decide I don't like one after I try it...delete! It's very user friendly and super convenient. I have the free registered account. May be bumping up to pro! If you like to treasure hunt recipes, this app is a must!
I use this app almost every day. I love cooking and I love recipes. I can clip any recipe on a whim, even if I might not make it. When I do make it, I can scale it to my needs, modify, make it MINE!
My go-to app. Love the scaling feature.

I've had Chef Tap on my kindle fires for over 2 years. The newest version has made an already easy to use app easier, faster and more comprehensive. I've been a chef tap pro subscriber for a year. Well worth the $7.99 annual fee.

I love the ease of getting the recipe directly off a web page.  Also, it's great that you have access online on your computer. I would recommend this app to those that love collecting recipes and cookbooks. When I purchased a new tablet, one of my deciding factors was checking to see if Chef Tap was available for download on the new device. Ha ha but there you have it. Try it you won't be disappointed.

I use this app more than any other. I love the fact that I can pull a recipe off the web and everything is in one place. The "make" button is also handy way to organize a rudimentary weekly menu. If it had a shopping list I'd be thrilled (hint).I use this in my kindle and phone... I wish I could have all recipes on both devices, but that is not currently available. The only issue is remembering which recipe is on which device, and if it's on the kindle, I can't pull up the recipe at the store so I have to write down my ingredients beforehand. Otherwise I highly recommend this app!

I don't have internet at home, but was able to download all my Pinterest recipes onto my Kindle Fire HD from work. I used to have to remember to print a page or two to take home with me, so this is great!! I love that these are all hand-picked-by-me recipes that I wanted and not a book filled with only a few I might actually want to try. It's easy to sort and type in any that you already have at home. Home run of an app, I absolutely love it!

Headings: just what I've been looking for
Base_Reviews: I have been wishing there was a way to build a data base of recipes as a result of searching the internet. This program not only will help build a list of recipes, but it also helps build menus and gives the home cook a way to record successes and flops. Another reason I love this program is that I have only a little room for cookbooks and the good ones tend to run more expensive than I can afford right now. This allows me to build my own "cookbook". I like that.

This is such a great app for cooking. I'm not sure what my Kindle settings are at the moment, but when I use this app, the Kindle doesn't go to sleep. This is great for when my hands are messy, and I don't want to "wake up" my Kindle. I love the way this separates the ingredient listing from the cooking steps. I have recommended this to several friends. Also - you can change ingredients to your liking.

Headings: Not what I was looking for
Base_Reviews: This is not what I was looking for so take my rating with a grain of salt, pun intended.  I was looking for an app that would give me a list of recipes.  This will download recipes you find on the internet and keep them all in one place.  This is great for people who love to cook and go surfing websites looking for yummy recipes.  I cook because a like to eat, not because I like to cook.  I want the recipes to come to me.
I rely on ChefTap daily. It's easy to use, easy to clip recipes, and easy to edit for my own personal experience. I've been using ChefTap for four years now. Love it!

Headings: great app for every day UAE
Base_Reviews: I give the developers give stars because ( in my own experience) they were very responsive to my issues and fixed them right away (and that was around Christmas when I expected to wait due to the holidays).I do love the app, would give it five stars if I could make my grocery list from the recipes I want to make, and then add additional shopping items.
