Headings: Works great and you can take it anywhere there is decent WIFI
Base_Reviews: I bought FUBO along with Sling and disconnected from Dish.  I use Amazon Fire TV recast and antennae for local channels. I use the Amazon Fire TV Stick on my home TV.  I  got FUBO because it has Fox News, which Sling does not, and Animal Planet.  I have traveled a fair amount and it works great on the road.  I bring my Chromecast dongle with me and cast FUBO to the TV I am using from my Iphone.  The picture is great.  I do love college football and FUBO has most channels other than ESPN.  Like all streaming services, if you like the channel lineup, you won't regret purchasing it.

1.  Pricing is deceptive.  Advertised at $54.99 but you are forced to take 2 add-ons at signup that increases price to $59.99.  2.  Large portion of the channels air classic TV. I'm currently in the FuboTV seven day trial. Thus far, I've found a few bugs in the Fire TV app. (At least, if you're using the Fire TV Game Controller.) Pause, fast forward and reverse do not work. They are definitely on the right track, but the Fire TV app is certainly in its infancy.

Headings: Flasely Advertised the Eagles vs Cowboys Game
Base_Reviews: It was advertised on Google search engine that the Eagles vs Cowboys game could be viewed on FuboTV. After signing up for the free trial, logged into the website and could not find the games broadcast on a search on the FuboTV website. I immediately cancelled the free trial subscription and after cancelling, I still continue to get emails about their services and links to reactivate the service. I have emailed them to confirm my cancellation (no response) and requested that no further contacted is needed because I do not deal with any company that advertises one thing and does not provide the actual solicited service. If the game that I was looking to view was blacked out or not available, it should have been indicated in the advertisement. Headings: terrible user interface, unreliable streaming, slow to connect, lower res "HD"
Base_Reviews: Boy do I regret believing the reviews on Fubo.  Yes, they have some sports coverage that's hard to get elsewhere.  But it's not worth it.Firstly the user interface is really really bad.  Who designed this thing?  It's clunky, allows very little customization, gives limited information about shows, makes it difficult to change channels, etc. etc.Then you find that it takes some time after you switch to a new channel to get a non-blurry picture.  What?  Are you running this out of your basement, Fubo?And every so often there's an outage.  Unexplained and usually unreported, but there you go, you can't get that stream now.  Has happened to me more than once, and usually right when there was a "I don't want to miss this" event.  I've stopped keeping track.Finally, all the so-called HD streams are really at 720p, not 1080p.  There's one "experimental" 4K channel, rarely has anything on it.Yeah, I've already cancelled my service, just waiting for the current sub to drain.  (Yes, drain is the right term.)  I'm considering Hulu -- it has most of the channels I want, and works well with Fire boxes. I'll miss the occasional La Liga and Ligue 1 and Serie A matches I was able to catch, but I can't justify Fubo for access to the few games I have time to watch.

Headings: Don't bother if you have Amazon Fire TV
Base_Reviews: Amazon Fire TV implementation is terrible. No entry for "Settings" at the top. The navigation between features is much less useful than any other alternative internet TV offering that I've seen. Like when you press the menu button on Playstation Vue, you see the current show, the next couple of shows, and can switch to the Guide if you want. On Fubo, you press the menu button and you can change the video resolution, worthless. They really need to work on navigation for users with Fire TV. About the only thing that you get for live TV are select, the arrow buttons, and return. I assume the Roku is much better, not going to pay $100 to find out, though. The only plus is that the local stations seem to work well. Not the stuttering that I see on Playstation Vue local channel, or all the myriad of problems with the local stations on Hulu with Live TV. But the navigation with Fire TV is so bad, I can't use it.What I'd really like to do is rearrange the guide to put all the sports channels together at the bottom of the guide, instead of having some at the top, and another group at the bottom. Really wacky the way that the channels are arranged. Some are alphabetical like you'd like (the non-sports ones), and the sports channels are just disorganized.But in the end it doesn't matter. Unless I can find another way to use this app without the Fire TV, ain't going to happen.

Headings: Some Problems But No Show Stoppers
Base_Reviews: I must say from the start that the only reason I purchased this app for to watch the Giro d'Italia (Italy's version of the Tour de France). I use NBC Sports Gold to watch cycling but the Giro was not a covered race. A quick Google search led me to fubotv. I primarily watch TV through FireTV so I downloaded the fubotv app and then subscribed through my computer. I have been using fubotv for less than a week. Based upon that experience I offer the following observations.I am able to watch the Giro as I desired. There are quite a few other channels available but I have not watch any, for reasons to be discussed below. The picture quality is fine and as with all internet apps it is dependent on you internet speed/quality.My biggest disappointment is the limited capacity of the "DVR" feature. While it is true you can "record" shows for later viewing you are limited to three "recording" total. Also, you must watch those recording within 72 hours of there recording, after which they will be deleted. This limitation has prevented me from recording any thing other than the Giro (which is a 21 day race) which explains why I have on experience with other channels. This wouldn't be too bad except the DVR does not provide the ability to record a "season". Rather, I have to go the desktop each day and set the DVR to record the next program (in my case, the next race three days in the future). A "Season" or "Record All" option sure would be nice.Another limitation, at least from the FireTV standpoint, is that you can't set the DVR to record a show from your TV. You can access the DVR to play a recording but to set new recordings you must use a computer. Also, the schedule on the FireTV fubotv app is limited to about 12 hours in the future.Finally, I have noticed that when the app is paused and then resumed there is a lot of buffering time before the show starts again. I don't believe this is a ISP problem as the buffering is much longer than with PBS, NBC Sports Gold, HBO Now or YouTube.Bottom line, I am pleased to be able to watch the Giro "legally". The fubotv allows me to do this. The grips above are really are more observations than show stoppers. With that said, to get cycling with the DVR feature I am paying more than $40 per month. I will cancel my subscription after the Giro is done, not because of the app but because I really don't have any interest in the other channels. If fubotv offers some programming that your looking for I would go for it.

Our free trial is now over and we plan to keep Fubo basic.  We get all our favorite channels and some that our cable provider charged a premium for. In addition we have had no outages with Fubo in a week, but 24 hours of dead time on cable in the same period. The 1080 picture is better too.There are some nice pluses like 30 free hours of cloud recordings, and two day access to programs you forget to watch. We will save over a hundred dollars a month- I ditched cable this morning and only wish I'd done it a year ago.There are choices in streaming providers but FuboTV was by far the best for our tastes. Well deserving of five stars.I wrote the above yesterday and then read an astonishing number of bad reviews by others blaming Fubo and/or Firestick for buffering problems and poor picture quality. I think these authors are uninformed. If you want to receive a high definition picture streaming live then the critical issue is the speed and strength of your internet connection from your internet provider, not Fubo and not Firestick. Mine is 100 Mbp/s and there are very few obstacles in the way of the receivers. No buffering and a perfect picture is the result. So to those reviewers- I suggest you look there first and get more wifi speed or a good repeater before laying blame in the wrong place. Most technical reviews (like CNET and others) rate Firestick and Fubo as best in class.

Headings: Not the best on Fire TV Stick
Base_Reviews: I decided to stick with FuboTV after debating between different live TV streaming services, mostly because of their vast channel lineup, as well as being sports-focused (although the lack of ABC and ESPN is quite glaring). I haven't had any issues with the video quality or frequent buffering as some of the other reviewers, but I have noticed that compared to the FuboTV app on the a device like the Roku, the app on the Fire TV Stick is not as intuitive.First of all, it takes a long time to load, not just the app, but even starting up any channels. The circle will spin for a while before streaming finally begins. Another thing I am not too particularly fond of is the rewinding/fast forwarding capability. It's not very streamlined, and you end up going too far backwards or forwards, and have to keep messing around to get to where you want to be. I wish Fubo could implement a thumbnail system like Sling and YouTube TV so you can see exactly where you are in the program when you're rewinding or fast-forwarding. Once you click play, it takes another long time to load.I personally prefer the Fire TV Stick over Roku, but until FuboTV can incorporate a few more features which will help make the service much more streamlined and easy to use, I will use the FuboTV app on the Roku as it is slightly faster and more responsive.

Base_Reviews: I was keen to test Bein Sports on fubo tv and was pretty happy with the coverage of non-football events like F1 racing and rugby. The problem I had with this app is the flakiness of the connection. We have a 75Mb broadband link (cable) which supports all the main on-demand movie channels (Amazon, Netflix, Hulu, Crackle) with no problem. Live apps like Twitch and CBS work fine, as did SlingTV (which we cancelled due to content rather than quality of experience). But fubo tv is a hit-or-miss experience where you often have to back out and retry 3-4 times before getting a reliable connection. When it finally connects, the quality is great - but the effort needed to get there is frustrating and not up to par for an online streaming service in 2016. We cancelled the subscription as a result but would be happy to try again (pun intended) in a few months.

Headings: An OK App That Could be Better
Base_Reviews: I struggled with rating this a 2 or a 3.  It's OK to pass the time for a little while, but could be so much better.  Various webcams from around the world are broadcast for several minutes each, and range from elephants in Indonesia to a Michigan forest to Times Square to a lake in New Zealand - well, you get the picture.  Most have no sounds, but some, like the New Orleans Karaoke Cam or Dublin Pub Cam, can irritate the heck out of you if the volume isn't turned down.  EarthCam chooses what you see, although you have a search ability to turn on any camera that they have used in the past day.  Their choices seem to be heavily weighed in favor of New York with cameras showing Times Square, New York streets and buildings, etc.  It is somewhat irritating to watch a camera for 5 minutes or so and then have it switched to something else,  Also, many of the cameras are frequently shown over and over, with one or two others shown in between, so you might get Times Square three or four times in an hour, while other cameras might be shown once a day for a few days and then dropped from the lineup completely.  It would be a vast improvement if you were able to choose any camera in their system and leave it on for as long as you'd like, or at least have the ability to keep a cam that you're interested in from switching automatically.  Finally, while some cams can be interesting, many more are as dull as can be and not much better than watching a painting on your wall.

Headings: Better than I thought at first
Base_Reviews: I'm retracting my original review (and deleting most, if not all, of it), which was very negative and premature.Actually, I quite like this app on my Amazon Fire TV (and I also like the EarthCam app on my android phone). It's better than I thought. And, I have discovered several fallacies in my previous reviews. The only detractor is that there is no screen of all available webcams through which one might scroll in order to navigate to a particular site. The lineup changes every day, and sometimes more than once a day, depending on popularity of displayed activities such as parades, or even newsworthy events such as hurricanes.Soon after I paid the fee to break out of the automatic schedule, which changes to a different camera location every five or ten minutes, I bemoaned the fact that I could not set up my own custom list of preferred webcams, but could only choose one, which would remain constant until I manually changed it to another one. This is actually somewhat of an advantage, because it enables me to watch one scene as long as I desire. For instance, a few days ago, we watched an awesome display of fireworks at the bridge over the Danube River in downtown Budapest, Hungary. We also recently watched a surprisingly long parade in Vinita, Oklahoma, celebrating Will Rogers Day.My previous assessment of the process of returning to the scheduled rotation of webcams was also premature. We just navigate to another webcam that we want to see. As it turns out, we rarely wish to get back to the set rotation anyway.All in all, we're pretty satisfied with the lineup and the way it operates. I recommend it highly.

Headings: Around the planet from your home.
Base_Reviews: Go around the world from your living room recliner!  This app on my Amazon Fire TV Stick is free, but well worth the low price to upgrade annually, giving you more control in what you view.  The HD (and often 4K) picture quality is incredible; many include sound.  The webcam worldwide locations -and the webcam placement at these locations- are like living postcards.  Oh, and that's what makes viewing Earthcam a neat experience... the fact that what you're viewing is, indeed, live (there's a "Live" label at the upper left of the screen).  So it's definitely a heightened sense of reality as you watch, for example, the 4K views (there are several) of Times Square in NYC; or the Elvis Wedding Chapel in Vegas; or Abbey Road in London.  Love that most cam views also provide the locale's time and temp, plus optional background music as you watch (you can select the music genre and auto-cycle thru the cameras at selected intervals or manually move from camera to camera).Again, my review is on the app for my Amazon Fire TV and I'm completely pleased, using it practically every morning with my first cup of coffee. I realize this app is also available for other media devices (desktops and laptops) that have additional features, like camera pan & tilt.Lots and lots of locations throughout the world. Hey! Mall of America.  Sure would like to see a Nickelodeon Universe webcam.  Or Disneyworld?

Headings: Earth to EarthCam--there's this thing called "user exerience."
Base_Reviews: Barely deserving of 3 stars. Even viewing schedule-free, on my Firestick TV, scrolling through the cameras is hopelessly frustrating. With luck and determination, you can scroll past countless, redundant selections of most cameras to find those you are seeking (how about a Favorites option, maybe?). And every now and then, after a seemingly interminable period of offering the same cameras, they surprise you with a new one--as if the strategy is to retain their audience by rationing, rather than opening their camera library. A lot of the featured cameras are boring, static views of forests, coastlines and distant city skylines (a ratings option, maybe?). EarthCam has all the elements of what could be a fascinating viewing experience. But they present it in such a haphazard, user-unfriendly way, you wonder who, if anyone, there is minding the store.

Good little free app for organizing flight info, hotel confirmations, car rentals and activities, as well as saving maps and directions between your stops.  Putting all your info on your phone or tablet allows you to share it with travel companions and alleviates the need to carry printed copies.  However, the $49 upgrade to Trip it Pro is useless.  They fail to provide the services promised (flight status), and while admitting their failure, they refuse to refund any portion of the annual fee...which was to paid specifically to get flight status updates.  Quite the business model...

I travel a lot, both domestically and overseas.  I had always wished there was a program that could keep track of my confirmation #s, flight info, car rental, hotel,  directions, phone numbers etc. without my having to pull them all off of emails, websites, etc.  Tripit does that.  It even keeps all of my activities organized so I can immediately see if I am double booked or not allowing enough time.  I tell my husband Tripit allows me to be spontaneous - in an organized way :)

This application has a lot of potential. The way my trip is booked, however, made me have to enter the data manually instead of forwarding emails to it for automatic entry. That said, I like the way that it automatically updated all my flight information once i entered the date and flight number, and it supposedly will update any changes to flights. It's also a good way to share the itinerary with family.

Headings: Nice to have all travel records at one place

So I could see everything online on my desktop but parts of my trip were missing on other devices. I decided to reinstall the app where it was not working properly and got everything correct on mobile devices. I wish it would fixed. Otherwise it is very helpful application.

It warned us but about 2 hours later than the airline did.Other than that, simply emailing your travel plans and easy viewing make this a winner.

I honestly don't think this is necessary since I think it is already very easy to check in and receive your tickets at the airport. It also isnt able to separate my work trips from personal ones. I can see how it could be useful for others though.

Headings: Elegant and Multi Platform and has a unique import feature
Base_Reviews: I don't travel a lot, but if I did I couldn't live without this.I have it loaded on my phone and my tablet and I use the web version as well and they all sync each other !  Change it on my phone and the others get changed. I love it.You can create multiple trips. Then you create a plan within the trip. Plans can  have segments within them.  The metaphors are natural.  Then comes the wizard feature. Set the program up to read an email account and it takes emails and turns them into plans !! Good stuff Maynard.One of the tricks I learned was to just put the zip code in for the address and it makes the time local. If you put a complete address in you can actually get a map.I feel bad I failed to pay for the full version, but I don't travel enough to worry about worry about alerts, alternate flights and seat tracking.  This is one of the five best apps I have

In all fairness, I should say that I never got beyond downloading this app.  In reading the terms of use, I realized that my travel information would be on a TripIt server somewhere waiting for a hacker to grab it (think Target credit cards!)  This app has the potential to provide criminals with the opportunity to find out if you are on vacation before robbing your house.  Far fetched?  Have you already forgotten Target?  Gather the information yourself - how hard is it to cut and paste it from your confirmations to a Word document?

Make your reservations nonlinear.Email the confirmations to Tripit.Within a few minutes they magically appear on a single itinerary in your account.I use it allot the time now.  I don't have to print anything out or write anything down anymore.  Once viewed, the information is even available while off line.  I can share the information very easily with others.  It's easy to make changes to my itinerary.  I can even add my own personal notes or make manual entries if I would like.Overall it's a great repository for all of my travel information.  The only thing even remotely negative that I could say is that once I made a reservation for a hotel whose confirmation the atripit software couldn't read.  I simply entered the information manually.  That happened only once out of dozens of airline, train, hotel, and rental car reservations I've made over the last few years.

Headings: Great service for a good price
Base_Reviews: TripIt is a very good product, I just wonder how long it will last. I have been a free user and now use the paid version. It culls my e-mail to help develop an itinerary which was a cumbersome manual task in the past. In chronological order I now see a sensible list of my flights, car rentals and hotel reservations with contact information.Try it for free and you'll love it. I only use two of the Pro features, but they are a big deal. The flight change notifications kept me from being left at the Philly airport because you couldn't hear the overhead notifications. Another is the ability to easily search for alternate flights, in my case due to weather changes.There is a 30 day free trial of Pro and if you travel frequently it is money well spent.

Headings: This app may not make travel fun, but at least it's much more efficient
Base_Reviews: The big value of this app, especially with the pro subscription, is that it gathers all the info you may need in one place. You can continue for forward various things like shuttle arrangements, activities while on a trip to plans@tripit.com and for most of them tripit parses them and inserts all the relevant info in your trip itinerary. On a recent trip, the airline had made some goofy codeshare arrangement where a separate ticket was issued by the other airline. Their agent couldn't find my ticket when I tried to check in. I looked in Tripit, there was the other ticket number, she recognized it was a different airlines ticket number and was able to help me. What are the  odds I would have made that flight without TripIt? Pretty low..

You can add all your travel plans via the website and will update when loaded.  Your confirmation letters from your airline and hotel reservations can be forwarded to a special email address that will be added to your plans.  I've used it for various trips both near and far.  I do like it.

Headings: The organization of MY trips is very good.

The organization of MY trips is very good.

Headings: Great Way to Keep Track of Trip Plans
Base_Reviews: I've been using TripIt for the past several trips.  It serves the purpose of keeping track of my full itinerary, and I can build it little by little as reservations are made (or modified).  It includes such things as airport transfers, flights, cruises, tours, hotels, etc.  The coolest thing is that, with most reservations, you can simply forward your confirmation e-mail to plans@tripit.com, and TripIt automatically incorporates it into your itinerary, subject to any editing you may wish to do later.  Once built, itineraries can be e-mailed easily to travel companions, family members, etc., so they have all the info as well.  You can easily print out the itinerary, or keep it available on your mobile device, such as a tablet.

Headings: I use TripIt Pro - GREAT convenience!

"Don't leave home without it" seriously applies to this app!TripIt Pro proactively feeds flight changes, allows you to look at alternate flights and available seat inventory and offers some additional bells and whistles - in my opinion well worth the slight upgrade price.

I love Trip It & have used it for years to keep my travel reservations organized.  It's as simple as forwarding your travel confirmation emails & Trip It knows how to organize it. Plus, you've got for example the hotel's address, phone number and confirmation number AND a map showing you how to get to the location. LOVE IT!

This is a great app for traveling.  It automatically organizes your hotel, car and flight information so you do not have to print and carry confirmations.  It will provide directions to the hotel, check in and check out information.  It also has detailed information about flights and car rental.  You can also input information manually such as tours.

Headings: Very easy to use, no learning curve or tedious typing in itinerary
Base_Reviews: Really useful.  I had no idea I needed this until my co-worker showed it to me on a business trip.  This helps us unorganized people to put the important travel information in one location.  Their clever trick of just forwarding the itinerary to tripit.com email address works great.  It's so easy I actually use it.

Headings: Gives me peace of mind when travel planning
Base_Reviews: I'm really glad this App was recommended to me. I have several trips planned this year and this has really helped to organize all my bookings in one location. Now I am assured that I have remembered to make all the necessary reservations for each trip. It even allows you to view your itinerary when you don't have wifi access.

I already had TripIt on my smart phone, but got it for my Kindle Fire as well.  I love the ability to carry all my travel plans on my phone/Kindle, instead of having to drag all the paper copies of confirmation numbers, itinerary, etc.  Would recommend to anyone that travels at all.
App was not what I was looking for. Wanted to be able to find and share various types of travel options

Too complicated to use.  I sent one of my confirmation e-mails to it and of course, it didn't make it. Then the e-mails start pouring in from tripit!  I have 3 upcoming trips, a couple with pretty complex plans, and I think I'll keep all of my details on paper, where I can keep track of everything!

This is one of my favorite APs. I don't travel much, but it seamlessly grabs itineraries from mailbox, and posts them along with all the pertinent info to my phone based AP. Makes it really easy to see flight times and confirmation numbers making it a lot easier to keep on track.
I used this app in the past for planning trips and I'm using it for an upcoming trip. I like that it takes my flight information and inserts it into the app.

The best way to organize all my trips.  Tripit searches my emails for trip related info and auto adds it.  Has a nice feature to send notices to you related to your trips as well as letting you see where others in your group are traveling and currently at.

This itinerary organizer is easy to use and very beneficial.  I have used it for repeated business trips as well as a number of leisure trips to the orient.  It feeds hotel and flight info seamlessly and give me one point to go to for all my travel confirmations,

Headings: Just starting to use this app but I can see that it will be very helpful
Base_Reviews: Lots better than my usual system of a stack of printed sheets to keep together.  Very easy to set up.
This app is extremely conveinient and relieves the stress of making sure you have printed all your confirmations and reservations. I would strongly recommend this app.

Great Product, I do not use the Pro series as am retired and travel only a few times a year.  Used it for 18 month and never failed me. I also interfaced it with flight track and always know what's going on with my travel.Thanks for the Great Product.
not as powerful as the web version or as well designed as the iphone app but does the main tasks well

Headings: Good at telling you what you already know.
Base_Reviews: I don't get it. I do all the planning, I make the reservations, put the confirmations into tripit and it tells me what I've done? I missed something important, I guess.But it gets one star for putting itself as my Kindle Fire Silk browser home page, and I can't figure out how to remove it.
App works very well for me.  Seamlessly syncs with emailed travel notifications.display on tablet is nice and map connections save looking up on different app
I've got all my holidays in it (flights, cars rented, hotel reservations), it provides you map, addresses evertyhing I need!
This app is very helpful. But I am tired of being pestered to review these things. I wonder when I
GREAT! Just what I was looking for, Thank you. Would recomend to all who are in need of this item.
Not sure how much better the Pro version is but the basics for the free one is great
Work for a travel agency & use it for personal as well.  Worth it to have even if not used all the time.
I only wish they had  a subscription for infrequent travelers, say 6 trip max, for a better price.

I couldn't use it. I have aol mail and it will only use Gmail or Yahoo. I sent our confirmation papers to my husband's gmail account and it still wouldn't' t take them because they weren't' t originals. Very frustrating. The app suggested I log them in manually. It was easier to write it down.
Nice to have everything in one place for our group of travelers

Good little free app for organizing flight info, hotel confirmations, car rentals and activities, as well as saving maps and directions between your stops.  Putting all your info on your phone or tablet allows you to share it with travel companions and alleviates the need to carry printed copies.  However, the $49 upgrade to Trip it Pro is useless.  They fail to provide the services promised (flight status), and while admitting their failure, they refuse to refund any portion of the annual fee...which was to paid specifically to get flight status updates.  Quite the business model...

I travel a lot, both domestically and overseas.  I had always wished there was a program that could keep track of my confirmation #s, flight info, car rental, hotel,  directions, phone numbers etc. without my having to pull them all off of emails, websites, etc.  Tripit does that.  It even keeps all of my activities organized so I can immediately see if I am double booked or not allowing enough time.  I tell my husband Tripit allows me to be spontaneous - in an organized way :)

This application has a lot of potential. The way my trip is booked, however, made me have to enter the data manually instead of forwarding emails to it for automatic entry. That said, I like the way that it automatically updated all my flight information once i entered the date and flight number, and it supposedly will update any changes to flights. It's also a good way to share the itinerary with family.

Headings: Planning a Road Trip with Tripit
Base_Reviews: I've just planned a road trip with Tripit and wonder if the time I spent with the learning curve and entering all the data was worth the trouble.  It looks good on my computer, but is awkward on my Kindle Fire.  I'd say the paper file I collected in the first place will be more helpful and less time-consuming.

Headings: Nice to have all travel records at one place
Base_Reviews: I love that organizer – especially when you travel different locations, change planes, hotels etc.I found one glitch though - not all the parts of my trip that I emailed to TripIt show up automatically on my iPhone, Kindle Fire or Galaxy. So I could see everything online on my desktop but parts of my trip were missing on other devices. I decided to reinstall the app where it was not working properly and got everything correct on mobile devices. I wish it would fixed. Otherwise it is very helpful application.

Designed mostly for flights,car,hotel type of travel but useful for keeping other information in one place.I just drove to a hotel,attended an outdoor concert,made reservations for dinner and it was convenient to keep addresses,check in times,etc.Couldn't get the website links after copying and pasting into notes,and other minor improvements could be made to make it more useful to other travelers besides the traditional car/flight/hotel mode.

At first the program worked perfectly. But as it was complicating the trip; I did not have the same results. Unless you travel constantly because of your work, I do not recommend buying it. The free version is regular. The program to compare your complete operations is very expensive.

I found out about this nifty app while on a plane as a recommendation by another traveler.Does a great job of organizing all of your travel details step by step with address and direction of hotels and airlines.Only problem I say was that the app did not warn us ahead of time of a flight cancellation. It warned us but about 2 hours later than the airline did.Other than that, simply emailing your travel plans and easy viewing make this a winner.

I honestly don't think this is necessary since I think it is already very easy to check in and receive your tickets at the airport. It also isnt able to separate my work trips from personal ones. I can see how it could be useful for others though.

Headings: Elegant and Multi Platform and has a unique import feature
Base_Reviews: I don't travel a lot, but if I did I couldn't live without this.I have it loaded on my phone and my tablet and I use the web version as well and they all sync each other !  Change it on my phone and the others get changed. I love it.You can create multiple trips. Then you create a plan within the trip. Plans can  have segments within them.  The metaphors are natural.  Then comes the wizard feature. Set the program up to read an email account and it takes emails and turns them into plans !! Good stuff Maynard.One of the tricks I learned was to just put the zip code in for the address and it makes the time local. If you put a complete address in you can actually get a map.I feel bad I failed to pay for the full version, but I don't travel enough to worry about worry about alerts, alternate flights and seat tracking.  This is one of the five best apps I have

In all fairness, I should say that I never got beyond downloading this app.  In reading the terms of use, I realized that my travel information would be on a TripIt server somewhere waiting for a hacker to grab it (think Target credit cards!)  This app has the potential to provide criminals with the opportunity to find out if you are on vacation before robbing your house.  Far fetched?  Have you already forgotten Target?  Gather the information yourself - how hard is it to cut and paste it from your confirmations to a Word document?

Make your reservations nonlinear.Email the confirmations to Tripit.Within a few minutes they magically appear on a single itinerary in your account.I use it allot the time now.  I don't have to print anything out or write anything down anymore.  Once viewed, the information is even available while off line.  I can share the information very easily with others.  It's easy to make changes to my itinerary.  I can even add my own personal notes or make manual entries if I would like.Overall it's a great repository for all of my travel information.  The only thing even remotely negative that I could say is that once I made a reservation for a hotel whose confirmation the atripit software couldn't read.  I simply entered the information manually.  That happened only once out of dozens of airline, train, hotel, and rental car reservations I've made over the last few years.

Headings: Great service for a good price
Base_Reviews: TripIt is a very good product, I just wonder how long it will last. I have been a free user and now use the paid version. It culls my e-mail to help develop an itinerary which was a cumbersome manual task in the past. In chronological order I now see a sensible list of my flights, car rentals and hotel reservations with contact information.Try it for free and you'll love it. I only use two of the Pro features, but they are a big deal. The flight change notifications kept me from being left at the Philly airport because you couldn't hear the overhead notifications. Another is the ability to easily search for alternate flights, in my case due to weather changes.There is a 30 day free trial of Pro and if you travel frequently it is money well spent.

Headings: This app may not make travel fun, but at least it's much more efficient
Base_Reviews: The big value of this app, especially with the pro subscription, is that it gathers all the info you may need in one place. You can continue for forward various things like shuttle arrangements, activities while on a trip to plans@tripit.com and for most of them tripit parses them and inserts all the relevant info in your trip itinerary. On a recent trip, the airline had made some goofy codeshare arrangement where a separate ticket was issued by the other airline. Their agent couldn't find my ticket when I tried to check in. I looked in Tripit, there was the other ticket number, she recognized it was a different airlines ticket number and was able to help me. What are the  odds I would have made that flight without TripIt? Pretty low..

You can add all your travel plans via the website and will update when loaded.  Your confirmation letters from your airline and hotel reservations can be forwarded to a special email address that will be added to your plans.  I've used it for various trips both near and far.  I do like it.

Headings: The organization of MY trips is very good.
Base_Reviews: I would have given it a 5 star rating except for the fact that when my children travel and send me their itineraries, it records them as my trips, asks for a hotel, sends me updates, etc.  Perhaps there's a way to avoid that, but directions are hard to come by these days.  The organization of MY trips is very good.

Headings: Great Way to Keep Track of Trip Plans
Base_Reviews: I've been using TripIt for the past several trips.  It serves the purpose of keeping track of my full itinerary, and I can build it little by little as reservations are made (or modified).  It includes such things as airport transfers, flights, cruises, tours, hotels, etc.  The coolest thing is that, with most reservations, you can simply forward your confirmation e-mail to plans@tripit.com, and TripIt automatically incorporates it into your itinerary, subject to any editing you may wish to do later.  Once built, itineraries can be e-mailed easily to travel companions, family members, etc., so they have all the info as well.  You can easily print out the itinerary, or keep it available on your mobile device, such as a tablet.

Headings: A great way to keep track of travel
Base_Reviews: They make it so easy to share flight info into the app it's one of the first things I do for each trip. Of course, since the Kindle Fire HD doesn't have an "anywhere" connection I can only use it when I'm near WiFi. That means I have to use the app on my phone instead when I'm travelling. Even so, it's an essential part of my travel material.

Don't leave home without it.  Every time we have to attend a world mark presentation ( I don't like to attend)  to stop the sales person and to get them off the sales pitch I show them the Tripit app..it's so good they ask me for Info.

Headings: I have not travelled except by automobile in several. ...
Base_Reviews: I have not travelled except by automobile in several.  Booking the various flights, rooms and car rental was difficult enough but I had trouble organizing the information to keep track of all of the information.  One of the travel sites I used sent me a link to tripit, I used it and it solved my issues.  Afterward, I used the app to keep all of the information available.

Headings: I use TripIt Pro - GREAT convenience!
Base_Reviews: I travel a lot - 125,000 miles per year is common. What a pain to have all these air, hotel, cruise etc. bookings - except now I e-mail them all to TripIt and it aggregates them into my trips. So on my Kindle Fire HDX or my smartphone, I have it all at my fingertips - ticket and reservations numbers, times, dates, appointments, you name it. How very smart, and how very convenient! "Don't leave home without it" seriously applies to this app!TripIt Pro proactively feeds flight changes, allows you to look at alternate flights and available seat inventory and offers some additional bells and whistles - in my opinion well worth the slight upgrade price.

Only issue I ever have is if I'm tracking 2 flights it dumps them into one "trip" and you need to go to web version to split them up (that's the only way I've found to do it).Love the app though and find it very useful. Recommend it to my friends all the time.

Headings: helpful but directions could be better
Base_Reviews: Pretty good app. It was a little repetitive adding all the things to the itinerary. Also I wish with the driving directions the app generated its own map or once the map was opened it would stay in the directions instead of having to open Google maps or another map app every time. Overall was very helpful on my trip.

Indispensable while traveling for business.  All I need in one place.  Never without confirmation numbers or directions.  But disclaimer,  work uses Concur as our travel partner.  Less work on my part

Headings: It is super great if you travel often
Base_Reviews: I was using this app before I got the premium version. It is super great if you travel often. It certainly has some quirks if you are flying around multiple places and it doesn't do a great job when you forward someone else's plans but those are things you can manually fix from a computer and logging in

I really, really like this app. I would love it if it had a trip checklist integrated into it to check off packing items, etc. Also if web links could directly be linked to entries for restaurants, activities, etc. Other than that, I have found it very useful so far in planning our trip to Estes Park this summer!

I was going to give this a lower rating but decided it probably isn't the app that's at fault, but the operator.  I can't even figure out how to use it!  Maybe it's not good on my Kindle Fire.  don't know how to input trips to even get started.  So I uninstalled it.  Too bad. :-(

I've used Tripit for a while, the website and the mobile version. Recently I downloaded the app to see if it provided more information than the mobile site. It does and it's great.It takes a little time to figure out the navigation. Otherwise, you'll have most of the functionality of the full website.

Headings: While it is a handy repository for travel information, ...
Base_Reviews: While it is a handy repository for travel information, I had understood you could use it without needing to be online. Unfortunately the map feature which activates when you click on most things requires internet connection.

Awesome APP.  Couldn't be easier to use.  FWD your trip emails to it and it creates your itinerary.  Synchs super fast.  A little weird at first giving away my very specific whereabouts, but I got over that. Just used it for 15 days across Thailand. Keeps all of your confirmation codes handy in an easy to view layout.  Highly recommend for travelers who prefer having an organized structure for your travel arrangements.

Headings: Good App for tracking Business and personal trips
Base_Reviews: I used this App for all trips. My daughter is in college and I always keep her plans in here as well so I know her flights for coming home and going back to school. I really like that I just forward confirmations from travel agents, airlines, hotels, etc to plans@tripit.com and then it shows up in my app. All I have I have to do is let TripIt know which email addresses to associate with my trips.Sometimes I need to go to the website to do a few things but rarely.

I've been using TripIt for 4 yrs and can't imagine traveling without it. I just loaded the app on my Kindle Fire in preparation for an upcoming trip (I had already set up the trip from my PC at work and by forwarding all my confirmation e-mails to plans @ tripit.com. The mobile app is great, but on a non-phone device it really should cache the login credentials since you don't always have access to wi-fi while traveling. Still, it seems to work fine so long as you remember not to explicitly log out.

I used to print out every reservation, plan etc for a trip and put them in my folder.  This has taken the place of the folder. I have this app on my computer, my phone and my tablet and can see every detail of my trips.  It is as easy as forwarding my email confirmations to their web site and it is in my itinerary.  You can share itineraries with others on the trip or anyone else you choose.

Headings: A must-have for any road warrior
Base_Reviews: If you're a frequent traveler, TripIt is absolutely essential.  I haven't found any other service that can better organize multiple trips with multiple people, all with mobile device integration across all of the major.platforms (including BlackBerry!)If you subscribe to TripIt Pro, there's no need to buy the paid version of this app; the free version will be ad -free for you on all devices.This version has been updated to work with the Kindle Fire and it looks great.  I now have TripIt on all of my on-the-go devices.

Tripit organizes your trips with dates, activity, maps that are printable & even line items costs & total trip cost!Email confirmations are simply forwarded to automatically update your trip intinerary.And you can share your trip so other family members can have your exact plans.I use Tripit on my Kindle and as I update it, my husband's phone gets each update and vice versa.Tripit has several catagories to add to your trip such as hotel, cruise ports, rental cars, activities, restaurant reservations....even gas!Another must-have for travelers!
very difficult to imput the information as display is not clear.  Tried to input my new trip, it does not allow everything in precise order
Tried a couple of trips and did not work for overseas and foreign airlines. If your travel is in the US it is probably ok.

Headings: Great for a road trip, too!
Base_Reviews: It takes some getting used to, but it's very handy to have all the travel details in one place-- most even autofill! Maps of the locations on your itinerary are included, and it will make a "Triptik" for driving from Point A to Point B.

Love it!  I was able to automatically upload all my flight details just by forwarding my confirmation email to them.  The hotel confirmation didn't work, but probably because it's in a different country. Still, it was very easy to add in all my trip activities online (easier to do on a computer than on the app, because there was a lot of copying and pasting).  When I was done, I was able to email my itinerary to family and friends who had expressed an interest.

I put all the details of a fairly extensive trip in, and all i could get back out was a listing of the hotels.  What i really needed more than anything, my flight information, was never seen again.  As this trip involved 10 different flights, I could have really used this data.
The product/service seems great for the frequent fliers.  I'm not one.  But if you are… go ahead and give it a try.

Headings: Saves so much time for major trips.
Base_Reviews: Making changes on an 18-day to the U.K. Is super easy. Reservation details are automatically added by Tripit. All you do is forward all confirmation emails and like magic they show up in your trip itinerary. Cost to go to Triple Pro after 30 days is very worthwhile. I used to do all the planning on a spreadsheet. This is infinitely better.

Headings: Worth the time to learn how to use it.
Base_Reviews: Now that I know how to use it, I think it will be worth the effort next time. It should be a lot easier to use. The learning curve was rather steep but intend to use it on our forthcoming trip to Florida, Georgia and South Carolina.

Headings: Go with straight Android or iOS as it doesn't work on my Kindel Fire.
Base_Reviews: This was a good program until it stopped working on my Kindle Fire.  One day it worked, the next day it stated this version is no longer supported.  Versions after this don't work on my Kindle Fire but I'm not upgrading hardware and Android OS for a single app.

You have to give this application full access to your email account, and they know your schedule and when you will be out of town. It accepted the flight and hotel reservations, which were embedded in the emails,  however It would not accept my itinerary regardless of the format (PDF, rich text, simple text , xml or html. You can close the account if you can find the link for it, which is hidden. There is no way to remove your data from the application.

Very convenient method of storing all your travel information and having it available through your tablet.  Once the details are completed than can be forwarded on to family and friends. The details can also be linked to your calendar, the only issue to throw you here is the activities are displayed in your home time.  Still quite good to show the trip in a different format.I'll certainly keep the app but probably won't keep the pro version.

Headings: You have to buy the full version to get the features you want.
Base_Reviews: But does do some of things I like. Putting the airplane ticketing information in one spot.Information about car rental.

If you already have your travel plans made, or more likely, someone has made them for you, you can recording them in this app.  If you want to MAKE plans, look for another app.  The start and finish date tool doesn't even indicate the day of the week!  There is NO provision for driving anywhere.  There are no maps, time calculators, or probable speed indicators.  How can this be a trip planner??? Forget it.

Really works well to keep you up to date with all your flight information in real time.  It would be nice to have a few more features like being able to check in to your flight through the app but it's still great.

Headings: I quick it with Trip It!
Base_Reviews: I love trip planner!It my quick glance guide for all my travel calender needs

Headings: Very good app. Was able to easily use to organize ...
Base_Reviews: Very good app. Was able to easily use to organize and start a family road trip. Easy to apply schedules, and descriptions to keep at your fingertips for the trip.

Does not accept all forwards of reservations so some things have to be entered manually. It is great for keeping all information for each trip in one place. The reservations that don't load automatically will show up in the notes file.

Headings: Perfect app and simple to use
Base_Reviews: Part of me wishes I traveled more so that I would have a reason to purchase the full version of this application.  It was very simple to use, allowed me to keep my itineraries handy, and kept me on schedule.  The mapping feature worked great too when leaving the airport.  I had doubts when I needed to email my travel plans, and was pleasantly surprised when the app came back 100% accurate.

Headings: Useless if you live in a small town that's not in their system
Base_Reviews: Looks like a nice app, but it didn't recognize the existence of my little town. Oddly, it did recognize a much smaller town about 20 miles away from me. So it was absolutely useless as I couldn't start my itinerary from where I live. Looks like it's mostly geared toward air travel anyway....I was looking for road trip apps. My hometown shows up on all the major mapmaking apps and gps's, it should be in there!

Headings: It seems like the apps I bought from Amazon would download but ...
Base_Reviews: I use it in my travels but when it's time to update  it would not install. It seems like the apps I bought from Amazon would download but would not install !

I was excited about this app as I have a trip planned for March.  But, my travel agent is apparently not on Tripit's approved list, so my trip could not be loaded to my account.  And it wouldn't work by manually entering my trip either!  The flights that I entered came up as different destinations than what I entered.  So, uninstalled the app, and closed my account.  Very disappointed.

Headings: great idea - works well on my Kindle FIRE
Base_Reviews: I found this app while cruising through the app store - it will be VERY useful during my travels.  I've always created an air itinerary on my computer, printed it to bring with me, along with other printouts for hotel reservations, entertainment tickets, etc.  Now, I can have them all in one place on my FIRE, and can save some trees at the same time.

I travel a lot and this has been one of the best ways to stay organized that I have found.  It looks through my gmail and finds my airline, rental car, and hotel reservations and then displays them all for me in one app.  I have it loaded on both my Kindle and phone and use it all the time.  Highly recommended.
Good product, wish it was easier to add plans like restaurants, meetings with friends etc. E.g. add the name and it brings in the address via a search
The more complex my travel itinerary, the more valuable this app is to me.
I will try to use it soon.
when i try to use it it makes me log in over and over and then tries to get me to upgrade and I was traveling and just really needed to look at my itinerary quickly!!!
It didn't open properly on my phone
I haven't used it much yet.
not really useful for me

I love this APP, it put everything in one place. I use for all my travel and even local events that I buy tickets for so I don't have to remember which ticket source I used.  I highly recommend this for any one who travels or goes to lots of local events.
with some of the vacation information that i had emailed to TRIP IT, it would not update, it was very nice for the information that i did automatically input via the email that was sent

The app picks up travel info in emails and automatically adds it to your trip, including flight, terminal, and get changes.  You can also manually add info into the trip data.  I've used the app for several years and have been very satisfied.  The premium version does more, but the free version is excellent.
My husband and I recently took two separate vacations (back-to-back) out West.  We found Tripit very helpful.  We were able to keep track of our travels with ease.
Didnt use it much.

Headings: Definitely a must if travel is your life
Base_Reviews: Just started using this and so far so good!  I do quite a bit of traveling with my job, so this is a good app to keep all travel in one location.
This app failed to provide me with any valuable info.  Data was missing or appeared too late to be of use.  I would not recommend it to any of my friends.

I found this app after I had made reservations for an up-coming trip, but after downloading tripit to both my computer and Kindle, I forwarded the (numerous) confirmation emails to plans@tripit.com. Tripit organized all confirmations by date, making complete itinerary (with all reservation info) available on both computer and Kindle. There are even spaces available to add notes. This is a great organizational tool.

Headings: How Can You Travel Without This App?
Base_Reviews: Tripit keeps track of everything. Air, gates, cars, hotels, miles, points, and all the phone numbers and maps for each.  You email in your confirmations, they sort it all out, and update your calendars.  I've used this app for years (had to re-download it for my new FireHD).  It's the best personal travel app there is.
works

I love Trip It & have used it for years to keep my travel reservations organized.  It's as simple as forwarding your travel confirmation emails & Trip It knows how to organize it. Plus, you've got for example the hotel's address, phone number and confirmation number AND a map showing you how to get to the location. LOVE IT!

This is a great app for traveling.  It automatically organizes your hotel, car and flight information so you do not have to print and carry confirmations.  It will provide directions to the hotel, check in and check out information.  It also has detailed information about flights and car rental.  You can also input information manually such as tours.

Headings: The perfect GPS app for off-line mapping and routing. Saves a lot of data.
Base_Reviews: If you have a smartphone with GPS or a tablet with GPS, this is a must have app. You do not need to have an Internet connection to use this, it works perfectly off-line and it is fast and easy to use.A word about off-line GPS apps. All search in a slightly different way: you set a filter for the country, city, street and then cross street which is easy to do. You can also pick a building or landmark as the cross. They choose show on map and refine exactly where you want to go.The turn by turn directions are great and as good as anything else. Like any route mapping system, once in a while you might make an extra turn but there isn't a system made that doesn't do that once in a while.I've used this on tablets and smartphones, it works great on all of them.To save data if you don't have an unlimited plan, simply turn your data off and this app will work off-line. It does also work well using WiFi or your data access if you want to go that route but I found that using this saves a lot of money and is hassle free.To get started, remember to download the Global base maps and then the maps for the country or state you need. The free version limits the number of downloads but unless you need more than that, the free version works just great. The paid for version isn't that expensive and you can get some additional advanced features.What I like is using this app on a tablet with the tablet's camera point at the road. Then whenever you want to you link a picture or video to a location for your records. It is simple to do.Adding favorites is super easy. Touch the location on the map and then choose add to my places from the menu. It is super easy and works.

OSM (the map database, which is different than the mapping program that uses it) is of, by and for the users. If something is missing, YOU, the user, can participate by adding to or fixing it. Headings: Best walking and cycling maps with OpenStreetMap
Base_Reviews: OsmAnd visualises OpenStreetMap maps. OpenStreetMap are much more up to date and better for walking and cycling than Google Maps. OsmAnd has many functions, and the interface can appear clutter. Configuration can greatly reduce the clutter but takes patients. OsmAnd permits the maps to be updated and corrected - very useful for an open source mapping system. The maps are download OFFLINE - ideal for areas without mobile cover (forest, mountains, etc). Navigation screen is Ok but not as clear and attractive as other apps. Excellent: the dynamic route planning. If you choose not to follow the route, the route will be recalculated. Route calculation options are limited for cycling. Komoot does a better job of distinguishing between road, touring, gravel, and mountain bike routes. The information is on the map, but the routing algorithm needs to be smart enough to use it. Komoot, however, does not have dynamic route planning. Choose, therefore, the less of two evils. With hourly updates of OpenStreetMap, OsmAnd is ideal for OpenStreetMap mapping community as you can see your corrections quickly and identify errors.

While in Germany, I used this application all the time to get around. It was much easier than using the paper tourist maps - I could enter the address of where I was and where I wanted to go. It also makes one look a bit less like a tourist (and hopefully less of a target for thieves then).The points of interest included most of the common tourist sites, many public transportation spots (subway, tram stops), restaurants, hotels, and more. Overall I was very happy with this application.

I had been wanting a map app for my kindle for those times I did not have access to wifi or 4g on my cellphone. This app is very good for what it is, though it is important to not overestimate it. It is not Google maps offline, nor is it a GPS device. If you need GPS, get a Garmin. This program gives you searchable, zoomable maps. It's not very robust at searching by content, but the address search is fine, and it's far better than trying to fold an old paper map. The app itself is free, and you can access all maps free so long as you have an internet connection. To get offline maps, which is the real reason anyone would use this over Google maps, is a in-app purchase, by country or state, as you need. I purchased the USA bundle and was very happy with it. To manage storage, you can choose to download all 50 states, or pick and choose, which I thought was a nice feature.

Headings: Great offline map for directions to get around, especially overseas
Base_Reviews: Traveling overseas without access to my phone's network, I needed something similar to what I normally get from the maps on my smart phone. Since my Kindle Fire only has Wifi I looked for offline maps and found this application. After briefly testing out the app itself online and confirming the directions seemed satisfactory, I paid for the global offline maps package (since I travel to different countries it seemed more cost-effective than just buying Germany where I was going). While in Germany, I used this application all the time to get around. It was much easier than using the paper tourist maps - I could enter the address of where I was and where I wanted to go. It also makes one look a bit less like a tourist (and hopefully less of a target for thieves then).The points of interest included most of the common tourist sites, many public transportation spots (subway, tram stops), restaurants, hotels, and more. The only time the application seemed a bit confused by the streets was in Munich where the streets can be navigated a bit differently on foot than by car (and the app does provide different directions by foot or by car). Overall I was very happy with this application.
